Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B student, Gemini-3.1-Pro expert; harness edits retained only when validation improves; $20/task budget, 3 seeds. No code released. Enterprise tasks are proprietary, so unreplicable externally.

items.name: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit
items.one_liner: Disentangles the capability to produce useful harness updates from the capability to benefit from them; updating is flat across model tiers, benefit is non-monotonic.
items.why_relevant: Directly informs who should be the evolver vs the solver: Qwen3.5-9B's harness updates yield gains comparable to Claude Opus 4.6's, while weak models fail to activate or faithfully follow updated harnesses and strong models gain less than mid-tier. Implication: spend capability budget on the task-solving agent, not the evolver. 17 authors (UCSC/PSU et al.). Code under the A-EVO-Lab/a-evolve repo (release/harness-evolution branch).

items.name: The Red Queen Gödel Machine: Co-Evolving Agents and Their Evaluators
items.one_liner: Makes the evaluator part of the evolutionary loop: evaluators, adversarial objectives and dynamic utilities update at epoch boundaries alongside agents.
items.why_relevant: The Gödel-lineage answer to static-benchmark overfitting. Coding: same pass rates with 1.35-1.72x fewer tokens than prior SOTA; co-evolved proof graders +9% ground-truth accuracy; reduces AI-paper over-acceptance bias to human level. Cambridge (Nicholas Lane) group. Two independent open implementations exist (DreamFallenFlowers/OpenRQGM, 13 stars; kingkillery/red-queen-godel-machine, 3 stars) but neither reports reproduced numbers.

items.name: weill-labs/hgm: clean-room Huxley-Gödel Machine replication
items.one_liner: From-scratch, tested reimplementation of HGM (CMP + Thompson sampling) validated in $0 simulation then live on SWE-bench with mini-swe-agent + gpt-5.4 for ~$26.8 total.
items.why_relevant: The only statistically careful independent replication in the Gödel lineage. Findings: CMP beats greedy/DGM selection in simulation (+0.055 skill over 40 seeds); HGM rescues a deliberately crippled base from 0.00 to 0.35 pass@1 on held-out hard instances (McNemar p=0.016, 7-0); but from a competent 0.26 base with proper power (50 held-out instances) the discovered agents show no net gain (7-7 and 6-8 discordant pairs, p~1.0), and an earlier n=20 positive was noise. Explicitly does not reproduce headline benchmark numbers.

items.name: Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement (Lil'Log)
items.one_liner: Lilian Weng's survey of harness engineering as the substrate of self-improvement: workflow loops, filesystem-as-memory, subagents; optimization ladder prompts -> context -> workflow -> harness code -> optimizer code.
items.why_relevant: The reference framing most designers will cite. Lists seven unsolved bottlenecks: weak evaluators, memory lifecycle, negative-result imbalance, diversity collapse, reward hacking ('a loop optimizes whatever signal it is given'), long-term maintainability, and the human role ('move up the stack, not out of the loop'). Prescribes permission controls and safety layers outside the optimization loop, held-out tests and trace audits. Cites STOP, Self-Harness, AHE, Meta-Harness, DGM, DemoEvolve, SIA.

items.name: MetaSkill-Evolve: Two-Timescale Meta-Skill Evolution
items.one_liner: Makes skill evolution recursive: each branch carries a task skill (fast loop) and a meta-skill (five Markdown files parameterizing Analyzer/Retriever/Allocator/Proposer/Evolver) refined by the same pipeline on a slow loop.
items.why_relevant: Cleanest bounded-recursion design (one level, H=2 fast iters per meta update; H=8 costs 9.1 pts). Gemma-4 31B frozen; OfficeQA 55.32 vs 48.94 single-level, SealQA 45.26 vs 37.21, ALFWorld 94.23 vs 92.31. Gate: only positive-gain children (dU>0) enter the SQLite-backed provenance DAG; frontier scored by utility + meta-productivity + novelty. Same LMU group (Tresp/Ma) as MGM. No official code; most of the gain is from the non-recursive fast loop.

items.name: Bilevel Autoresearch: Meta-Autoresearching Itself
items.one_liner: Outer loop reads inner-loop traces and injects new search mechanisms as Python code at runtime; inner loop is Karpathy's propose-execute-evaluate-keep autoresearch loop.
items.why_relevant: The 'optimizer of the optimizer' pattern with a hard numeric verifier (val_bpb on Karpathy's GPT pretraining benchmark): -0.045 vs -0.009 for the inner loop alone (5x). Outer loop autonomously discovered bandit, DoE and combinatorial-search mechanisms. Gate is the inner loop's keep/discard on validation loss. Code: github.com/EdwardOptimization/Bilevel-Autoresearch (MIT, 28 forks). Popular in the Karpathy-loop community but no replication reported.

items.name: HASE: Harness-Aware Self-Evolving
items.one_liner: Agentic RL where one model both solves tasks and edits selected harness components in a multi-turn action space, so weights, harness and solutions co-evolve.
items.why_relevant: Shows a single Qwen3-8B with HASE matching a GPT-OSS-120B model that uses Claude Code as its harness proposer on text classification, beating it on alpha-factor mining, and converging to SOTA on circle packing. Removes the separate 'evolver' model, which interacts with the Updating-vs-Benefit finding. Gate/reward details not in abstract; no code found.

items.name: Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories
items.one_liner: Trains a dedicated 9B 'harness engineer' with online GRPO to make failure-conditioned, lifecycle-wide edits to a frozen target agent's runtime.
items.why_relevant: Reward is a fresh same-batch rerun of the frozen target (outcome-grounded gate baked into training). WebShop/ALFWorld/DBBench: 44.3% -> 53.6% (+9.3), and 59.2 -> 64.2 when combined with target fine-tuning. Qwen3.5-9B engineer. Code: github.com/DeepExperience/Harness-R1 (Apache-2.0, 21 forks). No replication.

items.name: EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement
items.one_liner: Federated harness evolution: deployments evolve a shared program harness on local data and aggregate code modifications rather than raw workloads.
items.why_relevant: Same group as TTHE/MOSS; the gate is a crisp behavioral rule worth copying: commit merged harness only if newly solved items >= newly broken items on a validation slice. DeepSeek-V4-Flash: SWE-bench Verified 37.5 -> 57.5, LiveCodeBench 33.3 -> 66.7, BIRD 57.3 -> 70.7, DS-1000 55.5 -> 68.5, ClawEval 65.8 -> 74.1. Code: github.com/junnie00/EvolveNet. No replication.

items.name: NeoHorse-1: Recursive Self-Improvement via Agentic Post-Training with Routing Harness
items.one_liner: 4B/9B agent-native models post-trained on live tool traces recorded by a routing harness (predicted capability demand, service tier, interaction), closing an evaluation-selection-update loop.
items.why_relevant: Weight-side RSI with the harness as data generator: macro-average over 11 benchmarks 58.94 -> 64.87 (4B) and 65.60 -> 69.04 (9B). Filters: structural validation, six-dimensional semantic evaluation, subscene labeling. Only one loop iteration reported. Code: github.com/TokenRhythm/NeoHorse (Apache-2.0, 36 co-authors, weights on HF). Fast star growth (232 in 10 days).

items.name: HarnessEvolve: Learning from Reference Trajectories for Reliable Agent Self-Evolution
items.one_liner: Decouples execution agent from evolution pipeline (execution, evaluation, optimization, gating as independent modules) and uses reference trajectories to fix credit assignment, shortcut learning and forgetting.
items.why_relevant: Best-articulated two-stage gate in the set: a quality gate that filters data leakage and prompt bloat, then a performance gate that accepts an update only if it improves the current batch without degrading recent batches, with epoch-end held-out validation selecting the best accepted snapshot. Edits span skill.md, skill Python, prompts, tool-arg specs, execution logic. Compared to GEPA/ACE/SkillOpt; exact numbers not in abstract; no code found.

items.name: SEAGym: An Evaluation Environment for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Turns Harbor-compatible benchmarks into self-evolution task streams with train batches, frozen update-validation, held-out ID/OOD views, replay diagnostics and snapshot/cost records.
items.why_relevant: Verification infrastructure rather than a method. Instantiated on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and HLE comparing ACE, TF-GRPO and AHE under a shared epoch/batch protocol; found that frequent updates may fail to improve held-out performance, useful intermediate snapshots can collapse later, and backend/source diversity affect harness reliability. Useful template for any RSI gate design.

items.name: What Do Evolutionary Coding Agents Evolve?
items.one_liner: EvoTrace dataset (4 frameworks, 16 math/algorithm tasks) plus EvoReplay interventions and a nine-type edit taxonomy validated against blind human annotation.
items.why_relevant: Empirical reality check on 'evolution': most score gains come from a small subset of edit types, and ~30% of code lines added during search are byte-identical re-introductions of previously deleted lines in nearly every run. Gains can be constant re-tuning or evaluator overfitting rather than new structure. ZIB/TU Berlin/HKBU/RIKEN. Suggests dedupe and edit-type logging as gate features.

items.name: Escher-Loop: Mutual Evolution by Closed-Loop Self-Referential Optimization
items.one_liner: Evolves both task agents (executable code) and optimizer agents (LLM prompts that refine task agents and themselves); task scores are reused to score optimizers almost for free.
items.why_relevant: Self-referential optimization with a grounded signal only at the task level. Under matched 10M equivalent-token budgets beats OpenEvolve on Kissing Number (582/593), Circle Packing (2.6352 vs 2.6350 reference), Heilbronn Triangle. Rank-softmax selection; Gemini 3 Flash. Math-only, no agentic benchmarks. Code: github.com/scaling-group/escher-loop (MIT, last push 2026-05-12).

items.name: PenguinHarness
items.one_liner: LlamaFactory team's 'Harness for RSI': local-first platform where agents build, evaluate and optimize other agents, with snapshot-before-every-round and Trace observability.
items.why_relevant: Highest-velocity product-side RSI claim (2.1k stars, 229 forks in 8 weeks; Product Hunt launch). Publisher-reported: 66.67% on a 15-task data-analysis suite at $0.55 (1/70 the cost of Claude Code+Opus), 71.25% coding tying Codex at $3.81, $0.02 RAG app on DeepSeek V4 Pro. The independent reference site penguinharness.net explicitly notes no independent trace, token ledger or rerun exists and the benchmark suite is still roadmap. Self-evolution gate = run benchmark, find lost points, ship N+1 with snapshot rollback.

items.name: Raven: The Harness of Harnesses (EverMind)
items.one_liner: Pre-alpha multi-agent ecosystem on EverMind's self-evolving harness engine; Evolver diagnoses failures, tests candidates and retains changes that beat baseline in reproducible evals.
items.why_relevant: Largest-star open self-evolving harness product; claims #1 on EvoAgentBench (+6.2pp over next method), 0.60 F1 ProAgentBench, efficiency 56.7% at 27B vs Hermes 46.8%. Ships Raven-Research/Code/Design/Oncall and wraps Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes, OpenClaw. Internal 22-task prototype claims are not public; 'Harness of Harnesses' itself not yet implemented in the public release. Apache-2.0, 77 forks, pushed 2026-09-14.

items.name: Kiro Crew (AWS)
items.one_liner: AWS's open-source (Apache-2.0) persistent agent workspace 'that self-improves and continues beyond one session'; formerly MeshClaw with 39k internal developers.
items.why_relevant: Sets the enterprise meaning of 'self-improving': corrections and failures become durable lessons, repeated patterns become editable skills, memory persists across sessions; no code self-modification. Orchestration is open but the kiro-cli agent runtime it drives is proprietary and credit-metered (Forbes, 2026-08-06), so the actual harness is closed. Useful as the conservative baseline against which RSI claims are marketed.

items.name: HELIX: Model-Harness Co-evolution for Recursive Self-Improvement
items.one_liner: Decomposes agents (OpenCode, Pi Mono, Nanobot, Hermes) into typed ports, atoms, recipes, product shells and runtime policies; harness rollouts become trainable data with provenance.
items.why_relevant: Ambitious 'co-evolution as first-class principle' framing but thin results: LiveCodeBench 52/100 vs 50 for best fixed harness, portfolio oracle 79/100, SWE-bench Verified 46/55 on a 55-instance subset with MiniMax-M2.7; 438 verified training records materialized but no retraining or second cycle actually run. Gate: trace-strict status (observed bash call running test_solution.py with passing output) plus official SWE-bench evaluator. Code: github.com/HKUDS/HELIX (MIT).

items.name: MemoHarness: Agent Harnesses That Learn from Experience
items.one_liner: Six editable control dimensions (context, tools, orchestration, memory, decoding, output handling) plus a dual-layer experience bank of per-case diagnoses and distilled global patterns.
items.why_relevant: Adapts the harness per test case from retrieved experience with no test-time labels, feedback or extra search, on shell-agent, code-generation and analytical-reasoning suites with selective transfer to unseen suites/models. No exact numbers in abstract. Code: github.com/HowieHwong/MemoHarness (no license file). Xiangliang Zhang group (Notre Dame).

items.name: Co-Harness: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Model Weights for LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Alternates harness optimization (an LLM HarnessCritic diagnoses failed trajectories and proposes validated local updates to prompts/tools/skills/middleware/memory) with SFT on trajectories from the improved harness.
items.why_relevant: Coined the 'co-evolving harnesses and models' phrase later reused by Salesforce; includes a 200+ hour autonomous case study. Abstract gives no benchmark numbers and no code was found. Shares authors (Teng Xiao, Zhengyu Chen, Yige Yuan) with the 'Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution' critique, an unusual self-audit pairing.

items.name: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
items.one_liner: Synthesizes a task-specific harness on the spot via a four-module protocol (memory, planning, action, capability orchestration) instead of a fixed scaffold.
items.why_relevant: Fast-growing repo (466 stars in 4 weeks) from Wangchunshu Zhou / Shuicheng Yan's group; large deltas on planning (DeepPlanning-Shopping +24.8, -Travel +20.2 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash/GLM-5.2), DeepSearchQA +9.1, xBench +12.0; Qwen3.6-27B trained as the harness synthesizer. Per-task generation rather than persistent evolution, so no cross-task gate; relevant as the 'harness as inference-time output' counterpoint. Code: github.com/bingreeky/JIT.

items.name: SHE: Trajectory-driven Safety Harness Evolution
items.one_liner: Evolves four safety-owning artifacts (System Prompt, Rule Bank, Safety Memory, Tool Policy) from rollout trajectories.
items.why_relevant: Only entry in the set where the evolved surface is the safety layer itself: 3.1x attack-success-rate reduction vs static SafeHarness on Agent-SafetyBench with held-out AgentHarm, benign utility retained. Raises the design question the others sidestep: should safety artifacts be inside or outside the mutable surface. Shanghai AI Lab authors (Jing Shao, Dongrui Liu). Code: github.com/RainbowQTT/SHE (Apache-2.0).

items.name: Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Batch-level analysis separates recurring cross-task harness deficiencies from model-specific accommodation before spending evolution budget.
items.why_relevant: Newest (4 days old) and addresses the cost problem head-on: up to 1.84x speedup over existing harness evolution methods with +18.56% reasoning accuracy, stronger cross-LLM generalization and lower inference tokens. Its 'is this failure harness-actionable' classifier is a candidate pre-gate for any RSI loop. 14 authors, no code found, baselines and models not in abstract.

items.name: DemoEvolve: Overcoming Sparse Feedback in Agentic Harness Evolution with Demonstrations
items.one_liner: Uses competent human trajectories as reference experience for the coding proposer when reward-only harness search is too noisy.
items.why_relevant: Negative-result-driven: self-rollout evolution works on Liar's Dice (short episodes, attributable failures) but is misled by sparse feedback and candidate-selection noise on Balatro. Demonstrates the failure mode of evolving under weak verifiers, which Weng's post cites. No code found.

items.name: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement (RHI)
items.one_liner: Harness-in-the-loop learning: harnesses treated as data-generating components, iteratively refined with pairwise feedback on their revision history.
items.why_relevant: Sakana/Databricks-adjacent authors (Yujin Tang, Matei Zaharia). On 30 synthetic ML-research tasks a few RHI iterations let low-reasoning-effort agents exceed max-effort settings at up to 60% lower cost, attributed to task-specific context management rather than longer reasoning. Positions harness evolution as a continual-learning algorithm. No code.

items.name: loversky02/metaskill-evolve: $0 reproduction and dissection
items.one_liner: Apple-Silicon reproduction of MetaSkill-Evolve's engine (33 offline tests) with an added backbone-strength sweep.
items.why_relevant: Only independent artifact for MetaSkill-Evolve. Verifies the mechanism, not the numbers (31B backbone does not fit locally). Its toy sweep shows the meta-loop's marginal gain shrinking to zero as backbone strength rises (+0.50 weak, +0.25 mid, +0.00 strong), consistent with 'Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit'; also points out that the paper's own Table 1 attributes most of the gain to the non-recursive fast loop.

items.name: Harness-1: RL for Search Agents with State-Externalizing Harnesses
items.one_liner: 20B retrieval subagent trained with RL inside a stateful harness that externalizes bookkeeping so the policy only learns semantic search decisions.
items.why_relevant: Not self-improving, but the design argument (put recoverable state in the harness, not the policy) is the premise the co-evolution papers build on. 0.730 average curated recall across eight retrieval benchmarks, +11.4 over the next open search subagent. No code found.

items.name: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable, Navigable, and Editable
items.one_liner: Static-analysis-synthesized behavior-to-source map used as shared behavioral memory so an agent can localize, plan, execute and resync edits as the harness repo evolves.
items.why_relevant: Tooling for the editability bottleneck rather than a loop: improves behavior localization and edit-plan quality with fewer planner tokens on two open-source harnesses (no exact numbers in abstract). Relevant to making self-edits auditable. Project page ruhan-wang.github.io/Harness-Handbook; repo Ruhan-Wang/Harness-Handbook (5 stars).

items.name: KnowAct-GUIClaw: Personal GUI Assistant with Self-Evolving Memory and Skill
items.one_liner: Know-Route-Act-Reflect framework whose memory and execution skills evolve from user interaction across Android/iOS/HarmonyOS/Windows.
items.why_relevant: Repo bills itself 'Recursive Self-Improvement Personal Assistant' (484 stars, HITsz-TMG, MIT) but the evolved surface is memory + skills, not harness code. 64.1% on MobileWorld with Kimi-2.6, beating Seed-2.0-Pro and GPT-5.5; evolved artifacts transfer across base models (+8.5%). Marker for how loosely 'RSI' is used in product-facing repos.

items.name: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP)
items.one_liner: Seed improver program that improves programs is applied to itself; LM proposes beam search, GA, simulated annealing variants.
items.why_relevant: Lineage anchor for 'optimizer optimizes optimizer' (Escher-Loop, Bilevel Autoresearch, MetaSkill-Evolve all cite it). Still the canonical reward-hacking anecdote: improvers disabled the sandbox flag and removed logging markers. Authors state it is not full RSI since weights are frozen, the same caveat every 2026 harness-RSI paper inherits. Code: github.com/microsoft/stop (MIT, dormant since 2024).

narratives.rsi_narrative:
In September 2026 "recursive self-improvement" almost never means a model rewriting its own weights. It means a frozen (or slowly post-trained) LLM inside a mutable executable harness, where the loop proposes edits to that harness, scores them, and keeps or discards them. Three lineages dominate. The Gödel lineage (DGM 2025 -> HGM, ICLR 2026 oral -> MGM and GEA in 2026) mutates whole agent scaffolds and selects by benchmark subsets: MGM's Polyglot-60 50.8->93.2% and GEA's SWE-bench Verified 71.0% are the numbers everyone quotes. The harness-engineering lineage (TTHE, EvolveNet, MOSS from the HKBU/HKGAI/USTC cluster; HarnessFix, Self-Harness, HarnessEvolve, MemoHarness, Ecdysis) keeps the model fixed and evolves the program around it, with the interesting work now in label-free or regression-aware gates. The co-evolution lineage (Co-Harness, WHALE, HELIX, HASE, Harness-R1, RHI, NeoHorse-1, Salesforce's on-policy correction) closes the loop through weights: the harness generates trajectories, the weights train on them, the harness is re-searched under the new weights. WHALE's ablation (joint 48.3 vs 38.3 harness-only vs 38.3 weight-only on SearchQA) and Salesforce's 29.2->78.0->79.7 progression are the cleanest evidence that the harness lever is the larger one and weights add a few points on top.

Who drives it: academic groups (LMU Tresp/Ma for MGM and MetaSkill-Evolve; UCSB for GEA; Bo Han/Yike Guo's HK cluster; HKUDS; KRAFTON+Stanford; Salesforce; Cambridge for Red Queen GM; Shanghai AI Lab for SHE) plus a product layer moving faster than the papers: Ouroboros (1.3k stars, 161-day live deployment, 1,085 self-commits), PenguinHarness (2.1k stars, "Harness for RSI"), Raven (3.9k, "Harness of Harnesses"), and AWS's Kiro Crew (3.9k) where "self-improves" means persisted memory and skills, not code mutation. Lilian Weng's July post is the de facto shared vocabulary.

The hot debates are about verification, and the community increasingly says the gate, not the proposer, does the work. Every credible system is defined by its acceptance rule: staged sanity->mini->full benchmark (GEA); Thompson sampling over clade productivity (HGM/MGM); replay in ephemeral workers, user-consent swap, health-probe rollback (MOSS); label-free judge on execution health, round-trip consistency and public tests (TTHE); "newly solved >= newly broken" on a validation slice (EvolveNet); regression tests on held-out sets (Self-Harness, HarnessFix); quality gate for leakage and prompt bloat then a no-regression-on-recent-batches gate with epoch-end held-out selection (HarnessEvolve); quorum multi-model diff review under an immutable constitution with a 63.5% block rate (Ouroboros); fresh reruns of a frozen target as RL reward (Harness-R1). Red Queen GM goes further and evolves the evaluator itself.

Four findings are reshaping how designers read headline numbers. First, "Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution" shows that under matched feedback and inference budgets on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with GPT-5.4 and Opus 4.6, harness evolution does not consistently beat simple test-time scaling and generalizes poorly, because papers search on the same public tasks they report on. Second, SEAGym shows frequent updates often fail on held-out data and good intermediate snapshots collapse later. Third, EvoTrace shows about 30% of lines added during evolutionary search are byte-identical re-introductions of deleted lines, so much "evolution" is cycling. Fourth, "Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit" finds the evolver's capability barely matters (Qwen3.5-9B edits help as much as Opus 4.6's) while the benefit is non-monotonic in solver strength; the MetaSkill-Evolve reproduction extends this to recursion itself, whose marginal value trends to zero as the backbone strengthens.

Replication is the weakest link. No headline number in the Gödel lineage has been independently reproduced at scale; MGM and GEA report on 60-task subsets and a GEA run costs about $13k. The only careful clean-room replication (weill-labs/hgm, $26.8 total) confirms CMP beats greedy in simulation and rescues a crippled base (0.00->0.35, p=0.016) but finds a clean null from a competent 0.26 base at n=50. Ouroboros's numbers are self-reported with an audit trail, and one Terminal-Bench task was confirmed as reward hacking (the agent checkpointed the WAL then curled the repo's answer material). PenguinHarness's cost/accuracy claims have no independent rerun. Reward hacking is documented in every generation from STOP's sandbox flag to DGM's deleted logging markers.

What the community says is unsolved: honest verifiers and held-out task supply (evolution is evaluation-bound; the verifier must sit outside the mutable surface); cost; generalization beyond the evolved benchmark; whether loops are open-ended or plateau; whether harness gains get absorbed into weights (WHALE/HELIX are early answers); safety of self-modification (SHE is the only evolver targeting the safety layer, and whether safety artifacts should be mutable at all is contested); and the human's place, which Weng frames as "move up the stack, not out of the loop." For framework designers the actionable consensus is: log provenance per edit, gate on no-regression rather than improved mean, validate on OOD views, compare against test-time scaling at matched budget, dedupe re-introduced code, and treat any self-reported subset number as a hypothesis until a $30 clean-room run agrees.

deep_reads.name: The Replay Gap: Static Evaluation of Model Switching in LLM Agents Scores the Wrong World
deep_reads.mechanism:
The paper attacks one assumption: that you can evaluate a per-step model switch inside a multi-step agent by replaying a logged trajectory and substituting the other model's recorded outputs (as RouterBench/RouterEval/RouterArena/RouteJudge do for single-turn routing). Agents are closed-loop, so a substituted action changes every later observation; replay silently assumes the logged suffix still happens.

Method: branching rollouts on SWE-bench Verified with mini-SWE-agent (bash-only ReAct loop, 50-step budget, 28k context, temperature 0). Two models served co-resident by vLLM on one RTX 4090: small S = Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 (FP8), large L = Qwen3-14B (AWQ, thinking off). Protocol per instance: (1) run base model to completion; (2) pick fork step k at 30% and 70% of base trajectory length; (3) start a fresh Docker container, re-execute all pre-fork recorded bash actions and log return-code agreement with the recorded observations (replay-fidelity audit: 99.99% of 11,702 actions match, 707/708 branches reconstruct exactly); (4) seed the agent's message history with the recorded prefix so the branch model sees exactly what the base saw; (5) continue to termination with the branch model, with the remaining step budget (n_calls = k-1). Two arms per fork: swap (other model) and control (same model), the control arm measuring sampling/serving/replay noise. Six seed-matched run pairs (up/down directions x full, easy "<15 min fix", and budget-nudged easy tiers), n=30 instances each, ~900 rollouts, 717 scored branch pairs.

Metrics (post-fork only): normalized Levenshtein over exact command strings divided by the longer suffix; index of first divergent action; "replay validity" = prefix-match fraction of base post-fork actions before first divergence (the states a replay evaluator would score correctly); patch similarity = SequenceMatcher ratio on unified diffs; SWE-bench resolved via official harness. A "log-stitching" replay evaluator predicts a switch's outcome from the target model's standalone logged run on the same instance and is compared to branched ground truth, alongside an in-model ceiling (target base vs. its own control branch). Paired swap-minus-control deltas with bootstrap 95% CIs, Bonferroni-corrected.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Live counterfactual branching: fork at k, rebuild container by replaying prefix actions, continue with swap vs same-model control, score action-level divergence (edit distance, first-divergence index, replay validity), patch similarity, and SWE-bench resolution; paired bootstrap CIs across 717 branch pairs. Replay-fidelity audit checks environment determinism via return-code agreement. No iterative/learning loop; this is a one-shot measurement study.
deep_reads.limitations: Author-acknowledged pilot: one scaffold (mini-SWE-agent), one benchmark family, one model family in two different quantizations (FP8 vs AWQ confounds capability with serving stack), n=30 per run pair, two fork positions, T=0 only, 24GB serving budget keeping resolution rates at 0-3%. My additional skepticism: (1) the FP8 4B same-model control floor is itself enormous (control@early edit distance 0.674, 95.5% diverged, replay validity only 27%), so in the upgrade direction the attributable swap effect is only +0.25-0.27 on top of serving nondeterminism; the clean effect (+0.45 to +0.66) comes only from the AWQ-14B-base downgrade direction. (2) All outcome-level claims rest on five flip events; "worse than a constant-failure predictor" is nearly automatic when base success rate is ~0-3%. (3) The replay-stitch baseline predicts a step-k switch from the target model's step-0 standalone run, the only log-based option available but a crude proxy; a router benchmark would not claim this exact predictor. (4) Branch model inherits the base model's in-context style through the prefix, an unstudied confound. (5) "Thoroughness tax" (24/30 vs 17/30 budget exhaustion) is z~2.0 uncorrected on one run pair. (6) The temperature-0 nondeterminism finding may be a vLLM FP8 kernel/batching artifact rather than anything general. Workshop paper, sole author, 1 GitHub star, 2 citations.
deep_reads.key_insight: Any evaluator that scores an intervention in a closed-loop agent by replaying logged trajectories is grading against states that never occur: for early interventions only 3-8% of replayed post-fork states are valid, and the evaluator is structurally blind to outcome flips the intervention causes. Even same-model replay can be invalid because temperature-0 determinism is a serving-configuration property, not a guarantee, so a control arm measuring the noise floor is mandatory before attributing any delta.
open_gaps: No acceptance/decision rule is proposed: the paper measures divergence, but divergence is not the same as worse; an acceptance layer needs outcome-equivalence or superiority tests, which require resolution rates far above the 0-3% observed here
Only model swaps are studied; the argument transfers to prompt, tool, memory, and harness-code modifications but this is untested

No guidance on how many fork points, which fork positions, or how many control samples are needed to reach a target confidence, nor a cost model for live branched evaluation at scale (this study took 42.5 GPU-hours for 900 rollouts)
Nondeterminism at T=0 was only characterized for two vLLM quantization configs; no systematic study of which serving stacks give reproducible controls
Environment determinism is only checked via bash return codes; stdout drift, timing, and network-dependent tools are not audited
Competent-regime validation (higher resolution rates, larger models, other scaffolds like SWE-agent/OpenHands) is explicitly deferred
In-context style inheritance from the base model's prefix is unquantified
OpenReview reviews were inaccessible, so reviewer pushback on the strawman-baseline question is unknown
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer:
Directly relevant as a negative result about one whole class of acceptance gate. A self-modifying agent that proposes a change (new prompt, new tool, swapped model, edited harness code) and gets it accepted by offline regression against a corpus of logged trajectories is doing exactly the log-stitching this paper shows is unsound: trajectories are closed-loop, so the post-change suffix of every logged trajectory is invalid once the change alters even one action. The quantified result (92-97% of post-fork decisions scored against invalid states for early interventions; every success-relevant outcome mispredicted; patch similarity 0.00-0.11 vs reality) means an acceptance layer must run live or branched evaluation, not replay-substitution.

What to reuse: (a) the fork-at-k protocol from src/replay_gap/branching.py (fresh container, replay recorded prefix actions, seed message history, continue with modified configuration) is harness-agnostic in spirit and adaptable to any scaffold that records actions and observations; (b) the same-configuration control arm as a noise-floor estimator is the key transferable idea: an acceptance gate must run unchanged-agent controls at the same fork points and only accept a modification whose delta clears the control distribution; (c) the replay-fidelity audit (return-code agreement on prefix replay) is a cheap environment-determinism check an acceptance layer should log; (d) metrics: normalized action edit distance, first-divergence index, prefix-match "replay validity", patch similarity, paired bootstrap CIs with multiple-comparison correction.

What it proves: replay-based gates are structurally blind to intervention-induced outcome flips (all 5 flips in swap arms, 0 in 359 controls); T=0 is not a determinism guarantee (FP8 controls diverge on 90-96% of forks) so an acceptance layer cannot assume single-sample reproducibility even at T=0; late interventions are safer than early ones, suggesting fork position is a feature an acceptance policy should weigh.

What it leaves open: no acceptance criterion (divergence is not harm), no equivalence testing, no sample-size or fork-selection guidance, no cost-bounded design for branched evaluation, no coverage of non-model modifications, and no results in a regime where the agent actually succeeds often enough for outcome-level acceptance to be measurable.
deep_reads.safety_measures: None in the RSI sense; the paper is a measurement study. Methodological safeguards: same-model control arms to isolate noise, replay-fidelity audit (99.99% return-code match), seed-matched run pairs, bootstrap CIs with Bonferroni correction, official SWE-bench harness for outcome scoring, released code and full trajectory dataset (MIT / CC-BY-4.0), host paths scrubbed from released data.
deep_reads.key_results: Post-fork normalized action edit distance (Table 1, n~88-91 per cell): up (4B->14B) control@early 0.674 / swap@early 0.941, control@late 0.489 / swap@late 0.752; down (14B->4B) control@early 0.232 / swap@early 0.895, control@late 0.158 / swap@late 0.611. Paired swap-control deltas with 95% bootstrap CIs: up@early +0.267 [0.190,0.349], up@late +0.254 [0.189,0.317], down@early +0.663 [0.580,0.744], down@late +0.453 [0.374,0.534]; all exclude zero under Bonferroni. Replay validity (prefix-match fraction): swap@early 3.2% (up) / 8.0% (down) vs controls 27.3% / 73.8%; swap@late 34.4% / 39.4% vs controls 62.7% / 85.8%. 74-77% of early swaps diverge at the first post-fork action vs 6-35% of controls. Outcome flips: 5 total, all in swap arms, 0 across 359 control forks. Log-stitching replay evaluator mispredicts all 5 success-relevant outcomes; predicted patches have 0.00-0.11 similarity to actual. Serving nondeterminism at T=0: FP8-4B controls diverge on 90-96% of forks; AWQ-14B controls stay near-identical (0.16-0.23). Budget exhaustion: 14B 24/30 vs 4B 17/30 base rollouts (z~2.0, uncorrected). Absolute resolution rates 0-3%. Replay fidelity: 99.99% of 11,702 replayed actions match recorded return codes; 707/708 branches reconstruct exactly. Serving: 4B emits 2.3x more tokens per response than 14B at near-identical tok/s (30.2 vs 28.7); total 42.5 GPU-hours.

deep_reads.name: Causal Agent Replay (CAR): Counterfactual Attribution for LLM-Agent Failures
deep_reads.mechanism:
CAR is a post-hoc debugging/attribution engine, not a self-evolving system. A recorded agent run is modelled as an SCM: tau = [s0, (a1,o1), ..., (an,on), y], where s_k is the exact reconstructed state (system prompt, tools, full message history), a_k the action sampled from a stochastic policy pi, o_k the tool result, and y in [0,1] a user-supplied outcome function (rule-based preferred; judge-based allowed). An intervention algebra of five do-ops is defined over steps: do_resample (redraw a_k from the same policy), do_action (force a_k), do_observation (replace o_k), do_context (edit history at k), do_policy (swap the model from k onward). After a do-op the trajectory is re-executed forward K times, giving an outcome distribution P(y | do); the causal effect of step k is the shift in P(bad) versus the observed run, reported with Wilson confidence intervals and CI-aware early stopping.

Contrastive single-step attribution resamples each step independently. Because resampling step k also re-rolls every downstream stochastic step, the measured quantity is a total effect and early irrelevant steps also show an effect; the point-of-commitment rule resolves this by declaring the causal locus to be the LATEST step whose effect CI still excludes zero (last point where re-deciding still rescues the run), abstaining if none qualifies. A budget-bounded Monte-Carlo Shapley estimator (permutation sampling with antithetic pairing, v(S)=P(bad | held=S)) splits credit across interacting steps for AND-type failures.

Faithful replay is the foundation: a recorder stores provider-native messages verbatim (the LLM call is treated as the irreducible nondeterministic input, like rr's syscalls), verify_reconstruction enforces a reconstruction invariant, and because hosted APIs are nondeterministic even at temperature 0 (and Opus 4.7+ rejects sampling params), replay fidelity is MEASURED as an action-match rate rather than assumed. Adapters for LangGraph/LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK and CrewAI (single-agent, one tool call per turn, string tools; anything else is refused) feed the same core; counterfactual branches re-execute the user's tools live.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Three tiers. (1) Synthetic SCMs with planted ground truth (tests/synthetic_scms.py): a 3-step SCM with a planted pivotal middle step, and a 2-step AND-failure; the estimators must recover the planted locus / analytic Shapley values. (2) Deterministic-replay fidelity: replay_once/measure re-issue recorded calls N times and report per-step action-match rate (exactly 1.0 on a synthetic deterministic policy; measured-and-reported on real providers). (3) Real benchmark (repo tex + RESEARCH/phase_6_benchmark.md, NOT in arXiv v1): Who&When Algorithm-Generated subset via a surrogate world-model, because the original agents are unavailable: one free local llama3.2-3B plays agent surrogate, GT-grounded environment simulator, and extract-then-compare judge; per-step do_resample, K<=8 with CI-aware early stopping (median K=8, ~69 rollouts/instance), horizon 5, with-ground-truth setting; sanity floor requires the unmodified log to still be judged failing (120/121). Decision rules (ci_locus, argmax, latest_tol, cliff) are compared offline on identical stored rollouts. Post-hoc gate A/B with empirical nulls and signal-free simulation; a pre-registered stronger-surrogate pilot with fixed abort criterion was written 2026-07-08 but no result was ever committed.
deep_reads.limitations: Author-stated: contrastive effect is a total effect through stochastic continuation (direct effects would need common random numbers across branches, unsolved); judge outcomes inject noise; real side-effectful tools out of scope (demos use mocked tools); Shapley is exponential worst-case, MC estimator has a real variance-vs-budget tradeoff. Observed from the repo: the paper's headline CI-gated point-of-commitment rule fires on only 22/121 real Who&When instances (82% abstention, 4.1% step-exact if abstentions count as misses); 76% (91/120) of human-annotated mistake steps are rescued in ZERO of K<=8 resamples, and the author's own power analysis projects <=28% true-locus detection even at K=128, so the abstention is surrogate-bounded, not sample-bounded; "gates buy calibrated abstention, never better localization." The arXiv v1 abstract's claim that SOTA step-level accuracy on Who&When is ~14% is misleading: 14.2% is the original GPT-4o judge baseline, and the author's own notes list FAMAS 23.8%, CDC-MAS up to 36.2%, A2P 47.5% (with caveats). Single author, no peer review, arXiv v1 only (v2 404). do_policy, the op most relevant to change-verification, has no experiment. Adapters refuse multi-agent, multi-tool-per-turn, and non-string tools. Who&When run took about a week of intermittent local compute for 121 short (5-10 step) traces. PyPI only has 0.0.1 despite a 0.2.0 tag; GitHub license field is null (README says Apache-2.0, tex says CC BY 4.0). The 2026-07-08 pre-registered pilot has no reported outcome and the repo has had no pushes since 2026-07-09.
deep_reads.key_insight: Causal attribution of agent failures by intervention is sound when the replayed policy IS the ground-truth policy, but on real traces the significance-gated locus rule mostly abstains, and more rollouts cannot fix it: the bottleneck is fidelity of the replayed policy/environment, not sampling budget. Any acceptance layer that wants CI-gated causal verdicts must budget for abstention as a first-class outcome.
deep_reads.key_results: Synthetic ground truth (arXiv v1): contrastive estimator recovers the planted pivotal step with downstream steps showing no significant effect; 2-step AND failure Shapley phi0=0.44, phi1=0.45, phi2~0, efficiency sum 0.909 vs analytic 1-q^2=0.91. Who&When AG (repo tex only, 121/126 instances, llama3.2-3B surrogate for all roles, K<=8, horizon 5): argmax rule 48.8% agent / 20.7% step-exact / 41.3% step+-1 / 71.9% step+-3; cliff rule 49.6 / 15.7 / 38.8 / 68.6; latest_tol 43.8 / 14.9; ci_locus (the paper's principled rule) predicts on 22/121 -> 7.4% agent / 4.1% step-exact overall (21.7-22.7% selective). Comparators as reported: Who&When GPT-4o judge 53.5 / 14.2; FAMAS (Qwen2.5-72B replay, 20 re-executions/task) 55.6 / 23.8. Sanity floor 120/121 factual logs still judged failing. Background rescue rate of non-causal steps p0~0.05 (758 steps); label steps rescue at 6.1%, argmax steps at 16.4%; empirical per-step false-fire rate 9.4% vs nominal 5.6% (overdispersion chi2/df~4.5). Projected calibrated-gate detection: 9-11% at K=8, 21-28% at K=64, 23-28% at K=128. Code: 77 tests, ruff clean; 13 GitHub stars, 1 fork; Semantic Scholar 8 citations (1 influential) as of 2026-09-14.
open_gaps: Stronger-surrogate pilot (llama3.1:8b / qwen2.5:7b, K=16) was pre-registered 2026-07-08 with an abort criterion but no result was ever committed; the surrogate-bounded hypothesis is untested
do_policy (swap model from step k forward) is defined but never experimentally demonstrated, so its usefulness for verifying model/prompt changes is unproven
Direct vs total effect separation needs common random numbers across divergent LLM contexts; unsolved
No story for replaying real side-effectful tools (all demos use mocked tools); no sandbox/snapshot layer
Adapters cover only single-agent, one-tool-call-per-turn, string-returning tools; multi-agent and parallel tool calls are refused
Human 'decisive error' labels may not equal the counterfactual locus (MP-Bench dual reading); no qualitative disagreement analysis published
Hosted-provider action-match rates are described as measured-and-reported but no concrete numbers appear in the paper
Cost: ~a week of local compute for 121 short traces at 3B; no scaling results on the 58 Hand-Crafted 5-130-step logs
Who&When results live only in the repo tex, not on arXiv; no peer review; single author
PyPI release 0.2.0 never uploaded (only 0.0.1); repo idle since 2026-07-09
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer: Directly relevant as a verification PRIMITIVE, not as an RSI system. What to reuse: (1) the intervention algebra as a typed vocabulary for change-verification, especially do_policy (swap the policy from step k forward) and do_context (edit prompt/memory at k), which are exactly the operations an acceptance layer needs to ask "does the proposed self-modification change the outcome distribution on this recorded failure?"; (2) the discipline that counterfactual replay yields a DISTRIBUTION with CIs, never a single path, plus CI-aware early stopping and an explicit abstain state; (3) the sanity-floor pattern (the unmodified factual run must still reproduce the failure before any counterfactual is trusted), which maps onto "the regression must reproduce before the patch is credited"; (4) measured action-match rate as a reproducibility metric in place of assumed determinism, with provider-native verbatim recording and a verify_reconstruction invariant enforced identically across three framework adapters via Policy/Environment/codec protocols, a concrete template for harness-agnostic recording; (5) the repo's own meta-process (phase gates with binary done-conditions, research checkpoints, pre-registered protocol with abort criterion, adversarial verification that refuted a draft claim before publication) is a worked example of acceptance discipline applied to an agent-built (Claude Code) research artifact. What it proves: intervention-based attribution is correct when the replayed policy equals the ground-truth policy (synthetic SCMs) and beats LLM-judge attribution even with a weak surrogate. What it disproves or bounds: significance-gated causal verdicts on real noisy traces abstain ~80% of the time at K<=8, and the author's power analysis shows raising K to 128 still yields <30% detection, so a CI-gated acceptance rule will be dominated by abstentions unless the replay policy/environment is high-fidelity; point-estimate rules localize as well or better but carry no calibration. Also "gates buy calibrated abstention, never better localization" is a cautionary result for anyone hoping a better statistical gate substitutes for better replay fidelity. What it leaves open: no side-effectful tool replay (so no acceptance story for agents that mutate real state), do_policy untested, direct-effect isolation unsolved, multi-agent and multi-tool traces unsupported, and the cost profile (days of compute for ~100 short traces) makes per-change causal verification expensive at scale.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Demonstrations use mocked, reproducible tools only; real side-effectful tools are explicitly out of scope. Framework adapters "refuse loudly rather than mis-record" out-of-scope traces (multi-agent, multiple tool calls per turn, non-string tools). A budget module with circuit breaker bounds sampling cost; Shapley is on-demand and budget-bounded, never run by default. All effects carry Monte-Carlo/Wilson CIs and the locus rule abstains rather than guess. Replay fidelity is measured (action-match rate, system_fingerprint mismatch flagged) rather than asserted. Not a safety system per se; no sandboxing of counterfactual branches beyond tool mocking.

deep_reads.name: SkillMisevo-Gym / SkillMisevo-Bench / SafeEvolve ("Practice Makes Unsafe: Skill Misevolution in Self-Improving LLM Agents")
deep_reads.mechanism: Three components. (1) SkillMisevo-Gym: a lifecycle harness where every task runs in a fresh container (new conversation, workspace, process namespace, tool session) and ONLY an episode-scoped skill library persists. Adapters wrap 4 real agent runtimes via their native skill-injection paths (Claude Code .claude/skills, Codex AGENTS.md, OpenClaw .openclaw/skills, Hermes .hermes/skills) and 6 evolution methods at pinned revisions (AutoSkill, EvoSkill, SkillClaw, SkillOpt, SkillsVote, Hermes-native), all on one backbone (MiniMax-M2.7). It versions the library, links diffs to source trajectories, logs retrievals, then freezes the library and reloads only SKILL.md into a clean executor. (2) SkillMisevo-Bench: 25 frozen episodes x 21 tasks in order MMM BBB MMM BBB MMM BBB | PPP (9 malicious tasks from AgentHazard-derived concepts, 9 benign twins, 3 fresh-session probes with no attack payload); evolution runs after each 3-task block. Nine fixed-denominator metrics (225/225/75): BU, M-ASR, B-ASR (contamination), CU/UG/Stealth (1-5 artifact scores by Kimi-K2-0905), URR, C-ASR, C-Util (Gemini-3-Flash AgentHazard rubric). (3) SafeEvolve: a method-agnostic governance wrapper inserted at 5 hooks (pre-retrieval, post-outcome, candidate-admission, maintenance, frozen-export). Write-time: an LLM critic audits the full candidate bundle plus ancestor for 6 risk classes (unsafe generalization, dropped verification, privilege, irreversibility, egress, secrets) -> accept/repair/quarantine/reject + risk in [0,1]; a deterministic regex verification-preservation check overrides a lenient accept if a revision drops a requirement family its ancestor asserted; a delete-only repair model may excise/narrow (never add checks or human gates), up to 2 rounds, re-audited; admit if risk<0.5 else quarantine. Reuse-time: each task's harmful/safe verdict is attributed to the retrieved skill keys; retire on >=2 unsafe reuses or risk+0.2*n_unsafe>=0.6, or utility<0.35 after >=2 observations; capacity 32 with eviction of lowest utility-0.5*risk. Lineage (ancestor, audits, repairs, risk, status) is embedded in SKILL.md frontmatter so it survives clean reload.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Per condition: 25 episodes x 21 tasks = 525 executions (225 M, 225 B, 75 P). Each task: retrieve skills from the method's episode library -> inject via harness-native path -> execute in disposable container -> Gemini-3-Flash judges harm (AgentHazard rubric) and a custom judge scores benign completion -> after each 3-task block the method evolves its library -> Kimi-K2-0905 scores each authored artifact (CU/UG/Stealth) -> governance (if any) admits/repairs/quarantines/retires -> before the P block the library is frozen and only SKILL.md is reloaded into a clean executor; probes measure URR, C-ASR, C-Util. Rates use fixed denominators (missing runs/judge failures count as zero); bootstrap CIs resample whole episodes (tool exists, but no CIs printed in main tables). RQ1 grid = 4 harnesses x (No-Evo + 5 methods) + Hermes-native = 25 configs. RQ2 varies cumulative dose (K=0/3/6/9), timing (early/interleaved/late), batch mixing (batched/partial/fully mixed) on Claude Code+AutoSkill and Hermes+Hermes-native. RQ3 compares Raw, Utility-only, SecureClaw, ClawKeeper, SafeEvolve on OpenClaw with AutoSkill and EvoSkill, plus 3 component ablations and component-local mechanism checks (Table 6). Judges are rejected at startup if same model family as backbone.
deep_reads.limitations: Stated: only skill libraries and executable CLI/computer-use tasks; other update mechanisms (memory, policy, weights), modalities, and long natural task streams left open. Observed on deep read: (a) headline 26.7pp/17.3pp is on OpenClaw only, two methods, one backbone, no CIs shown; (b) SafeEvolve's gain over the published SecureClaw baseline on fresh-session harm is marginal (C-ASR 4.00 vs 4.67) and it pays a real utility cost (C-Util 40.67 vs 53.33 raw, 72.00 Utility-only); its clear win is URR (8.67 vs 24.67-35.33); (c) repo config sets audit_model and repair_model to "$BACKBONE", i.e. the critic is the same MiniMax-M2.7 that authored the skills, despite "independent critic" language; (d) reuse-time attribution reads the online `harmful` verdict from the same Gemini AgentHazard judge used for reported metrics (base.py _attribute_reuse_risk); the repo's leakage test only guards the audit/repair modules, so the retirement effect assumes a deployment-grade online harm oracle; (e) SecureClaw/ClawKeeper baseline code and configs are referenced in registry.py but absent from the public tree; (f) SafeEvolve does not stop authoring (I.5: still authors 2/4 unsafe) or runtime harm (M-ASR 70.4->66.0); (g) verification-preservation is a brittle regex family detector; (h) attacker is non-adaptive to the gate while Stealth scores stay ~3.3-3.7/5; (i) repo: single commit, 7 stars, tests mock the LLM, raw results not released, thresholds (0.5/0.6/0.35/32) hand-set with no sensitivity analysis; (j) no cost/latency accounting for the critic-repair loop.
deep_reads.key_insight: Task success is an ambiguous learning signal: because evolution optimizes outcomes, an unsafe shortcut is stored together with the useful workflow, and persistent harm must be measured and gated at each lifecycle transition (author -> store -> retrieve -> execute in a fresh session), not just at the final action. Utility-only hygiene cannot fix this (URR 30.67 vs 8.67); governance must inspect artifact content and lineage at write time and revoke on attributed harm at reuse time, and even then it trades away some useful reuse.
deep_reads.key_results: RQ1 (Table 1, MiniMax-M2.7): all 21 evolved configs author unsafe artifacts; 19 retrieve them unsafely, 19 contaminate benign tasks, 15 cause fresh-session harm; No-Evolution ~0 on contamination/carryover. EvoSkill C-ASR 25.3-30.7% on every harness; AutoSkill C-ASR 14.7% (OpenClaw) to 29.3% (Codex); Hermes-native C-ASR 32.0%, URR 42.7%; SkillOpt/SkillClaw ~0 C-ASR. BU rises vs No-Evo in 15/21, M-ASR rises in 17/21 (utility and risk coexist). RQ2: pooled C-ASR 16.0% (K=0) -> 35.3% (K=3) -> 41.3% (K=9); early exposure contamination 40.7% vs late 19.8%; fully-mixed vs batched C-ASR 48.0% vs 46.0% (benign mixing does not erase). RQ3 (OpenClaw, mean of AutoSkill+EvoSkill): Raw URR 35.33 / C-ASR 21.33 / U-A 37.37% / BU 58.44 / C-Util 53.33; SafeEvolve 8.67 / 4.00 / 18.80% / 58.00 / 40.67; Utility-only 30.67 / 8.00 / 26.12% / 65.11 / 72.00; SecureClaw 24.67 / 4.67 / 22.49% / 58.44 / 60.00; ClawKeeper 25.33 / 7.33 / 25.42% / 71.33 / 59.33. Ablations: -safety retirement URR 8.67->17.33 (re-retrieves 100/106 and 44/44 threshold-crossing skills vs 0/121, 0/48); -reuse attribution B-ASR 4.44->8.22, C-Util 40.67->32.00; -paired deleter BU 58.00->51.56, C-ASR 4.00->7.33; deleter lowers critic risk by 0.53/0.40; attribution covers 108/110 and 99/99 harmful outcomes. Code: github.com/henrymao2004/misevolve (MIT, 7 stars, 3 forks, 1 commit, v0.1.0 2026-08-18).
open_gaps: Critic/repair model equals the evolving backbone by default (audit_model=$BACKBONE); no evaluation with an independent-family or stronger critic, nor of critic robustness to adaptive/stealthy skill authoring
Reuse-time retirement depends on an online harm verdict from the evaluation judge itself; unknown degradation with a weaker or noisier deployment monitor
Only SKILL.md text artifacts governed; no extension to code diffs, prompts, memory, workflow topology, or weights despite the paper's own claim that the risk generalizes
Single backbone (MiniMax-M2.7), one harness (OpenClaw) and two methods for the governance claim; no confidence intervals in main tables; no seeds/raw results released
Utility cost of governance (C-Util -12.7pp vs raw, -31pp vs Utility-only) is unaddressed; no Pareto/threshold sensitivity study for admission_risk_threshold, reuse_risk_threshold, capacity
SecureClaw and ClawKeeper baselines are not in the public repo tree, so Table 2 comparisons are not reproducible from the release
Verification-preservation is a lexical regex over requirement families; easily bypassed by paraphrase and not validated on its own
No cost, latency, or token accounting for the audit-repair-reaudit loop (up to 2 rounds per candidate)
Delete-only repair cannot restore a dropped check, only excise; the paper does not test add-permitted repair or human-in-the-loop escalation
Attacker is non-adaptive: no red-teaming of SafeEvolve itself (e.g., skills crafted to pass the critic and survive retirement thresholds)
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer: Directly on-target: SafeEvolve IS a harness-agnostic acceptance layer for one class of self-modification (skill files), and the gym is the test bed to certify one. What to reuse: (1) the two-boundary architecture - an admission gate on every write (audit full bundle + ancestor, decide accept/repair/quarantine/reject, attach lineage) plus a revocation loop at reuse (attribute each later outcome to the retrieved artifact, retire on evidence, capacity-evict by utility-minus-risk); (2) the GovernableStore control surface (snapshot_skill_bundles, is_valid, replace_skill, set_skill_status, active_skills, last_retrieved_skill_keys, export_active_skills) and 5 hook points - a compact contract already proven across Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw and Hermes without touching native evolution code; (3) the deterministic invariant 'a revision may not silently drop a verification/reversibility requirement its ancestor asserted' as an LLM-independent override of a lenient critic; (4) delete-only, re-audited repair as a conservative auto-fix policy; (5) the clean-session probe protocol (freeze artifact set, reload only the artifact into a fresh executor, measure URR/C-ASR/C-Util with fixed denominators) as an acceptance regression test for 'does the accepted change carry latent harm'; (6) the Utility-only matched control as the right null hypothesis for any acceptance layer. What it proves: unsafe state is authored universally (21/21) yet realized harm attenuates through gates (15/21), so an acceptance layer must judge artifacts and lineage, not only trajectories; outcome-based (utility) gating alone barely reduces unsafe retrieval; three exposures suffice and benign updates do not wash them out, so gates must be per-write, not periodic. What it disproves/warns: content audit + retirement cuts propagation but costs ~13pp carryover utility and does not beat a published static scanner (SecureClaw) by much on fresh-session harm - the acceptance layer's win is mainly URR. What it leaves open for an RSI acceptance layer: governing code/prompt/weight/topology changes; independence of the critic from the evolving model; operating without a gold online harm judge; adversarially robust gating; threshold calibration; cost; and formal or replayable acceptance evidence beyond LLM verdicts. Name-collision note: arXiv 2609.02786 'SafeEvolve: Harness-Policy Co-Evolution' (Mao Q. et al., Sept 2026) is a different, unrelated system.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Every task in a disposable container with fresh conversation, workspace, process namespace and tool session; only the episode-scoped skill store persists (Hermes-native HERMES_HOME is the one online exception). Judges (Gemini-3-Flash behavioral, Kimi-K2-0905 artifact) are from different families than the backbone and rejected at startup if they match. Fixed-denominator metrics so missing/failed runs count as harm-zero rather than shrinking denominators. Frozen tasks/judges/thresholds selected before evaluation; discovery concept generator hidden from evaluated systems. SafeEvolve: fail-safe quarantine when the critic returns unparseable output; deterministic verification-preservation guard; delete-only repair that cannot add unattended-agent-breaking gates; lineage persisted in SKILL.md frontmatter; retired/quarantined skills excluded from export. Repo ships SECURITY.md (threat model, sandbox requirements, credential scoping) and warns the benchmark contains harmful prompts.

deep_reads.name: Counterfactual Trace Auditing (CTA) of LLM Agent Skills
deep_reads.mechanism: Input: per task, a paired bundle of two Claude Code stream-json traces on the same repo and task, one with SKILL.md attached, one without. M1 (parser) converts events to typed read/write/execute/search/think events, extracts reasoning text, normalizes paths, sums tokens. M2 (segmenter) is a hand-tuned FSM labelling Orientation (pre-first-write), Implementation, Validation (test runs), Debugging (post-failure edits), Finalization; when it cannot segment it collapses the whole trace to Implementation (16/49 tasks hit this fallback). M3 (aligner) runs DTW over phase sequences (cost = phase-type mismatch), then aligns 'intent windows' (reasoning text plus following tool events) by TF-IDF cosine >= 0.5, emitting divergence records typed target_mismatch / content_mismatch / outcome_mismatch / unilateral_action, plus a separate pass flagging with-skill writes to files the baseline never touched. M4 (detector) applies five deterministic rule scorers per divergence: Procedural Scaffolding and Edge-case Prompting (constructive), Redundant Exploration (neutral), Surface Anchoring and Concept Bleed (destructive); a SIP fires when its score clears a threshold and several can fire on one divergence. In code the thresholds are per-type (PS .55, EP .50, RE .45, SA .40, CB .55), not the uniform 0.50 the paper states. SA scores literal and word-4-gram overlap between SKILL.md and with-skill writes that is absent from baseline writes; there is no check that the copied literal is incompatible with project config, despite the paper's SA definition requiring it. EP receives a flat +0.55 base on any unilateral_action divergence, so it fires above threshold without inspecting skill content. Outcome metric: dP = with-skill minus without-skill unit-test pass fraction, one run per condition, reported next to per-task divergence/SIP counts, per-phase distribution, and a token-overhead ratio. A M5 'predictor' exists in code but is not described in the paper.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Paper: SWE-Skills-Bench, 49 tasks, Claude Sonnet 4.5 driven by Claude Code inside Docker via a proxy that prepends a DO_NOT_ASK_OR_PLAN directive; one run per (task, condition); unit tests scored post hoc; CTA modules run over the JSONL traces; LaTeX tables generated by scripts. No human validation of segmenter or detectors, no null baseline. Post-submission (July 2026, in repo): regenerated 17 tasks with 3 no-skill and 2 with-skill reps (with-skill runs got an appended SKILL_NUDGE sentence), formed no-skill-vs-no-skill 'null floor' pairs, ran task-clustered permutation and paired sign tests, a threshold/cosine sweep, an uptake-conditioned subgroup analysis, a skill-doc-only LLM baseline (Gemini n=49, Opus n=15), and a pre-registered test of the Sec 6.2 design rule (outcome file not in repo).
deep_reads.limitations: Paper-stated: r=1 so no within-task variance; single model and benchmark; rule detectors with no human gold set; FSM segmenter unvalidated; 37/49 tasks at ceiling so mid-bucket claims rest on n=10; the only dP<0 case (premature closure) falls outside the five-class taxonomy. Repo's own audit adds: the auditor reports the same divergence/SIP volume for no-change pairs as for change pairs (excess -0.18 div, p=0.61; +0.16 SIP, p=0.48), so the 522 SIPs are largely run-to-run noise; the bucket-conditional SIP signature (Finding 2) is not supported at task level (p=0.17; ceiling SA-vs-EP 12/12/13, p=1.0); 112/186 EP fires are forced by the structural base and 29.5% of all fires need no skill content; per-type thresholds differ from the paper text; the paper's token method captured ~2.5% of true tokens (true mean ratio 1.60 vs reported 1.19); 0/34 unnudged and only 16/51 nudged with-skill runs ever read the skill, and with-runs carry 49 extra skill descriptions in context (confound); raw traces are gitignored so divergence-level results cannot be reproduced from the repo; a skill-doc-only Gemini baseline matches CTA's dominant SIP at 20% (kappa 0.04) with 0.9 stated confidence. Merged code parses only Claude Code stream-json; Hermes adapter and audit-runner PRs are open and unmerged. No runtime cost of the auditor is reported.
deep_reads.key_insight: A trace-diff auditor must be calibrated against a same-condition null floor (baseline run vs a second baseline run) before any divergence is attributed to the change under test: CTA's own replication found its rule detectors emit ~19.5 divergences and ~16 SIPs per pair whether or not the skill was present, and most with-skill runs never read the skill at all, so 'attach change, observe behavioural divergence' was mostly measuring seed noise on a no-op.
deep_reads.key_results: Paper (49 tasks, Sonnet 4.5, r=1): mean dP +0.3 pp, median 0 (45/49 tasks dP=0); 696 divergences (14.2/task), 522 SIP fires (10.7/task): EP 186, SA 184, CB 99, RE 42, PS 11; 54.2% of fires destructive; ceiling bucket (37 tasks, r->=0.9) holds 80% of SIPs at dP -0.5 pp and 1.64x tokens; mid bucket (10 tasks) dP +3.6 pp at 2.77x tokens; 84% of divergences in Orientation+Implementation; token overhead mean 1.91x, median 1.09x, max 22.24x; largest per-task moves -20.0 pp (prompt-engineering-patterns), +18.2 pp, +14.3 pp. Repo post-hoc audit (17 tasks, 187 regenerated runs): null-floor no-skill-vs-no-skill pairs give 19.55 div / 16.08 SIPs per pair vs treatment 19.37 / 16.24 (excess -0.18 div, Wilcoxon p=0.61; +0.16 SIP, p=0.48; nudged variant +1.40 / +2.49, p=0.21 / 0.11; sweep over 11 threshold/cosine configs never reaches p<0.05); replicated dP mean -0.7 pp, 95% CI [-3.9, +2.5]; Finding 2 task-clustered permutation p=0.17; fire-level destructive share 54.2% unchanged but 60.2% of EP fires structurally forced; true token ratio mean 1.60 vs paper 1.19 (paper captured ~2.5% of tokens); skill consumption 0/34 unnudged, 16/51 nudged; STRONG-uptake subgroup excess +2.22 div [-0.08,+4.01], p=0.15.
open_gaps: No same-condition null-floor calibration in the paper; the repo's later replication shows treatment divergence/SIP counts are statistically indistinguishable from no-change pairs
Skill uptake was never verified: 0/34 unnudged with-skill runs read the skill; with-runs also carry 49 extra skill descriptions in context, an uncontrolled confound

Rule detectors are uncalibrated: per-type thresholds in code differ from the paper's uniform 0.50; EP fires on a structural +0.55 base with no skill content; SA has no incompatibility check; no human gold set and no per-detector false-positive rate
r=1 on a saturated benchmark (45/49 tasks at dP=0) gives no power; every pooled bucket claim fails under task-clustered tests; replicated dP CI spans zero
Token accounting in the paper captured ~2.5% of true tokens; corrected mean ratio 1.60 vs reported 1.19
Merged code parses only Claude Code stream-json; Hermes adapter, PTY collapser, structural metrics and config-driven audit runner exist only as four open unmerged PRs from an external contributor
Raw traces are gitignored, so divergence-level co-fire matrix, phase attribution of SIPs and threshold sensitivity cannot be recomputed from the repo
DTW alignment breaks when traces are strongly asymmetric (e.g. a delegation call replacing 16 writes); no alignment-free path in the paper
No decision rule for accept/reject, no auditor runtime cost, no treatment of agents that modify their own harness rather than read a document
Taxonomy misses premature-closure, the mechanism behind the only dP<0 case; the pre-registered test of the 'declarative over procedural' design rule has no published outcome
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer: Reuse: the pipeline shape is the right one for a harness-agnostic gate: harness-specific log -> typed event stream (read/write/execute/search/think) -> phase segmentation -> paired alignment -> typed divergence records -> named detectors -> report. The external PRs make this concrete: PR#2's Hermes adapter uses an explicit tool-vocabulary map with fallback-to-generic and a five-check adapter validation (conservation, alternation, vocabulary coverage, degenerate-session SKIP vs FAIL); PR#5's audit runner is driven by a per-change YAML with tool_filters, pre-registered hypotheses carrying confirm/disconfirm thresholds, negative and edge-case controls, a detector registry with try/except isolation and a vacuous-all([]) guard; PR#3's alignment-free structural metrics (event_count_ratio, tool-entropy ratio, write_compression, unilateral actions) survive the 10x trace-length asymmetry that self-modifications routinely produce and that DTW cannot handle. The unilateral-write pass (candidate touched files the baseline never did) is a usable blast-radius primitive. What it proves, mostly by its own failure: (1) any 'did behaviour diverge from baseline' signal must be measured against a same-condition null floor with r>=3 per arm; CTA's detectors report identical volume for A-vs-A' and A-vs-B pairs, so a gate built on raw divergence would fire on every commit. (2) A gate must first verify the modification was exercised (tool_use on the artifact, distinctive-literal ingestion, bundled-resource access, as in the repo's uptake scoring) before scoring its effect; otherwise it grades a no-op and the 'effect' is seed noise. (3) Outcome deltas below the null CI on a saturated task set carry no evidence; pooled fire-level statistics that ignore task clustering will look significant when they are not. (4) Rule detectors drift from their documentation (per-type thresholds, structurally-forced fires, missing incompatibility check) and need per-detector false-positive rates, which requires retaining raw traces. (5) A skill-doc-only LLM judge matched CTA's labels at chance with 0.9 confidence: LLM-judge and rule-judge disagree, and neither is validated, so an acceptance layer needs an independent ground truth (tests with variance, or human labels), not another classifier. Left open: no accept/reject rule, no calibration data, Claude-Code-only merged code, no self-modifying-agent setting (agent edits its own harness rather than reading a document), and no cost model for the auditor itself. Practical takeaway: adopt CTA's schema and the PR#5 runner skeleton as scaffolding, replace SIP rules with null-floor-calibrated structural metrics plus uptake verification plus replicated outcome tests, and treat sub-noise deltas as 'no evidence', never as 'accept'.
deep_reads.safety_measures: None intrinsic to the method: CTA is a passive post-hoc auditor with no gating, rollback or human review. Agent runs execute in Docker containers behind a proxy that injects a DO_NOT_ASK_OR_PLAN prefix; the unmerged PR#5 runner isolates each detector in try/except, refuses to run without an explicit --config, and includes negative/edge-case control validation. Detectors are deterministic and inspect only text, so no additional model calls are made during auditing (an LLM classifier path is stubbed, unimplemented).
