deep_reads.name: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Yike Wang, Huaisheng Zhu, Zhengyu Hu, Yige Yuan, Zhengyu Chen, Shakti Senthil, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Yulia Tsvetkov, Pradeep Dasigi, Teng Xiao (Allen Institute for AI / University of Washington)
deep_reads.last_activity: arXiv v2 2026-08-27; code repo last commit 2026-08-03 (README), authors answered issue #1 on 2026-08-16
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (cs.AI), no venue. Citation count unavailable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited). Coverage: DAIR.AI tweet, AI Weekly alert, HyperAI, EmergentMind; not cited in Lilian Weng's 2026-07-04 harness post. Code: github.com/rethinking-harness-evolution/code (37 stars, 5 forks).
deep_reads.mechanism:
Not a new evolution method; a controlled re-evaluation. The paper formalizes an agent as policy pi acting under harness h (prompts, tools, middleware, memory, control logic), a meta-agent M that edits h from an observation Phi of an experience store (trajectories, and unit-test outcomes R when allowed), and a budget K = total rollouts per task. Four methods are run under identical K=5, m=1 rollout per task per round, identical model for policy and meta-agent, 2 runs averaged:
(1) Parallel sampling: K independent rollouts with the fixed initial harness; without tests, an LLM "blind selector" picks one trajectory from traces only (audited against oracle); with tests, the highest-scoring candidate is chosen, so pass@1 == pass@5 by construction (authors confirmed in issue #1).
(2) Sequential refinement: K attempts, each conditioned on the previous trajectory (plus test feedback when allowed); final trajectory returned.
(3) Harness evolution: the AHE/NexAU evolution engine (explore/retrieval agent disabled) iterates K times over the whole task batch: ADB debugger analyses each failed trajectory, meta-agent (high reasoning) edits workspace/ (systemprompt.md, code_agent.yaml, tools, middleware, skills, LongTermMEMORY.md, sub-agents), writes change_manifest.json with predicted_fixes/risk_tasks, then re-evaluates. Without tests the last harness is used; with tests the argmax-score harness over iterations.
(4) Harness scaling (new baseline): per-task harness edits over K steps, returning any trajectory the outcome accepts.
Initial harness is deliberately minimal: one run_shell_command tool, ~550-byte system prompt, 200k context, 128k max output tokens, 300 max turns, E2B sandbox via Harbor.
Generalization protocol: Terminal-Bench 2.1's 89 tasks split into 45 train / 10 val / 34 test (seeds 42/43); each iteration's harness snapshot is re-run on the held-out splits (scripts/eval_held_out_iters.py).
deep_reads.eval_loop: Terminal-Bench 2.1 (89 tasks), Harbor + E2B sandboxes, models Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4 mini (policy == meta-agent). Three settings: (a) no unit-test feedback (hide_test_results_from_agents), pass@1 averaged over 2 runs; (b) unit-test feedback visible to the selector/meta-agent (never to the code agent during a rollout), reporting pass@1 and pass@5; (c) train-on-45 / evaluate-on-34-held-out with 10 val. Meta-loop bookkeeping: per-iteration pass/fail history, task stability classes (stable_pass/stable_fail/unstable), change attribution verdicts (EFFECTIVE/PARTIALLY_EFFECTIVE/MIXED/INEFFECTIVE/HARMFUL) and unattributed_regressions, best_ever.json. Blind rollout selection is audited against oracle pass labels.
deep_reads.key_results: Table 1 (no unit tests, pass@1, avg over Opus 4.6 / GPT-5.4 / GPT-5.4 mini): initial harness 68.2; parallel sampling 72.3 (best); sequential refinement 69.3; harness evolution 67.4 (below baseline; GPT-5.4 dropped 75.3 -> 69.7); harness scaling 71.8. Table 2 (with unit tests, Opus 4.6 + GPT-5.4): pass@1 avg initial 72.9; parallel 86.0; sequential 84.3; harness evolution 75.8; harness scaling 82.6. pass@5 avg: parallel 86.0; sequential 91.8 (GPT-5.4 93.3); harness evolution 86.2 (GPT-5.4 89.3); harness scaling 89.3. Table 3 (held-out 34 tasks): initial 67.7 -> evolved 68.3, +0.6 avg (Opus +1.2, GPT-5.4 +0.0). Qualitative: edits go prompt -> middleware (budget trackers, truncation, finalization gates) -> tool layer; most edits memorize task-specific fixes (file paths, command sequences) that "a competent agent can rediscover within a single rollout"; growing prompt text causes context bloat; a stable core of hard failures is untouched by any method.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Paper itself proposes evaluation safeguards, not runtime safety: separate optimization feedback from final measurement (disjoint train/val/test), matched-budget test-time-scaling controls, benchmarks with headroom and harness sensitivity. In the studied AHE loop, safeguards are prompt-level only: meta-agent told to modify only workspace/, not touch llm_config/verifier/infrastructure, not add task-specific logic or hardcoded solutions, not reverse-engineer tests, not delete original prompt rules, run validate_agent.py, and do a no-op when evidence is insufficient. There is no mechanical in-loop acceptance gate: the loop always advances to the latest edit, perform_auto_rollback is only invoked on resume, and best_ever.json is post-hoc selection. The paper's finding that harnesses encode task-specific paths/commands shows the prompt-level constraints are not enforced in practice.
deep_reads.limitations: Single benchmark (Terminal-Bench 2.1) already near saturation for frontier models; authors concede the value of harness evolution is "likely task dependent". Single budget K=5, m=1, no scaling curves; 2 runs, no confidence intervals (34 held-out tasks means one task = 2.9 points, so +0.6 is within noise either way). Only one harness-evolution implementation (AHE/NexAU with the explore agent disabled; Meta-Harness and AEVO not run), starting from a deliberately minimal one-tool harness. Meta-agent is always the same model as the policy; stronger meta-agents untested. "Matched budget" counts policy rollouts, not meta-agent or ADB-debugger tokens, so true cost of evolution is unreported. Parallel-sampling "pass@1" with unit tests is oracle best-of-5 (pass@1 == pass@5), i.e. instance-level search with no reusable artifact, which the paper compares against a reusable harness; the framing choice drives the headline. Held-out test is within TB2.1 only, no cross-benchmark transfer. Feedback is binary pass/fail only. No analysis of harness size growth beyond qualitative "context bloat". Code released as two 220-250KB monolithic scripts with 2 commits; README says "still a work in progress".
deep_reads.key_insight: Under matched rollout budgets and disjoint train/test splits, the gains reported for automatic harness evolution on Terminal-Bench mostly disappear: parallel sampling (72.3 vs 67.4 pass@1 without tests; 86.0 vs 75.8 with tests) and sequential refinement beat it, and evolved harnesses transfer only +0.6 points to held-out tasks because the meta-agent memorizes task-specific fixes rather than distilling general design principles.
open_gaps: No statistical treatment: 2 runs, no CIs, 34 held-out tasks; an acceptance rule needs paired tests / multiple seeds to distinguish +0.6 from noise
Budget matched in rollouts only; meta-agent and ADB-debugger token cost never accounted, so cost-normalized comparison is missing
Only AHE-style evolution tested from a minimal harness; Meta-Harness, AEVO, ADAS/DGM-style code search not run under the protocol
Cross-benchmark transfer (e.g. TB2.1 -> SWE-bench) untested, so whether AHE's claimed transfer holds under this protocol is open
No ablation over K, m, meta-agent strength, or feedback granularity (process rewards, partial credit)
No mechanical detector for task-specific leakage in harness diffs (paths, task names, command sequences) despite prompt-level prohibition
Context-bloat and harness-size growth are qualitative; no size/latency regression budget proposed
Harness-sensitive benchmarks with headroom are called for but not identified or built
Parallel-sampling pass@1 with oracle test selection equals best-of-5, so the 'reusable artifact vs instance search' comparison remains conceptually contested
No countermeasures tested (regularization, early stopping on val, edit pruning, rollback-on-regression)
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer: Directly load-bearing. This is the first controlled negative result showing the two failure modes an acceptance layer for self-modifying agents must guard against are real and large: (1) search/design conflation, where an evolved harness measured on the tasks it was searched on looks better mostly because of extra rollouts (harness evolution 75.8 vs parallel sampling 86.0 pass@1 with tests), and (2) shortcut overfitting, where the same harness yields +0.6 on 34 disjoint tasks. It also shows that self-judged feedback is a dangerous acceptance signal: without verifiable outcomes, evolution degraded GPT-5.4 by 5.6 points, so a gate should refuse edits justified only by self-assessment and default to no-op. Concrete acceptance criterion it implies: accept a harness modification only if its held-out delta (disjoint task set, ideally another benchmark) exceeds what a matched-budget test-time-scaling control (parallel-K or sequential-K on the unmodified harness) achieves, and exceeds noise across seeds. Reusable pieces from the code: the pi/h/M/Phi/R/K formalization; the 45/10/34 TB2.1 split lists (seeds 42/43) and scripts/eval_held_out_iters.py, which re-runs every iteration snapshot on held-out splits, a template for 'score every candidate off-distribution before promotion'; change_manifest.json (predicted_fixes, risk_tasks, constraint_level) with automatic attribution verdicts EFFECTIVE/PARTIALLY_EFFECTIVE/MIXED/INEFFECTIVE/HARMFUL plus unattributed_regressions, a ready-made per-change acceptance record; task stability classes (stable_pass/stable_fail/unstable) to separate flakiness from true regressions; best_ever.json; and the blind rollout selector plus audit script, which measures LLM-judge selection accuracy against oracle, a way to calibrate verifier quality when ground truth is scarce. What it proves is missing in AHE-style loops and therefore what the layer must add: there is no in-loop gate (the loop always advances to the latest edit; rollback exists only on resume), prohibitions such as 'no task-specific logic' and 'do not reverse-engineer tests' are prompt-level and were violated (memorized paths/commands), so the gate needs mechanical leakage checks on harness diffs and a harness-size/context-bloat budget. Leaves open: statistical thresholds for small-N held-out sets, cost-normalized budgets that include meta-agent tokens, cross-benchmark transfer, and any notion of safety/security acceptance beyond task performance.

deep_reads.name: SEA: Self-Evolving Agents with Anytime-Valid Certificates
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Biswa Sengupta (single author), LLM Suite Team, JPMorgan Chase & Co. (with JPMC disclaimer: "not a product of the Research Department")
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-07-01 (arXiv v1 only; no v2, no code release observed as of 2026-09-14)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (cs.AI, cs.CL), CC BY-SA 4.0, 30 pages; no venue; 0 citations (OpenAlex); no HF upvotes/comments found; not indexed on Semantic Scholar web (API rate-limited)
deep_reads.mechanism: Policy at round t is pi_t = L0 ∘ L1(t) ∘ L2(t): L0 a frozen LLM (never fine-tuned), L1 a tiny steering adapter (softmax logits over k strategy directives such as "explore broadly", "smallest diff"), L2 a versioned mutable harness (force-edit threshold, step budget, strategy guidance, grown macro/anti-macro library, repair primitives). Policy version = (L1, L2); policy distance = ||theta-theta'||2 plus a unit structural step if harnesses differ. Five "loop controllers" (ALG1-5) each wrap a published guarantee in anytime-valid machinery and emit an immutable certificate {algorithm, round, decision in {ACCEPT,HOLD,REJECT,NSF}, delta_spent, cumulative_delta, metrics, note} into a ledger; a composite scheduler runs them on a two-timescale period schedule and merges sub-certificates (precedence ACCEPT>NSF>REJECT>HOLD). ALG4 (SGM-CS) is the harness-edit acceptance gate: the frozen LLM proposes an L2 edit; baseline pi_{t-1} and candidate run concurrently on the same task batch under common random numbers; compute LCB = CS_lower_{delta_k}(R_cand - R_base) - eps*W1(R_cand,R_base) using a Howard et al. normal-mixture confidence sequence and an exact 1-D Wasserstein performative correction; admit iff LCB >= -eps_tol, else NSF (keep baseline). Per-edit error spend follows a horizon-free schedule delta_k = delta_0/(Z k log^2(k+1)), Z≈3.39, so sum = delta_0 exactly (fixes SGM's finite-horizon schedule; notes delta_0/(2k log^2) over-spends by 1.69x). A wild-bootstrap trend test widens the bound if the baseline stream drifts; a pre-gate pilot on a known-passable task gives cheap NSF; a "shadow-best" retains the best patch even when the harness edit is rejected. ALG1: PAC-Bayes time-uniform forgetting gate + orthogonal-gradient trust region on L1. ALG2: Nash-MP preference learning with 30% real-data anchor and a Hoeffding e-process drift gate (freeze at E_t >= 1/delta_k). ALG3: coin-betting (KT) credit assignment with drift restarts. ALG5: Stitch MDL abstraction into a MAP-Elites archive. Five verifier mechanisms (ALG6-10) supply dense grader-free signal: best-of-N/refine, beam search over verified one-line micro-edits with parse->apply->test cascade, self-authored reproduction oracles admitted only if they fail on unpatched base (score = flip fraction, voided on any regression), re-aimed controllers, verified self-repair of harness primitives.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Benchmark: seeded 52-instance draw of SWE-bench Verified (24 Django, 27 Matplotlib, 1 Flask), official execution-based grader (all fail-to-pass pass and all pass-to-pass keep passing). In-loop signal is grader-free: self-authored oracles from issue text (ALG8, 2 samples, ensemble-pooled), a shaped process reward, and a file-overlap-F1 proxy for development only; gold tests are used exactly once at the end and never steer search. Design: 4 base models x {stack off, stack on} = 8 cells plus GLM 5.2 {no-op control, on}; every cell is ONE run; 10-step budget, 4k completion cap; each instance solved once (cached). "Off" = bare ReAct actor, no controllers/search/test-runner. "On" (Algorithms-A) = ALG1/2/3/5 as certificate controllers + ALG7-10, with ALG4 DISABLED for wall-clock (~90 min/round vs ~7 min for everything else) and ALG6 removed. Deconfounding: only on GPT-5.5 was a "no-op composite" control run (scaffolding + directives on, all algorithms off): 29 vs single-pass 28. Single-algorithm ablation on GPT-5.5 (Table 4), one run per cell. Mechanism activity is read from the certificate ledger / per-decision JSONL event log rather than pass counts.
deep_reads.key_results: Table 3 (resolved/52, off->on): GEMMA gemma4:31b nvfp4 18->22 (+4); QWEN qwen3.6:27b 24->25 (+1); GPT-MINI gpt-5.4-mini 25->29 (+4); GPT gpt-5.5 (reasoning off) 28->34 (+6); GLM 5.2 24 (no-op control; no single-pass baseline run) -> 28 (+4). GPT no-op composite control = 29, so suite = +5 over control; best config 34/52 = 65% (the "65%" is simply 34/52). Table 4, GPT single-algorithm cells: ALG1 30, ALG2 34 (+5, directive learner), ALG3 31, ALG4 36 (gate accepted 0 edits, effectively ran the control config; flagged as artifact), ALG5 28 (~0 accepts), ALG6 26 (best-of-2 never produced a 2nd attempt, added apply failures; removed), ALG7 32, ALG8 32, ALG9 29, ALG10 30, full suite 34 — gains overlap rather than add (full = best single). Event logs (§9.2): run_tests calls +~50%, mean episode length +~1.3 steps vs control; ALG2 and ALG3 each made 52 policy updates; ALG1/4/5 "contribute less"; regressions: 4 pass-to-pass-flagged instances (full suite) vs 3 (control); 17/52 solved by every config, 10/52 by none (mostly Matplotlib). Defaults: delta_0=0.05, eps_tol=0.02, eps=0.1, CS alpha=0.05, sigma=0.5. Paper explicitly reports "magnitudes rather than significance."
deep_reads.safety_measures: Frozen base L0 (no weight updates in any reported run; LoRA distillation designed but not trained); self-edits confined to a low-dim adapter and a versioned harness so every policy version is identifiable and rollback-able; ALG4 edits only L2 and is "the governance layer to deploy first"; NSF abstention as the default outcome, keeps baseline; global error budget delta_0=0.05 spent by horizon-free CTHS so familywise error is bounded over unbounded edits; performative W1 correction and wild-bootstrap widening on drift; trust region + PAC-Bayes forgetting gate on adapter; 30% real-data anchor and e-process drift gate that freezes the preference model once budget is spent; gold tests held out from the loop; self-oracle score voided on any regression of a green check, patches reported as "promising" never "resolved"; oracle admission requires fail-on-base plus symptom judge; immutable per-round certificates plus an opt-in flushed JSONL per-decision audit sink that survives crashes; cost-aware scheduler skips controllers with no committed gain.
deep_reads.limitations: Author-stated: all endogenous-loop guarantees are conjectures, not theorems ("we do not derive new bounds"); compositions (two-timescale ALG2, backward-transfer ALG1, performative corrections in ALG1/ALG4) unproven; eps is a hyperparameter not estimable online with validity and eps*L<1 may fail at LLM scale; anytime gates are conservative ("ALG4 guarantees safety, not progress", may abstain forever); single run per cell; slow loop not trained; one harness only; per-task algorithm-problem matching unknown. Observed on deep read: the certificate gate ALG4 was disabled in the headline configuration and accepted 0 edits in isolation, ALG5 ~0 accepts, so the anytime-valid acceptance layer never demonstrably admitted a self-modification; the +4/+5 derives from ungated directive learners and per-task search. The ALG4 cell scoring 36 while running the control config shows run-to-run noise >= +7 on 52 instances (binomial sd ~3.5), exceeding the claimed +5. Only GPT-5.5 has both a single-pass baseline and a no-op control; GLM's +4 lacks a baseline. Certificate counts (ACCEPT/HOLD/REJECT/NSF per controller) are never tabulated despite the ledger. "Prevents regressions" rests on 4 vs 3 regressions. No code URL; single-author industry preprint with 0 citations.
deep_reads.key_insight: An honest anytime-valid acceptance gate on end-task reward, at realistic evaluation budgets (~50 tasks, paired concurrent deploys), is so conservative and so expensive (~90 min/round, 13x the rest of the loop) that it admits nothing and gets switched off — while the components that actually moved the metric (directive shaping, verified micro-search, self-authored test oracles) run ungated every round. The paper's own ledger, not its scores, is what caught a control-configuration run outscoring every real configuration.
open_gaps: ALG4, the anytime-valid harness-edit gate, was disabled in the headline suite and accepted 0 edits in its ablation; no reported run shows a certificate gate admitting a self-modification
Single run per cell; the ALG4 cell scored 36 running the control config, so run-to-run noise on the 52-instance slice is at least +7, larger than the claimed +5 suite effect
Only GPT-5.5 has both a single-pass baseline and a no-op control; GLM 5.2 has no baseline
No public code despite an 'executable reference implementation'; four GitHub searches found nothing
Familywise validity under an endogenous proposer that can exploit residual statistical slack is stated as open; eps is a hyperparameter and eps*L<1 is unverified
Per-controller certificate decision counts (ACCEPT/HOLD/REJECT/NSF) are never reported, so the ledger's actual behavior is opaque
'Prevents regressions' claim rests on 4 vs 3 pass-to-pass regressions with no statistics
One harness, one benchmark slice (Django/Matplotlib); the paper itself names a harness x model factorial study as the most informative next step
Slow loop (distilling verified traces into a LoRA) designed but never trained; gate over weight updates is untested
Gate cost (~90 min/round with three concurrent multi-step deploys) makes proper paired gating impractical at this budget; no cheaper surrogate for harness edits is validated
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer: Directly on-topic: SEA is an attempt at exactly a certificate-emitting acceptance layer for self-edits, and its failure mode is the most instructive part. REUSE: (1) the certificate schema (Appendix C) — immutable per-round record {algorithm, round, decision in ACCEPT/HOLD/REJECT/NSF, delta_spent, cumulative_delta, metrics map, note}, plus an opt-in flushed JSONL per-decision audit sink that survives crashes, and a composite merge rule (per-algorithm metric prefixes, summed spends, precedence ACCEPT>NSF>REJECT>HOLD) — is a ready-made ledger format; (2) the horizon-free CTHS spending schedule delta_k = delta_0/(Z k log^2(k+1)), Z≈3.39, which bounds familywise error over an unbounded edit stream without pre-committing a horizon (and the warning that the naive 1/(2k log^2) schedule silently over-spends by 1.69x); (3) the paired-evaluation protocol: baseline and candidate run concurrently on the same task batch under common random numbers in isolated workspaces, lower confidence bound via a time-uniform normal-mixture CS, admit iff LCB >= -eps_tol else NSF, free guards (no-op proposal / exhausted budget spend nothing), a cheap pre-gate pilot on a known-passable task, and wild-bootstrap widening when the baseline stream drifts; (4) the performative correction term eps*W1(R_cand,R_base) as a principled acknowledgement that an accepted edit changes the distribution it was judged on; (5) decoupling 'which harness to deploy' (gated) from 'which artifact to ship' (shadow-best) plus requeue of rejected harnesses that produced good outputs, so gate conservatism never discards good work; (6) the actor protocol (policy, task, attempt) -> (action, trajectory, process reward) as a harness-agnostic interface sketch; (7) self-authored test oracles with fail-on-base admission, symptom judging, and regression-voiding as a grader-free verifier whose failure mode is under-claiming only; (8) versioning identity (L1,L2) with a measurable policy distance, which is the paper's argument for why a frozen substrate is what makes deltas gate-able at all. WHAT IT PROVES/DISPROVES: it demonstrates empirically that a statistically honest per-edit gate on end-task pass rate at ~50 tasks (CS alpha=0.05, sigma=0.5) has a radius far wider than plausible per-edit gains, so it admits nothing (ALG4: 0 accepts; ALG5: ~0), and that proper paired gating is the dominant compute cost (~90 min/round vs 7 min) and therefore gets disabled — i.e. the acceptance layer must either accumulate evidence across many cheap rounds, gate on denser proxy signals with a cascade, or accept much larger batches. It also shows that ledger-based attribution, not the metric, is what detects 'gate accepted nothing but the score moved' — an argument that any acceptance layer must log decisions and spend, not just outcomes. It shows the uncomfortable split that what is gated does not move and what moves is not gated (directive learners fire every round ungated). LEAVES OPEN: validity when the proposer is endogenous and can exploit slack; online estimation of eps; any evidence that a certificate ever blocked a harmful edit; cross-harness generality (one harness tested); gating of weight updates (slow loop untrained); gating edits to the gate or evaluator itself; and reproducibility, since no code is public — everything must be re-implemented from Appendix A pseudocode, Appendix C schema and Appendix D defaults.

deep_reads.name: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit: Disentangling Evolution Capabilities in Self-Evolving LLM Agents
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Minhua Lin, Juncheng Wu, Zijun Wang, Zhan Shi, Yisi Sang, Bing He, Zewen Liu, Tianxin Wei, Zongyu Wu, Zhiwei Zhang, Dakuo Wang, Xiang Zhang, Benoit Dumoulin, Cihang Xie, Yuyin Zhou, Suhang Wang, Hanqing Lu — Penn State, UC Santa Cruz, Amazon, Emory, UIUC, Northeastern (A-EVO-Lab)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-08-22 (release/harness-evolution branch: README updated with EMNLP 2026 citation; main branch also pushed 2026-08-22)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: EMNLP 2026 Main (per repo README, 2026-08-22). OpenAlex: 0 citations as of 2026-09-14; Semantic Scholar rate-limited. 24 pages, 9 figures, 12 tables.
deep_reads.mechanism:
Setup: agent A_t=(f,H_t) with frozen model f and a file-system harness H (prompts/system.md, skills/*/SKILL.md, memory/*.jsonl; tools/ and eval scripts read-only). Solve->observe->evolve loop: batch X_t is solved under H_{t-1} and scored (score locked before that task's evidence enters), evidence D_t={(task, trajectory, output/feedback)} goes to an evolver model e which emits dH_t; H_t=Apply(H_{t-1},dH_t) is unconditional — no held-out check, no regression gate. In-situ: the same task stream is both evolution and evaluation set.

Code path (A-Evolve UnifiedEngine, branch release/harness-evolution): readers (PassFailReader, TrajectoryCompressor, ClaimReader, PatternDetector...) build a canonical-JSON evidence context; operator LLMBashEvolve makes one tool-using LLM call with a `workspace_bash` tool (cwd=workspace, 60s timeout, no sandbox) under a fixed system prompt ("meta-learning agent... analyze observation logs, refine drafts into skills, improve system prompt, update memory, verify with git diff"). Scope is enforced only post hoc: byte-snapshot restore of out-of-scope dirs plus a max_skills cap. MCP recipe also runs FixHallucinations (tool-name corrections), AutoSeedSkills and a deterministic SanityCheck (prompt <=4000 chars, drop skills <20 chars, Jaccard>0.6 dedup, strip batch-specific lines, <=15 skills). Verifier in every paper recipe is NoVerify (always accept). Git tags pre-evo-N/evo-N snapshot each cycle; StagnationRollback exists but is unused.

Configs: SWE-bench Verified 500 tasks, batch 20 (~25 cycles), 140 max steps; MCP-Atlas 500 tasks, batch 30, Sonnet 4.6 claims judge; SkillsBench 86 tasks, batch 1, <=2 solve-evolve cycles per task, plus success-gated draft promotion (threshold 1). Single seed 42 everywhere.

Decomposition: D_update(e)=mean gain over anchor agents {Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, Qwen3-235B}; D_benefit(f)=max gain over the same three as evolvers. 7 models paired (Qwen3.5-9B evolver-only). Diagnostics: Skill-Load Rate (valid standalone skill-load action in trajectory), Harness-Following Rate (Sonnet extracts a locked JSON rubric from SKILL.md, then judges the model-blinded trajectory per instruction at T=0), phase-level adherence (post-load/mid/final), pass-when-loaded rate, mechanical proxies (retrieval-to-use gap, early termination, answer-before-validation).
deep_reads.eval_loop: Per benchmark: fixed seed harness H_0 -> solve batch under H_{t-1} -> score with benchmark grader (SWE: hidden tests; MCP-Atlas: claims-based rubric with LLM judge; SkillsBench: task tests, partial scores) -> evolver rewrites harness via bash -> next batch. Metric is the in-situ pass rate over the whole stream; gain = evolved minus no-evolution baseline for the same agent. Exp0 varies evolver over 3 anchor agents (D_update); Exp1 varies agent over 3 anchor evolvers (D_benefit). Extreme-pairing check (Table 6). Agent-side failure analysis on SkillsBench via SLR/HFR/LPR and phase-level adherence. One seed per cell; no CIs or significance tests; no held-out split reported (a run_exp1.py train/test route exists in the repo but the paper uses in-situ only).
deep_reads.key_results: Base (SWE/MCP/SB): Opus 4.6 74.2/61.0/25.6; Sonnet 4.6 73.2/54.0/24.4; Qwen3-235B 20.7/25.0/4.7. D_update range: SWE 5.9-8.2 pp (best Qwen3-235B, worst GPT-OSS-120B), MCP 0.6-3.6 (best Opus, worst Qwen3-235B), SB 0.7-3.8 (best Qwen3.5-9B 3.8 vs Opus 2.3, worst Qwen3-32B); best-worst evolver gap <=3.1 pp, no evolver wins across benchmarks. D_benefit (SWE/MCP/SB): Qwen3-32B 4.4/1.0/5.8; Qwen3-235B 19.3/4.3/1.1; GPT-OSS-120B 15.8/7.0/7.0; Haiku 4.5 2.4/3.6/15.1; Sonnet 2.8/3.2/3.5; Opus 2.6/3.6/5.8 (inverted-U). Extreme pairing: strong agent + worst evolver beats weak agent + best evolver by 18.6-35.2 pp (SWE 75.2 vs 40.0; MCP 61.6 vs 29.3; SB 31.4 vs 8.1). SB diagnostics SLR/HFR/LPR: Qwen3-32B .251/.142/.023; GPT-OSS .446/.442/.040; Haiku .794/.600/.099; Qwen3-235B .961/.350/.022; Sonnet .959/.730/.145; Opus .957/.757/.177. Phase adherence load->mid->final: Qwen3-32B .52->.22->.13 (-.39), GPT-OSS .67->.48->.43 (-.24), Opus .89->.79->.80 (-.09). Negative cells exist: MCP Qwen3-235B self-evolved 24.3 vs 25.0 (-0.7); SB Sonnet-evolver->Qwen3-235B 3.5 vs 4.7 (-1.2). Case study: Qwen3.5-9B and Opus produce "procedurally isomorphic" skills for flink-query, both lifting the agent 0.67->1.0.
deep_reads.limitations: Single seed per cell (scripts: "DEC-7: single default seed"; adapters do not reshuffle task order), no variance or significance — on SkillsBench one task is ~1.2 pp, so the 0.7-3.8 pp D_update spread is 1-3 tasks and "flat" is indistinguishable from a noise floor; MCP gains of 0.6-3.6 pp are LLM-judged. D_benefit is a max over three noisy estimates, which biases it upward and could manufacture part of the inverted-U. In-situ only: evolver sees the same stream it is scored on (SWE-bench repos repeat), so gains may include distribution-specific memorization; no held-out generalization reported. Every update is accepted unconditionally (NoVerify); no per-update attribution, no bloat/interference or over-rounds analysis, no cost/token accounting, no adversarial or unsafe-update evaluation (ethics statement only). HFR/SLR measured only on SkillsBench; judge is a Claude model judging Claude and non-Claude trajectories (blinded, but same-family risk). Qwen3.5-9B only as evolver. Released SWE wrapper defaults (FEEDBACK=none, EVOLVER_DRIVEN=false) route to a no-op recipe unless overridden, and the evolver-driven scope grants prompts+memory, not the skills-only scope the paper states — reproduction details are ambiguous. Weights fixed; no comparison to fine-tuning or hybrid adaptation. Reproduction needs Bedrock, Docker, MCP-Atlas API keys.
deep_reads.key_insight: The bottleneck in harness self-evolution is consumption, not production: a 9B evolver writes updates as useful as Opus 4.6's, but whether an update helps depends almost entirely on whether the task-solving agent activates it (skill-load rate 25% vs 96%) and keeps following it over a long trajectory (adherence drifting .52->.13 vs .89->.80). Therefore an update's value is a property of the (update, consuming agent) pair, not of the update alone.
open_gaps: No acceptance gate is evaluated at all: the paper never asks whether a verifier could have rejected the negative cells (-0.7, -1.2 pp) or which of the accumulated skills drove the gains
No held-out / cross-distribution evaluation of evolved harnesses, though run_exp1.py implements a train/test route
Single seed and no CIs: the 'flat harness-updating' claim needs multi-seed replication before it can be used to size an evolver budget
Harness-benefit is a max over three evolvers (upward-biased); a mean or per-pair estimate is not reported

No analysis of harness growth, contradictory updates, or quality drift across the ~17-25 cycles; SanityCheck caps (15 skills, 4000-char prompt) silently delete content without being reported as an intervention
Activation and adherence are measured only on SkillsBench and only with a Claude judge; no human validation of HFR labels
No cost/latency accounting for evolver vs solver, which the 'spend budget on the solver' recommendation depends on
Evolver has unsandboxed bash over the workspace (60s timeout); sibling MetaHarness engine on main has a compile()-only candidate gate (issue #28) — safety of code-level harness edits is unaddressed
The 'bake harness invocation into agent training' recommendation is untested (no training experiment)
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer: Directly relevant as a negative baseline and as a source of reusable primitives. (1) What it proves: with Apply() unconditional and every recipe's verifier = NoVerify, regressions do get committed (MCP Qwen3-235B self-evolve -0.7 pp; SB Sonnet->Qwen3-235B -1.2 pp), so an acceptance layer is needed even with strong evolvers; and because evolver quality barely matters (<=3.1 pp spread, 9B ~ Opus) while benefit varies 1-19 pp by consuming agent, a gate that statically reviews the diff ("is this a good skill?") will have low discriminative power — acceptance must be agent-in-the-loop and execution-based, testing the update against the specific target agent. It also shows the two concrete failure channels an acceptance test should probe: activation (does the agent emit a valid load of the artifact when relevant? malformed multi-key load actions silently fail) and adherence (does it keep following the artifact late in the trajectory?). Cross-model verification is viable since same-family self-evolution shows no privilege. (2) What to reuse: the Reader/Operator/Verifier protocol with Verdict{accept, rollback, reason} is a clean harness-agnostic slot (agent_evolve/algorithms/unified/interfaces.py, types.py); git-tagged pre-evo-N/evo-N snapshots with rollback-as-new-commit (engine/versioning.py) give auditable revert; the artifact_scope {ro,rw,append,none} contract plus post-hoc byte-snapshot restore (_enforce_post_scope) is a reusable structural gate; StagnationRollback (unused) is a minimal score-based regression gate; the HFR pipeline (locked rubric extraction from SKILL.md -> blinded per-instruction adherence judging -> mechanical proxies like retrieval-to-use gap and answer-before-validation) is a ready-made 'was the update actually consumed' signal; SLR/LPR (pass-when-loaded) are cheap activation metrics; the in-situ score-locking rule (score under H_{t-1} before evidence enters) is a leakage-safe online metric; the D_update/D_benefit pairwise decomposition is a good evaluation design for benchmarking an acceptance layer itself (does the gate's accept/reject correlate with realized pairwise gain?). (3) What it leaves open: no held-out validation of any update, no per-update attribution, no drift/bloat monitoring across rounds, no adversarial or unsafe-update tests, single-seed deltas too noisy to calibrate acceptance thresholds, and the sibling MetaHarness path (issue #28) shows code-level harness edits gated only by compile() and executed in-process — an acceptance layer for this family must add sandboxed execution, held-out regression tests, and per-agent activation/adherence checks.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Evolver may not modify eval scripts, tools/, or weights (scope contract; enforced post hoc by snapshot restore, not by sandboxing — the bash tool runs unsandboxed in the workspace with a 60s timeout). All harness updates logged and git-tagged per cycle (pre-evo-N/evo-N), rollback preserved as new commits. MCP recipe: deterministic SanityCheck (size caps, dedup, strip batch-specific lines, seed-identity restore) and FixHallucinations. SkillsBench: skills distilled only from successful trajectories, promoted at threshold 1. No verifier in any recipe (NoVerify); StagnationRollback registered but unused. Ethics statement notes risks of persisted incorrect lessons, unsafe tool-use rules, and sensitive-info leakage; states benchmark logging/access controls do not guarantee safety in open deployment. Open issue #28 (main branch MetaHarness): proposer-written harness.py is exec'd in-process with a compile()-only gate.

deep_reads.name: PACE: Anytime-Valid Acceptance Tests for Self-Evolving Agents (Paired Anytime-valid Commit Evaluation)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-06-06 (arXiv v1 only; no revisions, no code). Downstream: cited by arXiv 2608.24876 (Recuris, Aug 2026) and 2609.06593 (Sep 2026).
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Zayx Shawn (sole author, listed as Independent Researcher; no affiliation, no funding/acknowledgments; Semantic Scholar profile shows 2 papers total, h-index 0)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (cs.AI), CC BY 4.0, not peer-reviewed. Semantic Scholar: 2 citations, 0 influential, 32 references (as of 2026-09-14). Not on HF Papers. Note name collision with unrelated "PACE: Two-Timescale Self-Evolution for SLM Agents" (2605.23019) and "PACE-Bench" (2608.14441).
deep_reads.mechanism:
Problem framing: a self-evolution loop applies "commit if dev score went up" hundreds of times against the same small, noisy dev set. This is uncorrected adaptive multiple testing on a reused holdout (cites Dwork et al. 2015): the agent p-hacks itself, accumulating false commits that cause churn and drift. A larger dev set only postpones the problem (noise shrinks as 1/sqrt(n) while adaptive comparisons grow with the run); Bonferroni-style corrections need T known in advance; fresh labeled data per round is impractical.

PACE recasts each commit decision as a sequential test. For candidate c' vs incumbent c: evaluate both on the SAME dev instances one at a time (paired design removes instance-difficulty variance). Discard ties (both right / both wrong, McNemar-style). For each discordant pair set w_i = 1 if candidate right and incumbent wrong, else 0. Maintain betting wealth E_0 = 1, E <- E * (1 + lambda*(2*w_i - 1)) with fixed lambda = 0.5. Null H0: Pr[w_i = 1 | past] <= 1/2 (candidate not better); under H0, E is a nonnegative supermartingale, so by Ville's inequality Pr[sup_t E_t >= 1/alpha] <= alpha regardless of when you stop looking. Commit the moment E >= 1/alpha (alpha = 0.05, i.e. E >= 20); if the dev set/budget is exhausted first, reject. Early stopping is what saves evaluations (the run is anytime-valid so peeking is free). Under H1 wealth grows exponentially; under H0 it hovers near 1.

Interface: the gate only consumes paired per-instance pass/fail outcomes, so it is training-free and, in principle, proposer- and loop-agnostic (prompts, skills, workflows, code). The guarantee is explicitly per-candidate ("conditional on its own evaluation stream"), not a run-level familywise bound; expected false commits across a run grow as at most alpha per non-improving candidate, and the authors state loop-level adaptivity (same 40 dev items reused for every candidate) "is treated as an empirical matter, not a theoretical claim."
deep_reads.eval_loop: Own prompt-evolution loop (not embedded in DSPy/ADAS/DGM). Agent = frozen Qwen2.5-Instruct 0.5B/1.5B/3B steered by an editable system prompt; a separate, unnamed proposer LLM proposes one prompt edit per round; the accept rule decides commit. Data: reused dev n=40; disjoint audit pool n=120 that the accept rule never sees (metrics are "audit-labelled" at temperature 0, not ground truth). Tasks: GSM8K exact-match (main), SVAMP and ARC-Challenge (Table 5, 1.5B only). Two regimes: (1) Controlled, temperature 0, 5 seeds: incumbent prompt carries one deliberately harmful instruction the proposer can remove for a known large true gain (~+0.57 to +0.74), hidden among noisy proposals; a milder variant (+0.18 true gain) tests power. (2) Stochastic, agent sampled at T=0.7, 3 seeds: no real gain exists, so every commit is spurious. Baselines: greedy (commit iff dev score rose), paired fixed-n McNemar test (n=40), and a "decaying-memory online-FDR" variant (algorithm and decay not specified). Metrics: commits/run, false commit (audited delta <= 0), harmful commit (audited delta < 0), end-to-end audit accuracy delta, evaluation cost = number of dev problems scored. Sensitivity: alpha in {0.01, 0.05, 0.10}, n in {20, 40, 80}. Number of rounds T per run is never stated (greedy's 2080-eval cost at n=40 implies roughly 50 candidates per run). No code released.
deep_reads.key_results: Controlled GSM8K (Table 1): 1.5B greedy 3.4+-1.2 commits/run, 42% false, 33% harmful, delta +0.57+-0.03; PACE 1.0 commit, 0% false, 0% harmful, delta +0.57+-0.04. 3B greedy 3.0+-2.6 commits, 30% false, 10% harmful, delta +0.54+-0.30; PACE 1.0 commit, 0/0%, delta +0.74+-0.04 (same mean gain, variance ~8x lower). Cost at 1.5B: PACE 1712 vs greedy 2080 paired dev problems (~18% fewer) via early stopping. Stochastic GSM8K (Table 2, no real gain): greedy 20.7/15.3/13.3 commits per run for 0.5B/1.5B/3B, 82%/72%/100% false, 0.5B held-out accuracy driven down 4.9+-3.0 points; PACE 0.3/0.3/0.0 commits (i.e. one commit total across 3 seeds for 0.5B and 1.5B, which was audited false -> the reported "33% false" is on a near-empty denominator), delta ~0. Paired fixed-n McNemar baseline matches PACE in the controlled regime (1 commit, 0% false) but is worse in stochastic (1.5B: 0.7 commits, 67% false). Online-FDR commits nothing in stochastic (good) but loses the genuine improvement entirely at alpha=0.01 (delta 0.000) and only partially at n=20 (delta +0.41). Sensitivity (Table 4): PACE commits the one real edit with 0% false at every alpha/n setting (delta ~+0.57-0.58) while greedy is 33-53% false. Cross-task (Table 5, 1.5B): SVAMP controlled greedy 5.3 commits/43% false/+0.41 vs PACE 1.0/0%/+0.43; SVAMP stochastic greedy 12.0/74% vs PACE 0.0/0%; ARC stochastic greedy 16.0/67% vs PACE 0.0/0%. Power cost: with the milder +0.18 handicap PACE kept 78% of the gain vs greedy's 100% (greedy paid 17% false/harmful commits).
deep_reads.limitations: Author-acknowledged (Table 3, Section 6): guarantee is per-candidate only, not run-level familywise; results are audit-labelled at temperature 0, not ground truth; only 3-5 seeds; strongest effects on tiny (0.5B-3B) agents; prompt-level edits only, one model family, one proposer, own loop rather than a third-party system, so "proposer-/loop-agnostic" is argued not shown; power is the price of safety (a +0.18 gain was only 78% recovered; gains too small for the budget are rejected), so the gate is the wrong tool when true gains are tiny and misses cost more than false commits; the gate inherits dev-set coverage and cannot certify improvements the dev set cannot see. Reviewer-noted: the controlled regime is easy (a single large planted improvement of +0.57-0.74 among noise); no code, proposer identity, proposer prompt, handicap text, rounds T, batch size, or online-FDR algorithm are specified, so it is not reproducible from the text; the same 40 dev items are reused for every candidate, so the supermartingale's conditional-fairness assumption is only clean within one candidate and cross-candidate dependence (the exact reused-holdout problem the paper opens with) is left unaddressed theoretically; unclear whether incumbent outputs are cached or re-sampled under T=0.7, which affects both cost accounting and the validity of the paired sign test; lambda is fixed at 0.5 rather than adaptive/mixture betting, which is neither power-optimal nor discussed; binary pass/fail outcomes only, no continuous or multi-objective metrics; the fixed-n McNemar baseline already achieves 0% false in the controlled regime, so PACE's marginal contribution there is the ~18% early-stopping saving, not safety; the "33% false" PACE stochastic cells are 1 event over 3 seeds; single independent author, unreviewed, 2 citations, no follow-up.
deep_reads.key_insight: The weak point in self-evolution loops is the acceptor, not the proposer: "keep it if the dev score went up" applied repeatedly to one small reused dev set is uncontrolled adaptive multiple testing, so the agent p-hacks itself into churn and drift. Replacing that rule with a paired, testing-by-betting e-process (commit only when wealth E >= 1/alpha, evaluations run one instance at a time on identical inputs) gives a training-free, harness-agnostic, per-candidate false-commit bound that is valid under optional stopping, which simultaneously makes early stopping free (~18% cheaper) and removes essentially all false commits without losing the real one.
open_gaps: Run-level / familywise or FDR control across an entire self-improvement run is not provided; only per-candidate alpha, so expected false commits still scale with the number of candidates tested

Dependence induced by reusing the same dev set for every candidate is treated as an empirical matter, not covered by the theorem; no analysis of how many rounds until the reused dev set is effectively burned
Only binary pass/fail paired outcomes; no extension to continuous scores, multi-objective acceptance, cost/latency constraints, or safety/invariant checks

Only prompt-level edits on 0.5B-3B Qwen models on GSM8K/SVAMP/ARC; nothing at the code, skill, workflow, or harness level, and no integration into an existing self-evolving system (DGM, ADAS, DSPy, GEPA) despite the claimed interface generality
Low power for small real gains (78% recovery of a +0.18 gain); no adaptive or mixture betting (lambda fixed at 0.5), no power analysis, no budget-aware alpha allocation
No code, no proposer identity or prompt, no stated T, batch size, or online-FDR algorithm; not reproducible from the paper
Metrics are audit-labelled on a 120-item pool at temperature 0 rather than ground-truth; 3-5 seeds
Unclear whether incumbent outputs are cached across candidates; under T=0.7 sampling this matters for both the paired-test validity and the cost comparison
Adversarial or dev-set-overfitting proposers (the case where a candidate is genuinely better on dev but not on the distribution) are not studied; the gate inherits dev coverage by construction
No mechanism for updating the incumbent's evidence or for rollback/re-testing previously committed edits as the dev set or distribution drifts
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer:
Directly on-target: this is the only item in the RSI literature I have seen whose entire contribution is the acceptance gate rather than the proposer, and it articulates the core failure mode an acceptance layer must defend against (repeated greedy acceptance on a reused noisy evaluator = self-p-hacking, producing churn and drift rather than improvement, demonstrated as 30-100% false commits and a 4.9-point held-out regression on the weakest agent).

What to reuse: (1) The interface contract. PACE needs nothing from the harness except paired per-instance pass/fail outcomes for (incumbent, candidate) on identical inputs; that is exactly the harness-agnostic boundary an acceptance layer wants, and it works for prompts, skills, workflows, or code diffs alike. (2) The decision rule itself: discard ties, w = 1[candidate right, incumbent wrong], E *= 1 + lambda(2w-1), commit at E >= 1/alpha, reject on budget exhaustion. It is ~10 lines, has no training, and its anytime validity means the layer can stream evaluations and stop early without invalidating the guarantee, which is the property that makes it cheaper than the fixed-n McNemar test while equally safe. Open-source anytime-valid libraries (e.g. assuncaolfi/savvi, confseq-style betting CIs) can supply the same primitive with adaptive betting fractions. (3) The evaluation protocol: a reused dev set for decisions plus a disjoint, never-touched audit pool for post-hoc labelling of false/harmful commits, plus the "planted known improvement among noise" and "no-real-gain stochastic" regimes, are a reusable benchmark design for stress-testing any acceptance gate (does it commit the real one, and nothing else?).

What it proves: a per-candidate statistical gate with optional-stopping validity matches greedy's mean gain at much lower variance, kills essentially all spurious commits, and is robust across alpha in [0.01, 0.10] and n in [20, 80], at least for prompt edits on small models. It also shows the naive alternatives fail differently: greedy is unsafe, fixed-n paired tests are safe but waste budget and still misfire under sampling noise, and online-FDR over-corrects and loses real gains at small alpha.

What it leaves open for the layer: PACE controls only per-candidate error, so a long run still accumulates ~alpha false commits per rejected-in-truth candidate; the layer needs a run-level budget (alpha-investing / e-value merging across candidates, or a global e-process over the commit history) and a rollback/re-verification path. It gives no treatment of dev-set reuse across candidates, which is the same reusable-holdout problem it opens with, so the layer needs dev-set rotation, holdout refresh, or reusable-holdout-style noise. It handles only binary correctness; an acceptance layer for self-modifying agents must also gate on invariants (tests still pass, no capability regressions, cost/latency, safety constraints), which suggests composing PACE-style e-processes per criterion and multiplying/averaging e-values. Its power ceiling (78% recovery of a +0.18 gain at n=40) means an acceptance layer using it will systematically reject small but real improvements, so budget-aware alpha and adaptive betting (lambda via ONS/mixture) are needed. Finally, none of this has been validated on code-level self-modification, larger models, or inside any real harness (DGM, ADAS, GEPA), and there is no code, so the layer would have to reimplement and re-validate it; that is cheap to do and is a high-value early experiment.
deep_reads.safety_measures: The commit gate itself is the safety mechanism: per-candidate false-commit probability <= alpha under optional stopping (Ville's inequality on a test supermartingale), reject-on-budget-exhaustion, and strict separation of a reused dev set from a disjoint audit pool the accept rule never sees. No sandboxing, rollback, invariant checks, or run-level error budget; edits are confined to the system prompt of a frozen model so there is no code execution risk in the experiments.

deep_reads.name: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Yuhao Wu, Jingyuan Zhang, Jiajun Shi (core) + 16 others incl. Jiaheng Liu, Shen Yan, Wenhao Huang, Ge Zhang, Wenxuan Zhang — ByteDance Seed, TokenWave.AI, SUTD, Georgia Tech, M-A-P
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-09 (project-page repo Self-Developing-Agents.github.io last push); paper v1 2026-09-01
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (cs.SE, cs.CL), v1; no citations yet. Third paper in ByteDance Seed/TokenWave 'Self-Developing Agents' series with Aspire (2608.31100) and S3Gym (2608.31111).
deep_reads.mechanism:
HarnessDev is a benchmark, not a self-improvement method. It measures whether a frontier LLM (the "creator", run inside Claude Code 2.1.177 or Codex 0.144.3) can build and then evolve the model-external execution harness that a downstream "executor" LLM runs inside.

Stage 1, Creation: creator starts from a deliberately weak but runnable Python seed (H_seed) that only parses tasks, exposes passive primitives (file ops, search, process exec), configures the LLM endpoint, and writes audit artifacts (result.json, trajectory.jsonl, response.md). Unmodified it scores 0 everywhere. Creator receives a task-family spec, permission constraints, a short design tutorial and 1-3 dev cases, and must implement six modules under a shared interface contract: execution loop (run/step), tools (register/call), context (build/compress), state and memory (save/load/resume), lifecycle and recovery (beforeAction/afterAction/onFailure/onTimeout), verification (evaluate(result,criteria)->Score, recordTrajectory). Three independent creations per creator per domain (avg@3). Four domains: Code (SWE-Pro, Terminal-Bench 2.1), Data/ML (MLE-bench), Writing (EQ-Bench3), Search (BrowseComp); 2,207 downstream instances, 6 creators.

Stage 2, Evolution (Code only): creator iterates on its own frozen H0 using execution feedback from a fixed 100-task SWE-Pro + 89-task Terminal-Bench feedback set. Budget: 10 post-H0 full paired evaluations, at most 2 cheap 5-task probes between charged pairs (probes never count). A version is "official" only after both legs complete; creator terminates by declaring a non-H0 commit (H_dec). Every official version is also scored on 630 held-out SWE-Pro instances never shown to the creator. Metric: pair-score = mean of the two feedback percentages.

Two evaluation modes: Self-Eval (creator = executor) and Unified-Eval (all harnesses run under a fixed Gemini 3.1 Pro executor) to expose executor co-adaptation. Evolution is also re-run as separate lineages under the fixed Gemini executor. Scoring path is isolated from the harness: self-reported status is never an input; SWE-Pro credit comes only from the real repo diff, Terminal-Bench only from final environment state. Post-hoc audit of harness source plus trajectories checks four prohibited routes.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Creator sees only feedback-set scores (100 SWE-Pro + 89 Terminal-Bench) plus its own trajectory artifacts; held-out-630 scores are withheld until freeze. Selection is done by the creator (declare H_dec); no automated gate. Same commit varies about +/-4.75 pair-score points across reruns (noise band). Human references are top public leaderboard systems (Claude Code, GPT-5.6 Sol, MLEvolve, Kimi Writer), not paired controls under one executor. Dev-environment token cost excluded from efficiency metrics; downstream cost tracked (MLE-bench 29.3M-208.4M tokens, 19x spread). Compute: MLE-bench 1x A800-80GB, 34,200 s, 500-step cap; code benchmarks 7,200 s, 500-step cap. Author-run audit of every reported run against prohibited routes returned a null result.
deep_reads.key_results: Creation (Self-Eval, avg@3, Table 3): Opus 4.8 avg 67.8 (SWE-Pro 69.3%, TB 64.8%, MLE 32.9 medals, EQ-Bench3 84.6, BrowseComp 52.4%); Gemini 3.1 Pro 55.6; GPT-5.5 55.1; DeepSeek V4 Pro 45.2; Qwen 3.7 Max 44.0; Seed 2.0 Pro 22.8; human refs 86.2 (SWE-Pro 80.0, TB 88.8, MLE 24.0, EQ 83.7, BC 92.2); seed 0. Model harnesses match/exceed references on writing and ML, lag badly on code and search. Unified-Eval (fixed Gemini executor, Table 4): Opus SWE-Pro drops 69.3 -> 33.0 (one replica hard-coded a 120-step limit tuned to Opus; post-hoc clean 49.1); Opus avg 53.3, Gemini 55.6, Qwen 52.8, DeepSeek 48.8, GPT-5.5 44.8, Seed 29.8. Evolution (9 lineages, 73 official versions, 64 adjacent switches): visible feedback gains +3.0 to +13.9 pair-score vs held-out gains only +1.43 to +4.44 (mean +3.11) under self-runtime; under fixed Gemini executor only Opus improves (+2.70), Qwen -1.11, DeepSeek -2.38, GPT-5.5 -10.32. Of 64 switches: 8 regress on both benchmarks, 16 single-benchmark regression, 3 trade-off, 7 no change, 27 'gains' inside the +/-4.75 noise band; feedback and held-out directions agree on only 34/64 (53.1%); only 2/9 declared finals are held-out-optimal. Edit categories: execution 58, tools 37, lifecycle 17, context 16, state 4, standalone verifier 0. Artifact analysis (18 Code harnesses): 11/18 define a State class, 1/18 expose save, 1/18 checkpoint, 0 checkpoint events in 26,679 trajectories; 18/108 declared components never observed at runtime, all state/memory. 124/587 Writing features and 36 Data mechanisms are dead code. 441/2,325 Data tasks produced degenerate submissions no harness detected. Failure diagnosis weakest: trajectory interface called twice total; explicitly inspected failures 0.5%-40.2% of 189 feedback tasks. Self-test count Spearman rho 0.13-0.26 (n.s.) vs revision calls rho 0.57 (p<=.0005). Edit size does not predict score (Gemini +1,006 LOC, best TB score).
deep_reads.limitations: Author-admitted: four domains do not cover all deployments; human baselines uneven, leaderboard-derived, not paired controls (so Code/Search gap partly reflects stronger executor models like GPT-5.6); Unified-Eval reduces but cannot remove executor effects; evolution has one trajectory per creator-runtime cell so no uncertainty estimates; held-out evaluation exists only for SWE-Pro, not Terminal-Bench; dev environment fixed (whether an evolved harness can bootstrap further evolution left open); no claim that heuristic learning replaces training. My skepticism: code, seed, audit script, and held-out splits are 'will be released' with no GitHub repo as of 2026-09-14 (the org has only a blog repo), so nothing is reproducible yet; n=3 creations with collapsed replicas materially move means; the +/-4.75 noise band is about the same size as most reported evolution gains, so headline 'gains' are barely resolvable; creator model names are frontier-2026 closed models, limiting replication; the audit only checks cheating routes, not quality, and was run by the authors on their own runs; cost accounting excludes creator-side tokens, which is where most spend likely sits.
deep_reads.key_insight: Agents' visible-feedback self-selection of harness versions is close to a coin flip on held-out tasks (34/64 direction agreement, 2/9 finals optimal), most 'improvements' sit inside run-to-run noise, and no agent in 64 evolution steps ever built or touched a standalone verifier -- so the acceptance/verification layer must be supplied externally, must use withheld tasks plus repeated runs, and must check what a harness actually executes rather than what its code declares.
open_gaps: No code/seed/audit script/held-out splits released yet (stated as forthcoming); the 73 frozen harness versions and 26,679 trajectories are not public
Evolution is a single trajectory per cell with no seeds/replicates, so no confidence intervals on the +1.4 to +4.4 held-out gains
Held-out generalization measured on SWE-Pro only; Terminal-Bench, Data, Writing, Search evolution untested
No counterfactual: the paper never applies a held-out or repeated-run acceptance gate to the 73 versions to show how much better selection would have been
Audit checks only four cheating routes post hoc; no quality gate, no rollback protocol, no regression suite -- the project page recommends 'versioning and rollback' but does not test it
Whether an evolved harness can serve as the development environment for the next round (true closed loop) is explicitly deferred
Human references are not paired controls; a same-executor human-harness baseline is missing
Creator-side token/time cost of harness development is not reported
Dead-code and 'declared vs observed' analysis is done manually/statically by authors; no automated mechanism-coverage tool provided
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer:
This is the strongest empirical case to date that self-modifying agents need an external, harness-agnostic acceptance layer, and it supplies several reusable design elements.

What it proves: (1) Agent self-selection from visible feedback is unreliable -- feedback and held-out scores agree on 34/64 switches, 2/9 declared finals are held-out-optimal, and 27/64 'gains' are inside a +/-4.75 noise band. A gate cannot be a single-score comparison; it needs a withheld split plus replicate runs and a noise-aware decision rule. (2) Agents do not build their own verifier: 0 of 64 evolution edits touched a standalone verifier, 441/2,325 degenerate submissions went undetected, and validation was 'mostly syntactic'. The acceptance layer must be imposed, not expected to emerge. (3) Static inspection is insufficient: 18/108 declared mechanisms (all state/memory) never fired in 26,679 trajectories, 124/587 Writing features were dead code. Acceptance should require runtime-trace evidence that a claimed change actually executes (mechanism coverage), not code review alone. (4) Executor co-adaptation is real: Opus's harness fell from 69.3 to 33.0 under a fixed Gemini executor due to a hard-coded 120-step limit, and three of four fixed-executor evolution lineages regressed. A harness-agnostic gate should include a portability check under an alternate executor or perturbed runtime binding. (5) Revision-driven diagnosis (rho 0.57), not test count (rho 0.13-0.26), predicts quality -- the gate should reward read-failure-fix-reverify loops, e.g. by requiring failure-case inspection artifacts.

What to reuse directly: the score-path isolation principle (harness self-report is never a scoring input; credit only from ground-truth artifacts such as repo diff or final env state); the artifact contract (result.json, trajectory.jsonl, frozen source per version) enabling post-hoc audit; the four prohibited-route audit (instance hard-coding, ID-derived patches, hidden-test access, runtime-interface replacement); the probe-vs-official budget pattern (cheap 5-task probes to pre-screen, full paired eval to certify); and the six-module interface contract as a candidate harness-agnostic surface for instrumenting any harness.

What it leaves open: no acceptance mechanism is actually implemented or evaluated -- the withheld split is used to measure, not to gate; no rollback/regression protocol; no automated mechanism-coverage tooling; only SWE-Pro held-out; nothing released yet, so a reimplementation of the seed contract and audit is required to build on it. A natural first experiment for an acceptance layer is the counterfactual this paper skipped: replay their selection policy versus a noise-aware, held-out, fixed-executor gate over the 73 versions.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Constraint set on harnesses: no instance-specific hard-coding, no patches derived from task IDs, no consulting hidden tests/answers, no replacing the provider-neutral LLM interface, no abusing scorer internals. Enforcement: scoring path isolated from harness (self-reported status never scored; SWE-Pro credit only from real repo diff, Terminal-Bench only from final environment state); every run retains trajectory/result/metric artifacts alongside frozen source for post-hoc audit; authors audited all reported runs (null result). Held-out 630 SWE-Pro scores withheld from creators until freeze. Ethics statement warns generated harnesses should be treated as untrusted code because automated construction can amplify insecure tool use. Sandboxed execution with step (500) and time caps. No rollback, regression testing, or human-in-the-loop review inside the evolution loop.

deep_reads.name: EvoHarnessBench: Can Your Agents Keep Pace with an Evolving Harness?
deep_reads.mechanism: Takes two existing verifier-based agent benchmarks — EnterpriseOps-Gym (EOG: ServiceNow MCP gyms for calendar/CSM/drive/email/HR/ITSM/teams plus hybrids, each task backed by a seeded SQL database) and Agents' Last Exam (ALE) — and, without authoring new tasks, converts them into 17 multi-stage "harness streams" along three independent axes: tools (520), skills (42 hidden reference procedures extracted rule-based from system prompts), and specialist agents (62 entity-scoped bundles). Per axis, capabilities are ranked by how many tasks need them and partitioned into T=3-6 release buckets; stage t exposes the cumulative harness H_t = {c : r(c) <= t}, so core capabilities arrive first, the long tail later, and nothing is ever removed. Each task joins the cohort of the first stage at which all its oracle capabilities exist; each stage has an adaptation (train) split and an eval (test) split. By the final stage 89.0% of exposed tools (79.2-98.3% per stream), 66.7-81.1% of skills and 57.2-91.2% of agents are distractors for any given task. Two protocols: (1) Deployment — a fresh stateless agent is instantiated at each stage with H_t and run on the cumulative eval set, isolating the pure effect of harness growth; (2) Self-evolving adaptation — the agent keeps a persistent state z_t (memories, evolved prompts, learned skills, harness code, routing policies) that it may update on the cumulative adaptation split before each evaluation; artifacts are carried forward unconditionally. Results fill a stage x cohort accuracy matrix from which Pass, Score (partial credit), backward transfer (BWT: change on earlier cohorts as the harness grows) and forward transfer (FWT: performance on the newest cohort) are derived; negative BWT under Deployment is named "harness-induced forgetting". Systems: ReAct(GPT-5), Codex, Claude Code (Sonnet 4.6, appendix), AutoGen, DeLM. Adaptation methods: Raw Memory, ReasoningBank, MemToolAgent, G-Memory, LEGOMem (memory), GEPA (prompt evolution), Meta-Harness (harness-code optimization), Codex Memory. Each HF task record ships oracle_tools, cummulative_tools, MCP gym config with seed DB, and a verifiers[] list of database_state SQL checks (query + expected_value + comparison_type).
deep_reads.eval_loop: Outer loop: for each stream, iterate stages t=1..T (3-6). At each stage the harness H_t is expanded; the system is either re-instantiated fresh (Deployment) or allowed to update persistent state z_t using the cumulative adaptation split D_<=t,adapt (Self-evolving). It is then run on the cumulative eval split of all cohorts <= t. Task success is decided by deterministic final-state verifiers supplied by the seed benchmark (for EOG: SQL queries over the seeded gym database with expected values; ALE verifiers as in ALE), independent of which tools/skills/agents the agent actually used. Scores populate a stage x cohort matrix; metrics are Pass (fraction of tasks with verifier success), Score (mean verifier score), BWT (change on earlier cohorts as harness grows) and FWT (performance on the newly released cohort). Ablations swap the adaptation context (cumulative evolving pool vs task-specific capabilities vs final pool from stage 1) to measure the cost of evolution itself. Uncertainty is reported as +/- (0.0-4.5 points) but the number of seeds, temperature and model snapshot dates are not stated. Runs cost 20M-587M tokens and 2.8-97.7 hours per method per axis. The public leaderboard runs through a hosted SDK (wheel + API key from a demo login, ngrok-served eval service); no self-hosted runner is published.
deep_reads.limitations: (1) No benchmark code repository; evaluation runs through a hosted SDK/eval service behind an API key, so reproducibility depends on Salesforce keeping the service up, though the jsonl datasets (Apache-2.0) and seed gyms (EnterpriseOps-Gym, ALE) are open. (2) Seeds, temperature and noise floor are unreported; the tools (-5.3%) and skills (-4.0%) BWT effects are of the same magnitude as the +/- bounds, so only the agents-axis forgetting (-34.7%) is clearly outside noise; an independent critique (jjakimoto/research-issues #1364) argues the effect is retrieval/selection under catalog crowding rather than evolution per se, since context grows ~2.8x and distractor rates hit 98.3%. (3) Growth is monotonic-additive only: no capability replacement, deprecation, breaking API changes or removal. (4) Adaptation artifacts are carried across stages unconditionally; no held-out validation, rollback or gate is ever applied, so the paper cannot say whether gating would fix retention. (5) Skill-task association is a keyword heuristic that "does not guarantee that the matched skills are necessary, sufficient, or unique"; GPT-5 by default invokes almost none of the offered skills (GEPA 31%, Claude Code 15%, GPT-5.5 task-specific 82%), so skills-axis numbers partly measure willingness to read skill files. (6) ALE results are mostly at or below baseline and some agents-axis runs (G-Memory, DeLM on ALE) were not completed; Claude Code is only in the appendix. (7) "Codex Memory" is listed but never defined. (8) Whether self-evolving methods see verifier ground truth on the adaptation split is not made explicit, and overfitting/gaming of verifiers is not tested. (9) Extremely expensive to run (up to 587M tokens, ~98h per method), which limits use as a routine regression suite.
deep_reads.key_insight: Purely additive harness growth — same model, same tasks, only more tools/skills/agents exposed — is not regression-safe: previously passing tasks silently fail (BWT -5.3% tools, -4.0% skills, -34.7% agents), and the self-evolution methods that best preserve old competence are usually the worst at adopting new capabilities, so any acceptance signal for a harness mutation must measure retention (BWT) and adaptation (FWT) separately rather than a single pass rate.
open_gaps: No self-hostable benchmark runner; leaderboard depends on a hosted SDK/eval service behind an API key and ngrok URL
Seeds, temperature and noise floor unreported, so small BWT effects on tools/skills axes cannot be separated from run-to-run variance and a gate threshold cannot be calibrated from the paper
Only monotonic additive growth is modeled; capability replacement, retirement, deprecation and breaking changes are explicitly left to future work
Adaptation artifacts (memories, prompts, harness code) are carried forward unconditionally; no experiment tests a validate-then-accept or rollback gate on those artifacts
Retrieval/selection difficulty under crowded catalogs is confounded with genuine forgetting (no token-matched or synthetic-distractor control), per the external critique
Skill-task association is keyword-heuristic; skill engagement rates vary 0-82% by model, confounding skill-axis conclusions
Verifier overfitting/gaming by self-evolving systems on the adaptation split is not examined
ALE results are incomplete for several methods and mostly at or below baseline, so conclusions rest mainly on EnterpriseOps-Gym
Per-task verifiers only; no cross-task invariants, safety properties or side-effect checks are verified
Cost (20M-587M tokens, 2.8-97.7h per run) is prohibitive for use as a routine pre-merge regression suite; selective regression via oracle-capability impact analysis is untested
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer: Directly relevant as evidence and as a reusable measurement design, not as a gate itself. REUSE: (a) The stage x cohort retention matrix with BWT as the primary regression signal is the right shape for an acceptance test on any harness mutation: accept only if BWT on previously-passing cohorts >= -epsilon while FWT on the targeted cohort improves; a single aggregate pass rate hides the retention/adaptation tradeoff the paper documents (Gap 3). (b) The verifier design is harness-agnostic by construction: success is a deterministic check on final environment state (SQL over a seeded gym DB, expected_value + comparison_type) that runs identically whether the agent was Codex, Claude Code, ReAct, AutoGen or DeLM and regardless of which tools/skills/agents it invoked; the HF jsonl schema (verifiers[], oracle_tools, cummulative_tools, gym_servers_config) is a good template for a portable acceptance spec that an RSI loop can execute against any harness via MCP. (c) The Deployment protocol (fresh agent + mutated harness) is a clean control arm to separate the effect of a harness change from the effect of accumulated self-modification state; an acceptance layer should run both arms. (d) The oracle-capability annotations enable impact analysis: when a mutation touches capability c, re-run only cohorts whose oracle set includes c plus a sampled retention set, addressing the cost problem. (e) The delegation-drift finding (forgotten tasks stop calling sub-agents that were in previously successful traces) suggests a cheap pre-verifier: diff invocation sets of the mutated run against stored passing traces and flag drops. PROVES: "additive-only changes cannot regress" is false, so acceptance must re-run old passing tasks, not just new ones; self-evolution artifacts can be net-negative on retention even when they raise adaptation. LEAVES OPEN: the paper never applies any gate, rollback or held-out validation to carried artifacts, so it gives no evidence on whether gating restores retention; it has no noise floor, so epsilon cannot be set from it; it covers only additive growth (no replace/retire/breaking changes, which are the common RSI mutations); it does not test verifier gaming by systems that see verifier feedback during adaptation; and the external critique implies an acceptance suite should evaluate at the final crowded harness size, not only incrementally. Net: reuse the metric matrix, the state-based verifier spec and the two-arm protocol; treat the numbers as motivating evidence, not calibration.
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Salesforce AI Research (Zixuan Ke, Vaidehi Patil, Haizhou Shi as equal-contribution leads; Yang Li, Ye Liu, Sarath Shekkizhar, Anurag Koul, Jiayu Wang, Xuan Phi Nguyen, Semih Yavuz, Shafiq Joty) with UNC Chapel Hill (Mohit Bansal) and University of Wisconsin-Madison

deep_reads.key_results: Scale: 17 streams, 802 tasks (1,510 axis-specific examples), 520 tools, 42 skills, 62 agents, 3-6 stages; final-stage distractor rate 89.0% tools (79.2-98.3%), 66.7-81.1% skills, 57.2-91.2% agents. Deployment (fresh agent, Codex) pass: tools EOG 30.2+/-0.8 / ALE 12.2+/-0.7; skills EOG 18.9+/-0.6 / ALE 8.3+/-0.7; agents EOG 8.8+/-4.5 / ALE 4.2+/-2.0. Harness-induced forgetting (BWT under deployment): -5.3% tools, -4.0% skills, -34.7% agents (Codex on ALE); relative pass drops on earlier cohorts of 12.1% / 13.8% / 46.4%. Best self-evolving adapters (EOG): tools MemToolAgent 38.6+/-1.0 (+8.4 over 30.2, +27.8% rel.); skills GEPA 24.1+/-1.4 (+5.2, +27.5% rel.); agents Meta-Harness 18.5+/-2.5 and G-Memory 18.2+/-1.1 (+9.7 over 8.8, +110% rel.). On ALE most adapters are at or below deployment baseline (e.g. tools: Raw Memory 7.9, DeLM 6.2 vs 12.2). Skill invocation: GPT-5 default ~0%, GPT-5+GEPA 31%, Claude Code 15%, GPT-5.5 task-specific 82%. Skill-learning (App. I.2): batch teacher feedback best, joint 23.6 vs sequential 22.1.
