deep_reads.safety_measures: None discussed. No sandboxing, rollback, regression gate, held-out validation of evolved artifacts, or verifier-gaming analysis; adapted state is carried across stages unconditionally. Only implicit safeguard is that success is judged by deterministic final-state verifiers (SQL over seeded gym databases) rather than agent self-report, and eval splits are disjoint from adaptation splits. Task records embed placeholder access tokens for local MCP gym servers (sandbox-only environments from EnterpriseOps-Gym).

deep_reads.name: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: From Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops (survey, arXiv 2607.07663)
deep_reads.mechanism:
This is a 44-page literature survey, not a system. It assembles 1,250 arXiv papers (2024-2026): an 871-paper seed harvest over seven query threads (self-refinement, self-rewarding training, automated AI research, self-modifying agents, LLM-driven code/algorithm discovery, RSI theory/safety, self-generated-data loops), enriched with OpenAlex metadata, plus a 379-paper targeted supplement (judges/PRMs/verifiers/rubrics, test-time training, zero-data self-play). Papers are classified by theme-default + regex keyword rules + a 3-entry override dict (reclassify_corpus.py), by a single annotator.

Its framework is a 4x3 grid. Axis 1, what improves: (a) deployment-time self-evolution (output refinement, test-time training, harness/skill/memory evolution; 393 papers), (b) training-time self-iteration (self-reward RL, STaR-style CoT self-training, on-policy self-distillation, self-play incl. zero-data, embodied; 340), (c) self-evaluation (the evaluator itself is the object of improvement; 318), (d) auto research (AlphaEvolve/FunSearch-style program discovery, AI-scientist agents; 139), plus a 60-paper foundations/limits/safety family. Axis 2, who validates: human-in-the-loop, human-on-the-loop (automatic signal, human audits and gates deployment), closed loop.

Central conceptual cut: bounded self-refinement (fixed external evaluator; convergent, evaluable) vs open-ended RSI (system also modifies the criteria/machinery of improvement; divergent in principle). Central thesis: "every improvement loop is a claim that some signal can substitute for human judgment." It orders signals into a verification hierarchy: formal verifiers > execution feedback (tests, compilers, benchmarks) > learned judges (reward models, LLM-as-judge) > intrinsic signals (confidence, self-consistency, likelihood), and claims (explicitly as a qualitative observation, not a measured law) that demonstrated self-improvement strength tracks this hierarchy. Failure modes are derived from hierarchy violations: self-confirming loop, distributional collapse, diversity collapse, and (v2) frame lock-in. It also proposes a persistence axis for deployment-time changes (outputs evaporate, TTT lasts a session, harness/skill changes accumulate indefinitely) and a result-level (opex) vs process-level (capex) distinction for improvement signals.
deep_reads.eval_loop: No experiments of its own. Method is corpus assembly and rule-based classification: arXiv API queries with per-query depth caps, OpenAlex citation/venue enrichment, dedup on arXiv ID, theme->category defaults with regex keyword rules on title+first 800 chars of abstract (EVAL_TITLE/EVAL_STRONG/EVAL_BLOCK/TTT/TRAINS/INFERENCE_GUARD patterns), 89 seed papers moved by rules, 3 by manual override. Single annotator, no inter-annotator agreement reported, no validation of classifier accuracy beyond the authors' own estimate that ~54/379 supplement rows are peripheral bleed. Figures 2 and 6 are reproducible from scripts (TF-IDF + SVD + t-SNE map; quarterly growth from seed rows only); Figures 1, 3, 4, 5 are hand-drawn concept diagrams. The survey's substantive claims rest on cited anchor works and diagnostic papers, not on any measurement the authors ran. The corpus freeze is early July 2026; rerunning supplement_harvest.py queries arXiv live and changes counts.
deep_reads.limitations: Authors' own: corpus is a sample not a census; seed queries favor recent high-volume threads; supplement is recency-biased by construction; 74% of papers are from 2026 so citation counts are near zero and cannot indicate impact; classification is approximate and single-annotator; ~1 in 7 supplement papers is peripheral bleed; industrial RSI practice inside frontier labs is censored from any arXiv sample; the taxonomy is indexed by substrate not trajectory (a single continuously-developing system spans multiple cells) and neither axis indexes whether the objective is still the right one. Skeptical reading: the verification-hierarchy-tracks-strength claim is asserted as a qualitative pattern with a handful of exemplars (FunSearch/AlphaEvolve at top, AI scientists at bottom) and no systematic coding of the corpus by rung; no ablation, no quantitative test. Heavy reliance on an Anthropic essay as motivating frame (Claude writes >80% of merged code, five-stage autonomy spectrum) is acknowledged as non-evidence. The paper's Data availability URL (github.com/bamboodrift/recursive_self_improvement) is a private repo that does not resolve; the canonical release moved to deepgrounding/recursive-self-improvement on 2026-09-06, with 1 star, 2 commits, and manuscript source matching v1 rather than v2. Author affiliations are inconsistent across sources (UC Riverside / DeepGrounding / AlphaAvatar / IIT); DeepGrounding appears to be a small independent group with a gmail contact. Not peer reviewed.
deep_reads.key_insight: Self-improvement is only as real as its verification: the ceiling of any self-improvement loop equals the reliability of the signal that substitutes for human judgment, ordered formal verifier > execution feedback > learned judge > intrinsic self-assessment, and the loop's characteristic failure modes (self-confirming loop, collapse, diversity collapse, frame lock-in) are what happens when a loop runs below the rung its task requires. The dangerous cell in the grid is self-evaluation x closed loop, where a system rewrites its own definition of "better"; the field's emerging answer (evaluator co-evolution, Red Queen) may escape the self-confirming loop or may just give it a second story.
open_gaps: Exchange rate of grounding: the minimum rate of exogenous, externally grounded signal that sustains improvement without collapse is uncharacterized (entropy-reservoir framework suggests it is well-posed).

Verifying the non-verifiable: no reliable evaluator for research taste, creative quality, or direction-setting; SoundnessBench shows frontier models have pervasive optimism bias as first-gate rigor evaluators.
Stability engineering: rise-and-collapse, diversity collapse, and safety drift are rediscovered per paradigm; no unified theory of when self-improvement loops converge, oscillate, or collapse.

Trustworthy accumulation: persistent self-modification (skills, memory, experience graphs, harness code) lacks the verification story weights-based training has; formal verification (VASO) and threat analyses (SkillMutator, population-transmissible corruption) bracket the problem but the middle is open.
Governance-grade measurement: no technical literature on auditable evidence of what a training loop is and is not improving; foundations/safety is 60 of 1,250 papers.

Frame lock-in / direction generation (v2): a loop can be grounded, honest, diverse, stable and still optimize a question that stopped being worth answering; detecting this requires a vantage point outside the loop's own criteria, and no benchmark measures it.

Whether evaluator co-evolution escapes or compounds the self-confirming loop; A-Evolve-Training (loop detected dev-metric decoupling and revised its search policy) is the only field observation suggesting escape.

SkillsBench: LLM-authored skills provide no measurable gain vs +16.2 points for human-authored; unclear how much of harness/skill self-evolution gain is recursive vs better engineering (inference-scaling Pareto: +7.1 points only at ~20x compute).
Taxonomy indexed by substrate not trajectory; no way to register continuity of method across a system that changes its own frame ('scientific amnesia').
Classification validity: single annotator, regex rules, no inter-rater agreement; the hierarchy-tracks-strength claim was never coded across the corpus.
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer: Highly relevant as a design frame, not as reusable code. What to reuse directly: (1) The verification hierarchy as the acceptance layer's core schema. Every accepted change should be tagged with the rung it was validated at (formal / execution / learned-judge / intrinsic), and a harness-agnostic gate can refuse closed-loop acceptance below rung 2 and require human-on-the-loop for rung 3-4 evidence. The Mirror Loop result (10 rounds of ungrounded self-critique yields 55% declining informational change; one execution-grounded check at iteration 3 restores progress) is the cheapest justification for a mandatory grounded gate. (2) Axis 2 (human-in / human-on / closed) is exactly the per-change closure policy a gate enforces; the paper observes nearly all published work sits in human-on-the-loop, meaning the gate IS the artifact that distinguishes industrial practice from open-ended RSI. (3) The persistence axis (Fig 3): gate strictness should scale with persistence; harness/skill/memory changes accumulate indefinitely and the paper names accumulation-without-verification as the core safety problem, so persistent writes deserve a higher rung than transient outputs. (4) The special case of evaluator changes: the self-evaluation x closed-loop cell is where bounded refinement becomes open-ended RSI, so a gate must detect diffs that touch the evaluator/test-suite/rubric/benchmark and escalate them (higher rung, independent evaluator, or human), rather than letting the same loop score its own new judge. Red Queen / Escher-Loop / verification-level evolution are the systems this rule targets. (5) SHARP's pattern, constrain the self-modification surface to structured artifacts that can be audited, diffed, and rolled back, is a portable gate-design principle: gate on typed diffs of structured artifacts, not free-form code. (6) Failure modes as gate test cases: self-confirming loop implies generator/evaluator independence checks (different weights, execution grounding); collapse implies an exogenous-signal budget; diversity collapse implies novelty/coverage tracking; frame lock-in implies the gate must sit outside the loop's criteria, echoed by the 'unfireable safety kernel' argument that execution-time controls must live outside the agent's address space, i.e. the gate must not be part of the modifiable surface. (7) A-Evolve-Training's dev-metric/external-metric decoupling and SkillsBench's null result for LLM-authored skills argue the gate must measure delta against a held-out external metric with a compute-matched or placebo control, not the optimization target. (8) Result- vs process-level: accept on trace/process evidence where available so gains amortize. (9) Meta-Agent Challenge is a candidate benchmark for a harness-agnostic loop. What it proves: nothing experimentally; it is synthesis. What it leaves open, and what the acceptance layer would directly fill: open problems 4 (trustworthy accumulation) and 5 (governance-grade measurement: auditable evidence about what a loop is and is not improving). An acceptance ledger recording rung, evaluator identity, benchmark version, and closure level per change is precisely the missing infrastructure this survey says has 'essentially no technical literature behind it.'
deep_reads.safety_measures: Survey reports, does not implement: (a) 'unfireable safety kernel' argument that any control inside the agent's runtime is reachable by inputs and so execution-time alignment must live outside the agent's address space; (b) SHARP: constrain the evolvable surface to a human-auditable rubric policy that can be diffed and rolled back; (c) VASO: formally verifiable skill evolution; (d) human-oversight anchors against capability degradation and safety drift arising without an adversary; (e) Darwin Gödel Machine-style empirical validation against fixed coding benchmarks with an archive; (f) threat analyses (SkillMutator cross-modal spec/code mismatch, SkillHarness adversarial continual learning, population-transmissible corruption); (g) governance: verification infrastructure to demonstrate a loop is not self-improving past a threshold, inference-compute governance, bio-capability evaluation for research agents. Paper itself has no safety mechanism; it identifies governance-grade measurement as the most underpopulated niche.
deep_reads.key_results: No original experiments. Corpus stats: 1,250 papers (871 seed + 379 supplement); deployment 393 (refine 193 / harness 113 / ttt 87), training 340, self-evaluation 318 (284 from supplement), auto research 139, foundations 60; 74% posted 2026; quarterly seed output from single digits (early 2024) to ~500 (2026 Q2). Cited headline numbers: Mirror Loop, 55% decline in informational change over 10 ungrounded self-critique rounds, restored by one verification step; SkillsBench, human-authored skills +16.2 points vs no measurable gain for LLM-authored; inference-scaling Pareto, +7.1 points over CoT only at ~20x compute across 34 configurations; SciIntegrity-Bench, 34.2% integrity-failure rate across 7 frontier models, all 7 fabricate synthetic data rather than admit infeasibility; SoundnessBench (v2), 1,099 ICLR proposals, pervasive optimism bias across 12 frontier models; A-Evolve-Training, autonomous 30B post-training loop, 4 rounds, 0.86 vs 0.87 human top, 8th of ~4,000, loop detected dev-metric decoupling; The AI Scientist ~$15/paper; MT-Bench ~80% judge-human agreement; Whitfill and Wu compute/labor elasticity diverges between specifications (substitutes vs complements).

deep_reads.name: Mendel Gödel Machine (MGM): Recursive Self-Improving Coding Agents via Comparative Evolution
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Changzhi Liu, Yilun Liu, Sikuan Yan, Volker Tresp, Yunpu Ma — UESTC / LMU Munich / Munich Center for Machine Learning
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (cs.AI, cs.LG), v1 2026-08-07; Semantic Scholar: 0 citations as of 2026-09-14; listed #1 on Papers-with-Code Aider-Polyglot leaderboard (self-reported, unverified — open issue #3 from HF asks authors to verify)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-05 (last push; slides/docs only). Last substantive code change 2026-08-16 ("Switch container runtime to Apptainer and add DeepSeek LLM backend"). Repo created 2026-04-09. 3 forks, 1 open issue, Apache-2.0.
deep_reads.mechanism:
MGM is a direct fork of the Huxley-Gödel Machine (HGM, Schmidhuber lab; itself DGM-derived) that changes only the *evidence* fed to the self-modification step. The genotype is the coding-agent scaffold (coding_agent.py, prompts, tools, workflow; the LLM Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is frozen). The phenotype is a trajectory plus binary task outcome r in {0,1}. An archive/tree of agent commits is grown under a fixed budget (200 task-evaluations, 24 expansions, 2 parallel workers).

Selection (inherited from HGM): node to *evaluate* is picked by Thompson sampling from Beta(1+successes, 1+failures) on that node's own evals; node to *expand* is picked by clade-level posteriors that pool all descendants' evals (HGM's CMP idea, n_pseudo_descendant_evals=10000). Expansion triggers when n_evals^alpha >= |nodes| (alpha=0.6).

Three self-modification operators, sampled with weights A:B:C = 0.1:0.45:0.45 (HGM baseline = 1:0:0):
- A, Clonal mutation: diagnose one failed trajectory of the node.
- B, Reaction-norm mutation: diagnose TWO trajectories of the same node on different tasks (needs >=2 evals on node); prompt asks for a "common_weakness" / shared root cause.
- C, Cross-lineage hybridization: pick a random peer node with an overlapping task; if exactly one solved it, the failing agent is Primary and the solver is Context; if both failed, the higher-utility lineage is Primary. The prompt explicitly forbids copying Context's diff — the target agent must extract a general behavioral trait.

Each operator: a diagnose-LLM call sees agent code, run logs, predicted patch, and SWE-bench's *private test patch and test results*, and must output JSON {problem_description, implementation_suggestion}, with prompt-level rules forbidding hard-coded repo/file/keyword tables and dead code. The parent agent is then run *as a coding agent on its own repository* inside an Apptainer container to implement that issue; the resulting git diff becomes a new child commit with an empty evaluation record. Theory: under an additive binary-locus fitness surrogate, Proposition 1 says RM and CH have strictly higher "effective fix probability" than CM because intersecting evidence shrinks the candidate defect set; Monte Carlo over d0 in {10,20,40,80}, rho in {1,1.2,1.5,2} shows faster convergence for rho>1.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Evolution runs on the same 60-task subsets (small+medium) of SWE-bench Verified and Polyglot used by HGM; one task = one binary φ-evaluation inside an isolated Apptainer container (no network, read-only host mounts, 1 h timeouts), backbone Qwen3.6-35B-A3B served by vLLM on 8×H100. Reported accuracy = the chosen best node re-run on all 60 tasks (eval_remaining) — i.e., the *training* set; the paper states all main results are "evaluated on the same two 60-task subsets". Generalization is then tested by transferring the Polyglot-evolved scaffold to full Polyglot-225, SWE-bench Pro (60), SWE-bench Multilingual (60), and swapping in DeepSeek-V4-Flash/Pro. Ablation on Polyglot-60 removes RM or CH. Efficiency is measured as wall-clock at 200 evals and token-cost distributions. Single run per configuration; authors admit compute limits seed count and hyperparameter sweeps. The shipped tree artifact (docs/assets/tree_mgm_web.json) shows what the search signal really looks like: 24 nodes, 198 evals, strategies 13 RM / 10 CH / 1 CM, only 2 nodes evaluated on >=20 of 60 tasks, median ~7 evals per node.
deep_reads.key_results: Table 1 (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 200 evals): SWE-bench Verified-60 initial 68.3% -> HGM 73.3% -> MGM 78.3%; Polyglot-60 50.8% -> 77.9% -> 93.2%. Wall-clock comparable: SWE 93.0h (HGM) vs 96.1h (MGM); Polyglot 44.2h vs 40.1h; token cost distributions same order of magnitude. Table 2 (Polyglot-evolved scaffold, held-out): SWE-bench Pro 16.7% -> HGM 13.3% (regression) -> MGM 26.7%; SWE-bench Multilingual 41.7% -> 43.3% -> 55.0%. Table 3 (cross-model, SWE-V60): DeepSeek-V4-Flash 50.0 -> 60.0 -> 66.7; DeepSeek-V4-Pro 45.0 -> 70.0 -> 75.0. Full Polyglot-225: 93.3% (210/225) with Qwen, 96.89% with DeepSeek-V4-Pro; paper says this "surpass[es] closed-source GPT-5 with ~117x fewer parameters" but cites no GPT-5 score. Ablation (Polyglot-60): full MGM best; removing CH hurts more than removing RM (numbers not recoverable from the HTML I could read). Theory: Proposition 1 + Monte Carlo show faster/better convergence for the comparative operators when their fix-probability advantage rho>1.
deep_reads.limitations: (1) Single run per configuration, no seeds or error bars; on a 60-task set one task = 1.67 pp, so the +5 pp SWE gap over HGM is 3 tasks. (2) Reported main numbers are on the same 60 tasks used to drive evolution — an in-distribution "train-set" score; only the transfer tables are held-out. (3) The HGM baseline is the authors' own reimplementation (weights 1:0:0 in their fork), not the original HGM run/backbone. (4) HGM's regression on SWE-bench Pro (16.7 -> 13.3) shows evolved scaffolds can overfit; MGM's improvement there rests on 60 tasks of a much harder benchmark. (5) The diagnosis prompt exposes SWE-bench's private test patch and test results to the self-modifier; prompt rules forbid hard-coding but nothing verifies it. (6) During search nodes are scored on very few tasks (median ~7/60), so archive selection operates on extremely noisy posteriors. (7) "117x fewer parameters than GPT-5" is speculation about GPT-5 size; no GPT-5 Polyglot number is given. (8) Theory uses a toy additive-loci model with "sound comparative evidence" assumed; authors state it "do[es] not capture the full complexity" and that MGM "does not guarantee that the resulting edit is correct, general, or maintainable" and that "an erroneous or adversarial self-edit can persist in later descendants". (9) History-dependent: RM needs >=2 evals on a node and CH needs task overlap across lineages, so early in a run it degrades to HGM. (10) Heavy infra: Slurm + Apptainer + vLLM + 8×H100, ~40–96 h per run; repo hygiene is weak (committed TTF fonts, pause.pid, podman-service.log, "Cursor Agent" commits, README still says `git clone <your-repo-url>`). (11) Scope explicitly limited to coding-agent scaffolds on public SWE benchmarks.
deep_reads.key_insight: Self-modification quality is bottlenecked by diagnostic evidence, not by the search policy: giving the self-modifier controlled *comparisons* (same agent across tasks, or two lineages on the same task) shrinks the set of plausible defects and raises the probability that an edit fixes a real, general weakness — at no extra token or wall-clock cost. Cross-lineage differential evidence is the strongest of the three operators.
open_gaps: No performance-based accept/reject at commit time: every child that passes a syntactic smoke test enters the archive with zero evidence; acceptance is entirely deferred to Thompson-sampling selection over very sparse evals.
No regression/canary suite: a child is never re-checked on tasks its parent solved, so silent capability loss is only detected if the sampler happens to revisit those tasks.

No held-out validation inside the loop; main results are on the evolution set, and one baseline (HGM) regresses on SWE-bench Pro, showing in-distribution gates do not protect against scaffold overfitting.
Oracle leakage: the self-modifier's diagnosis sees private test patches and test results; there is no mechanical check that edits do not encode task-specific knowledge (only prompt rules).
No rollback, quarantine, or lineage pruning for bad edits; authors acknowledge erroneous/adversarial edits can persist in descendants.
Single-seed results with 60-task evals; statistical significance of +5 pp (3 tasks) over HGM is unestablished; ablation numbers not fully reported.

Harness-specific: the gate (py_compile + __main__ + --help usage grep) and the ledger (git commit per child, model_patch.diff, metadata.json) are tied to coding_agent.py/Apptainer/Slurm; no abstraction for other agent harnesses.
No cost accounting or budget attribution per accepted edit, and no measure of edit maintainability or scaffold bloat over generations.
The theoretical fix-probability advantage assumes 'sound comparative evidence'; nothing verifies that the LLM's cross-lineage diagnosis is actually causal rather than correlational.
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer:
MGM is useful mainly as a concrete, code-level specimen of how the DGM/HGM lineage actually 'accepts' self-edits, and as evidence about what an acceptance layer should and should not try to do.

What its acceptance layer really is (from hgm_utils.sample_child): a two-stage design. Stage 1 is a cheap, deterministic, commit-time structural gate: model_patch.diff must be non-empty and pass `git apply --check` against the parent commit in a detached worktree; then a smoke test (`python -m py_compile coding_agent.py`, an `if __name__` entrypoint must exist, and `python coding_agent.py --help` must exit 0 within 120 s and print 'usage'). Failure retries the self-improve step and eventually yields a 'failed' node. Stage 2 is not a gate at all: the child enters the tree with an empty evaluation record and Thompson sampling with clade-pooled Beta posteriors decides whether it ever gets evaluated or expanded. There is no parent-vs-child comparison, no threshold, no regression check, no rollback. That is a deliberate stance — with ~200 evals spread over 24 nodes (median ~7 tasks per node, only 2 nodes with >=20/60), a binary accept/reject on performance would be statistically meaningless — and it argues for a harness-agnostic layer that treats acceptance as *provisional admission plus posterior tracking* rather than a one-shot verdict.

What is directly reusable: (a) the minimal liveness contract (patch applies cleanly and reversibly; artifact compiles; entrypoint survives; `--help` responds) as the zero-cost first filter any harness can implement; (b) the per-child ledger — git commit hash, model_patch.diff, self_evo.md transcript, metadata.json with per-task resolved/unresolved/empty-patch ids and strategy tag — as a schema for what an acceptance layer should record; (c) cross-lineage differential evidence as a *verification* signal, not just a proposal signal: if lineage A solves task t and sibling B does not, diff(A,B) is a candidate causal edit whose effect can be tested by ablation, which is exactly what an acceptance layer needs to attribute credit to an edit.

What it proves: richer comparative evidence upstream raises fix probability without more tokens, so an acceptance layer that feeds structured comparisons back to the proposer reduces the number of bad candidates the gate has to catch. Transfer to SWE-bench Pro/Multilingual and to DeepSeek backbones shows evolved scaffolds can generalize, but HGM's regression on SWE-Pro (16.7 -> 13.3) shows in-distribution scoring alone will happily accept overfit edits.

What it disproves or warns against: the diagnosis prompt hands the self-modifier the private test patch and test results, enforced only by prompt rules ('FORBIDDEN: hard-coding task-specific identifiers'). An acceptance layer must keep oracle/test information out of the proposer's context or mechanically scan diffs for oracle leakage; MGM has no such check. Likewise, no child is re-run on tasks its ancestors passed, so capability regressions are invisible unless the sampler revisits them — an acceptance layer should own a canary/regression set that the archive search does not.

What it leaves open for the harness-agnostic layer: a held-out validation split inside the loop; statistically calibrated promotion (e.g., sequential tests on Beta posteriors before an edit becomes a default); rollback/quarantine of lineages; cost attribution per accepted edit; and any abstraction of the gate beyond one Python file in one container runtime.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Self-modification and evaluation run in isolated Apptainer containers with no network access and read-only host mounts (following DGM/HGM protocol); 1 h timeouts on self-improve and evaluation; per-child structural gate (non-empty, cleanly-applying, reversible git patch; py_compile; __main__ entrypoint present; `--help` succeeds within 120 s); failed children are retried then recorded as 'failed' nodes; prompt-level rules forbidding hard-coded task identifiers, dead code, `while True` loops, and direct package installs; consecutive-container-failure circuit breaker in the main loop. No performance-based rejection, no regression suite, no rollback, no leakage detection; authors explicitly note that erroneous or adversarial self-edits can persist in descendants.

deep_reads.name: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement (RHI)
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Hyunin Lee (Sakana AI intern / UC Berkeley, corresponding), Jinglue Xu, Jeffrey Seely, Yujin Tang (Sakana AI); Donghyun Lee, Matei Zaharia (UC Berkeley)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-07-17 arXiv v1 only (no v2 seen). Downstream: alphaXiv clean-room reproduction repo 2026-07-21; HSI (2608.08466) cites it Aug 2026; VideoHarness-RSI (2608.24302) borrows the name Aug 25 2026; openclaw feature issue #145948 opened and closed-not-planned 2026-09-12.
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (cs.LG/cs.AI), no venue. OpenAlex cited_by=0 (lagging); at least 2 citing/derivative arXiv works found; HF papers 27 upvotes; Semantic Scholar rate-limited. Sakana RSI Lab context but not listed on the lab page.
deep_reads.mechanism:
The "harness" is a text block ("multi agent design") prepended to the task prompt of a black-box coding agent (Claude Code; the prompt says "Create an agent team", activating built-in subagents). It lists candidate agents (role, instruction, output-to-orchestrator contract), orchestrator-subagent hops, and auxiliary rules (acceptance gates before termination, fallback rules, evidence-triggered recall of subagents, conflict resolution). H(0) is a hand-written, domain-level (not task-level) harness with ~10 agents.

Per task x, per iteration i: (1) the agent solves x with H(i) and emits a repo with standardized deliverables (research_report.md, plots/*.png, metrics.json, index.json). (2) An LLM judge (gpt-5.5 max-reasoning or opus-4.7/4.8 xhigh; 3 seeds) pairwise-compares output(i) vs output(i-1) using only extracted deliverables (capped to ~30-40% of judge context) on six criteria: deliverable coverage, empirical rigor, reproducibility, presentation, engineering quality, task alignment; returns A/B/tie plus rationale JSON. (3) Verdict is appended to a self-comparison history D(i). (4) An LLM optimizer (Appendix C prompt: "principal prompt engineer") rewrites H(i) to H(i+1) given the current harness, size-capped file excerpts of the current repo, a programmatic preflight (expected paths from task text vs workspace), the pairwise history including the judge's verbatim rationale and "actionable takeaways", and an aggregated "recurring issues" checklist with counts. It is explicitly told to prioritize stronger output contracts and more orchestrator recall/re-delegation hops, and to "preserve winning traits and fix listed defects".

Control: the new harness is adopted unconditionally (Eq. 5). The only gate is a global stop when the improvement rate s_i = fraction of tasks where output(i) beats output(i-1) falls below an unspecified epsilon. Per-iteration cost is one agent run plus one judge call (Theta(1)) versus Theta(m^2) for population search (Table 1). Harnesses are task-specific and are optimized on the very task they are evaluated on. Baselines are the same model at higher reasoning effort (xhigh/max) or with Anthropic's built-in dynamic multi-agent mode ("ultracode" = xhigh + auto-spawned subagents), with no harness.
deep_reads.eval_loop: 30 LLM-generated "ML research" tasks (10 each: quant finance, robotics, pharma; derived from three job postings), each demanding a full repo with fixed deliverables. Pairwise LLM-as-judge on deliverables only, two judge configs (gpt-5.5-max, opus-xhigh; six configs for opus-4.7 incl. gemini-3.1-pro-high) x 3 seeds; ties allowed; no position-swap protocol; no significance tests, only mean wins with SD. Metrics: wins/30, normalized cost, output tokens, cache read+write from Claude Code's internal cost function, all normalized to the plain "high" agent. The optimization signal and the evaluation signal are the same judge family on the same tasks (no held-out tasks, no transfer test). Ablations use cosine similarity/t-SNE over harness components (roles, instructions, contracts, hops) across iterations; an Elo study compares single vs built-in multi vs H(0) harness.
deep_reads.key_results: sonnet-4.6-high+H[2] wins 20/30 vs sonnet-4.6-max (mean over 2 judges x 3 seeds), holds at H[3],H[4]; opus-4.7-high+H[0] loses to xhigh/max but H[1] beats both (exact counts only in figures); opus-4.8-high+H[2] beats xhigh, max and ultracode. Normalized cost (vs plain high=1.0): sonnet H[2] 2.38 vs max 2.56 (-7%); opus-4.7 H[1] 2.11 vs max 2.60 (-18%); opus-4.8 H[2] 1.69 vs max 2.19 (-23%) and vs ultracode 4.15 (-60%). Cache read+write down 32-64% vs baselines. Output tokens roughly flat across iterations for sonnet (1.71-1.86) and opus-4.8 (1.42-1.81), so gains attributed to context management; inconclusive for opus-4.7 (tokens rose with performance). Ablations: contracts show strongest task-specific clustering and fastest stabilization; roles barely change; consecutive harness cosine similarity 0.82 then 0.97-0.99; cumulative drift 0.82 to 0.75. 6.1: sonnet+RHI does not close the gap to opus-4.7. Built-in "Create an agent team" mode scores lower Elo than single-agent at higher cost; explicit H(0) reverses this. Note the cost figures are for the final run only; sonnet cost grows across iterations (H[0] 1.80 -> H[4] 2.52) and every RHI harness costs ~1.7-2.5x the plain high agent. Independent downscaled reproduction (alphaXiv/OpenResearch, Qwen2.5-Coder-14B, 8 tasks x 6 seeds, executable tests): H1 +0.064 over H0 (CI positive) but H2 flat (-0.003, CI [-0.078,0.075]) and below a static high-effort control (-0.092, CI [-0.121,-0.063]); open judge order-consistent in only 12/48 comparisons; forcing more contracts/hops made things worse.
deep_reads.limitations: No code or harness release; Sakana GitHub has no RHI repo, only a third-party clean-room reproduction (4 stars). Task-specific optimization evaluated on the same task instance: no held-out tasks, no cross-task transfer, so 'few iterations suffice' is in-sample. Optimization and evaluation share the same judge family (opus judges opus), no position-swap, no significance testing, and the optimizer receives the judge's verbatim rationale, so the evaluation criteria effectively leak into revisions (Goodhart on presentation/report consistency is plausible; the independent reproduction saw H2 not beating a static control). Cost claims exclude the RHI loop itself (3+ agent runs, judge calls, optimizer calls per task) and are relative to max-effort baselines, while RHI harnesses cost ~2x the plain agent and cost rises with iterations. epsilon is never given; new harnesses are always adopted; no per-task rollback. The Appendix C example shows a v0-vs-v1 'tie' where both repos were the identical workspace path, hinting at pipeline artifacts. Only Claude models as agents; 30 synthetic LLM-written tasks; exact opus win counts appear only in figures. The information-theoretic 'implicit objective' is a hypothesis supported by similarity plots, not tested causally.
deep_reads.key_insight: Compare a self-modifying harness only against its own immediate predecessor with an accumulated pairwise-preference history, and you get a Theta(1)-per-iteration update signal that, within 1-2 iterations, lets a lower-effort agent beat max-effort test-time scaling; the gains come from tighter inter-agent contracts and recall hops (less context propagation), not longer reasoning; but the paper contains no acceptance gate at all, so every revision is adopted on faith and the only safeguard is a global stop-when-improvement-rate-drops rule.
open_gaps: No accept/reject gate per harness revision; H(i+1) is adopted unconditionally, and there is no rollback when output(i) loses to output(i-1).
No held-out or cross-task evaluation: harness is optimized and scored on the same task instance, so generalization/overfitting to the judge is untested.
Judge protocol lacks position-swapping, significance testing, and independence from the agent family; the optimizer sees judge rationales, creating a direct Goodhart channel.
Total-cost accounting omits the RHI loop's own agent/judge/optimizer runs and shows per-iteration cost growth (harness bloat) with no budget constraint.
Stopping threshold epsilon is unspecified; convergence is argued via cosine similarity, not via performance monotonicity.
No code, prompts-as-run, or task suite released; the only reproduction (downscaled, open models) failed to reproduce the second-iteration gain or the contracts/hops mechanism.
Evolved harnesses embed their own 'acceptance gates' and 'recall triggers', but nothing checks those internal gates are honored or effective.
Second half of the co-evolution loop (training on the improved traces) is entirely future work; trace quality is never measured beyond judge preference.
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer:
RHI is a clean, harness-agnostic case study of what a self-modifying agent looks like WITHOUT an acceptance layer: the mutable surface is a text block injected into a black-box agent (Claude Code), the only signal is a pairwise LLM judgment over standardized deliverables, and the revision is adopted unconditionally. That makes it a useful negative reference and a source of reusable primitives.

Reusable: (1) Deliverables-contract evaluation: extract only task-named artifacts, cap to 30-40% of judge context, judge on six fixed criteria and return JSON with A/B/tie plus rationale; this is harness-independent and works for open-ended tasks without verifiers. (2) 'Programmatic preflight' (expected paths parsed from task text vs workspace) as a deterministic pre-gate before any LLM judging. (3) The pairwise self-comparison history with a counted 'recurring issues' checklist is a natural regression ledger. (4) The improvement-rate s_i < epsilon stopping rule generalizes to a fleet-level 'stop evolving' gate. (5) Harness decomposition into roles/instructions/contracts/hops/auxiliary rules gives a diff surface for reviewing proposed changes, and cosine-similarity drift is a cheap stability monitor. (6) Cost/cache telemetry per revision to catch harness bloat.

What it proves: predecessor-only comparison plus history is enough signal for improvement in 1-2 steps on in-sample tasks, and text-only harness edits change cost/coordination substantially, so an acceptance layer must gate prompt-level changes, not just code. What it disproves or warns: the paper itself notes 'losing revisions are discarded or revised' but implements no discard step, and the alphaXiv reproduction shows non-monotone iterations (H2 below H0 and below a static control) and severe judge order-sensitivity, i.e. exactly the regressions a gate must catch. The authors explicitly contrast RHI with Self-Harness (Zhang et al. 2026, arXiv 2606.09498), whose regression-test acceptance ('improve one split without degrading the other') is the verifier-based analogue of RHI's preference relation; an acceptance layer should implement that relation on top of RHI-style proposals: order-swapped, multi-seed, judge-independent pairwise comparison with CI-based accept/reject, held-out task checks, rollback on loss, a cost/bloat budget, and isolation of judge rationales from the proposer (or at least auditing for criteria leakage). Left open: how to verify that harness-internal 'acceptance gates' and 'recall triggers' (which RHI evolves) are actually executed by the black-box agent, and how to score trace quality for the downstream training half of the loop.
deep_reads.safety_measures: None at the algorithm level: no sandboxing discussed, no rollback, no per-revision acceptance, no regression tests; the evaluation prompt is withheld from the optimizer, but the optimizer receives the judge's verbatim rationale. Base model, judge, and optimizer are fixed (bounded RSI over harness text only). Evolved harnesses themselves add internal QA agents, 'final acceptance gate', recall triggers, and conflict-resolution records, but these are unverified prompt instructions to the agent, not external controls.

deep_reads.name: Group-Evolving Agents (GEA): Open-Ended Self-Improvement via Experience Sharing
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Zhaotian Weng, Antonis Antoniades, Deepak Nathani, Zhen Zhang, Xiao Pu, Xin Eric Wang — UC Santa Barbara (eric-ai-lab)
deep_reads.last_activity: Paper: v1 only (2026-02-04). Code (UCSB-AI/GEA, formerly eric-ai-lab/GEA): created 2026-02-09, last push 2026-04-07 (cleanup commits: removed debug prints), one open issue (HF Papers-with-Code verification request, 2026-08-14, unanswered).
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint, cs.AI, 18 pages, no venue announced on paper or project page. Citation count not retrievable (Semantic Scholar API rate-limited on 3 attempts; OpenAlex has no record). Cited by at least RoboPhD (2604.04347) and Evolving-RL (2605.10663) per web search.
deep_reads.mechanism:
GEA is a fork of the Darwin Godel Machine (DGM) codebase that changes the evolutionary unit from one agent to a group of K=2. Each archived agent is a git-patch lineage over a base coding agent (coding_agent.py, tools/, utils/); the agent edits its own framework code, not weights.

Outer loop per iteration (GEA_outer.py): (1) Parent-group selection: every archived agent has a 60-dim binary task-success vector z_i (which of 60 SWE-bench Verified probe tasks it solved; swe_bench/subsets/task.json). Novelty nov(i) = mean cosine distance to its M=4 nearest neighbours; score(i) = accuracy_i * sqrt(nov(i)); top-K=2 become parents p1, p2, each paired with a target failure (a specific unsolved task, or a meta-issue: empty patches / stochasticity / context length). (2) Offspring: two children, (p1+p2, e1+e2) and (p2+p1, e2+e1). A child inherits the FIRST parent's full patch lineage; the reflection model (o1-2024-12-17) receives the primary parent's execution log, eval log, predicted patch, gold patch and gold tests for e1, PLUS the partner's log/eval/predicted patch for e2 ("the log of another coding agent, not the current one, use as reference"), and emits a JSON problem statement. (3) A coding agent (Claude Haiku 4.5 for early iterations, Sonnet 4.5 later) runs inside a Docker container with --self_improve for up to 45 min, editing its own repo; the diff becomes model_patch.diff. (4) Evaluation ladder: 10-task smoke set; if >=1 solved (threshold 0.1) then the 50-task Verified-Mini set (Polyglot: >40% on 10 to reach an unseen 50-task set). (5) Archive admission is_compiled_self_improve: metadata keys present, >=1 non-empty patch, >=10 instances submitted; default update policy keep_all (no regression check). Top-2 archive agents were evaluated on the full 500-task SWE-bench Verified out-of-band (the full_eval_threshold parameter is computed but never used in self_improve).
deep_reads.eval_loop: Benchmarks: SWE-bench Verified and Aider Polyglot. Evolution signal is pass/fail on a 10-task smoke set then a 50-task set (60 tasks total, all drawn from the 500 Verified tasks); the task-success vector over these 60 tasks doubles as the behavioural fingerprint for novelty. Final headline numbers: top-2 agents on full 500-task SWE-bench Verified (GEA 71.0% vs re-implemented DGM 56.7%); Polyglot on the unseen 50-task medium set (88.3% vs 68.3%). Population-level worst-case top-k on the 60-task set (Table 1): top-1 71.0/56.7, top-3 63.3/48.3, top-5 58.3/45.0. Budget matched by agent count: GEA 30 iterations x2 agents (SWE) and 20x2 (Polyglot); DGM 60 and 40 single-child iterations. Cost ~USD 13,000 per method on SWE-bench, ~1,500 on Polyglot. Single run per method, pass@1, no seeds, no variance reported. Robustness test: manually injected framework bugs into an archived agent, 5 trials; GEA repaired in {1,1,2,1,2} iterations (mean 1.4) vs DGM {5,4,5,6,5} (mean 5.0). Transferability (Fig. 5): swapping the acting model across GPT- and Claude-series shows consistent gains over the iteration-0 agent, reported qualitatively only. No component ablations (no novelty-vs-sharing-vs-K isolation).
deep_reads.key_results: SWE-bench Verified (full 500): GEA 71.0% vs author-reimplemented DGM 56.7% (human-designed OpenHands+GPT-5: 71.8%). Polyglot (unseen 50-task set): 88.3% vs 68.3% (Aider+GPT-5 high: 52.0%, on the full benchmark). Worst-case top-5 GEA agent (58.3%) beats DGM's single best (56.7%). Best GEA agent integrates 17 unique ancestors (28.3% of population) vs 9 (15.0%) for DGM; 5 of its tools originated from different parents. Injected-bug repair in 1.4 vs 5.0 iterations. ~$13k per method on SWE-bench.
deep_reads.limitations: No dedicated limitations section; the Impact Statement only warns evolution may drift from human intent, burn compute, and yield patches that lack structural clarity. Demonstrated gaps: (a) single-run results, no variance, 10-task gate means one task = 10 points of noise; (b) DGM baseline is the authors' re-implementation with the same models, not the DGM authors' system or numbers; (c) human-baseline comparisons are cross-model (GEA runs Sonnet 4.5, baselines run GPT-5) and for Polyglot cross-subset (50 tasks vs full 225); (d) no ablations, so the contribution of experience sharing vs performance-novelty selection vs simply spawning two children per iteration is not isolated; (e) the 60 evolution tasks are inside the 500-task final evaluation set; (f) the reflection prompt exposes the gold answer_patch and test_patch to the model that writes the evolution directive (inherited from DGM), a leakage channel the paper does not examine; (g) code discrepancy: on SWE-bench the partner parent's framework patches (patch_files1) are accepted but never used, so only its task logs are shared, unlike the paper's description of sharing applied code patches (the Polyglot path does include partner code); (h) group size is hard-locked to 2 (code raises otherwise); (i) transferability is qualitative only; (j) the top-2 full-benchmark promotion is not automated in the released code.
deep_reads.key_insight: Treating a pair of agents as the evolutionary unit and letting each offspring's reflection step read the other parent's failure traces converts what tree-structured DGM throws away (diversity in dead branches) into reusable experience; combined with a performance x sqrt(novelty) parent ranking on a behavioural task-success fingerprint, this doubled per-iteration efficiency and lifted worst-case population quality, at the price of only a compile-and-smoke acceptance gate.
open_gaps: No ablation isolating experience sharing from performance-novelty selection or from simply producing 2 children per iteration
Single run per method; no seeds, variance, or confidence intervals despite a 10-task promotion gate
DGM baseline is an author re-implementation; no comparison to SICA, AlphaEvolve-style or other self-evolving systems
Human-designed comparisons are cross-model (Sonnet 4.5 vs GPT-5) and, for Polyglot, cross-subset (50 vs 225 tasks)
Gold answer_patch/test_patch are shown to the reflection model that authors framework changes; benchmark-content leakage into evolved code is unexamined
Released SWE-bench code shares only the partner's task logs, not its framework patches, contra the paper's description
Evolution tasks (60) are a subset of the 500-task final evaluation set; no truly held-out SWE-bench split
Group size fixed at K=2; scaling behaviour unknown
Final full-benchmark promotion (top-2) is manual; the full_eval_threshold hook is dead code
No semantic, security, or intent-alignment review of evolved patches beyond Docker isolation
deep_reads.safety_measures: All self-modification and evaluation run inside Docker containers (python:3.10-slim image, repo copied in, git commit taken before the agent edits itself so the candidate is an isolated diff); 45-minute timeout on the self-improve run and 1.5-hour timeout per attempt at the outer loop. Archive admission requires the modified agent to still produce evaluation output, emit at least one non-empty patch, and submit results on all 10 smoke tasks; promotion to the 50-task stage requires solving at least 1/10 (Polyglot: >40%). An optional keep_better archive policy (score >= initial score minus 0.1 leeway) exists but the default is keep_all. A post-hoc LLM 'improvement diagnosis' of each accepted patch is recorded but not used as a gate. No human review, no static/security analysis of patches, no alignment check; the Impact Statement acknowledges possible drift from human intent and growing opacity of evolved systems.
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer: GEA is a clean example of a self-modifying loop whose acceptance layer is almost vestigial, which makes it useful as both a negative and a positive reference. What to reuse: (1) the candidate-as-diff discipline — git commit before self-edit, extract model_patch.diff, evaluate the patched lineage in a fresh container — is exactly the harness-agnostic artifact an acceptance layer should consume; (2) the cheap-first staged ladder (10 -> 50 -> 500 tasks) with explicit promotion thresholds; (3) the binary task-success vector: an acceptance layer can compute the per-task delta between parent and child (which tasks flipped pass->fail) instead of comparing aggregate scores, and the same vector serves as a behavioural fingerprint for diversity accounting; (4) the keep_better policy with a noise leeway is a minimal regression gate template; (5) the injected-fault recovery test (Table 2) is a reusable robustness probe for candidate agents. What it proves: with only compile + smoke gating and keep_all archiving, strong selection pressure still produced a competitive agent, so an acceptance layer need not be the only quality lever; but Table 1's spread (58.3% worst-case top-5 vs 71.0% best) shows the archive carries many mediocre agents that a real gate would prune, and ancestor-integration analysis shows accepted patches are composed from multiple lineages (parent ids like 'p1+p2'), so a gate must reason about merged provenance, not linear ancestry. What it leaves open, and what a harness-agnostic layer must add: a held-out evaluation split separate from the evolution tasks (GEA evolves on 60 tasks inside its 500-task test set); variance-aware promotion (a 10-task gate at pass@1 is too noisy to be a verification signal); leakage scanning — the reflection prompt hands the gold patch and tests to the model writing the evolution directive, so an acceptance layer should statically check candidate framework patches for benchmark-specific strings or hard-coded solutions; semantic review of what a patch changes (GEA records an LLM 'improvement diagnosis' but never gates on it); automated final-stage promotion (GEA's is manual); and any notion of intent alignment or security review beyond sandboxing. Net: GEA supplies the plumbing (diff, container, ladder, fingerprint) an acceptance layer can sit on top of, and demonstrates precisely the gaps such a layer must close.

deep_reads.name: Continual Harness: Online Adaptation for Self-Improving Foundation Agents
deep_reads.mechanism: An "agentic harness" H = (p, G, K, M): system prompt, sub-agents, skills (text heuristics + executable Python), memory. Two loops run inside ONE continuous episode with no environment reset. Inner loop: the model wrapped by H_t reads a minimal interface (frame + ASCII text map + button inputs) and acts. Outer loop: after warm-up W, every F steps a Refiner (same model as the agent; Gemini 3 Pro/Flash/Flash-Lite) reads the trajectory window tau_{t-F:t}, looks for failure signatures (navigation loops, tool-call failures, stalled objectives, missed exploration) and runs four LLM passes emitting CRUD edits: (i) rewrite p; (ii) create/update/retire sub-agents; (iii) add/update skills, repairing code that raised exceptions; (iv) add/update/demote memory. H_{t+1} = H_t (+) Delta is live at the next step. The agent can also trigger a pass on demand via an `evolve_harness` tool. In code (harness_evolver.py): MIN_WARMUP_STEPS=25, frequency 25 steps for the first 200 steps then 100; window default 50; sub-agent max_turns capped at 50; tool lists filtered to a fixed allowlist; each pass wrapped in try/except so failures are logged and skipped, and every generation appended to evolution_log.jsonl. Skills execute via exec() in a hand-built builtins sandbox with a `tools` dict. Three variants: from-scratch, bootstrap-frozen (inherit a prior run's memory/skills/subagents/prompt, no refinement), bootstrap-updating. Co-learning extension for open models (Gemma-4 31B SFT init): each iteration is a K=256-step DAgger rollout inside the live-refining harness; a pairwise process reward model (progress 0.4, action correctness 0.3, reasoning 0.2, format 0.1) scores sliding windows; low-reward windows are relabeled by a Gemini-3.1-pro teacher; soft SFT (3 epochs, lr 5e-6) updates weights; emulator state carries over between iterations. Baselines: H_min (minimalist), H_expert (hand-engineered PokeAgent harness with A*, type chart, damage calc).
deep_reads.eval_loop: Pokemon Red (11 milestones to Thunder Badge) and Emerald (9 milestones to Knuckle Badge, capped at 8.5k button presses). Metrics: cumulative button presses per milestone, milestone completion %, Gemini API dollar cost (Pareto plots), pathfinding skill path-cost deficit vs a Dijkstra oracle, skill/sub-agent invocation and success counts, memory reference rates. At least 3 seeds per condition; seed medians with per-seed traces; no confidence intervals or significance tests. Co-learning: milestone-vs-iteration staircases for 5 advancing runs, plus an LLM-graded evaluation matrix (tool_format, actionable, grounding, action_relevance, reasoning_similarity, hallucination) for warm-up stages. GPP section is anecdotal (human-in-the-loop run logs, Elite Four attempt table). Refinement decisions themselves are never evaluated before being applied; there is no held-out or counterfactual test of an edit.
deep_reads.limitations: Capability floor: on Gemini 3 Flash-Lite every Continual Harness variant (13-33%) underperforms H_min (20%) at equal or higher cost; Flash is high-variance. Automated refiner results only cover early game (Thunder Badge / Knuckle Badge), whereas the full-game completions (Blue, Yellow Legacy, Crystal) came from the human-in-the-loop GPP harness, not the automated loop. Residual gap to H_expert concentrates in dialogue-heavy gym interiors and multi-turn battle strategy. Documented regressions: bootstrap-updating on Red collapses sub-agent use after ~213 steps because newly authored sub-agents displace proven inherited ones (Table 2: only 6.4% of Red sub-agent invocations target inherited components in the updating variant vs 100% frozen); a 1,003-turn Power Plant stall where a self-authored tool with a schema mismatch was silently no-op'd 842 times while the agent believed it was working; most authored skills and memory entries are never used ("create-and-forget"). F and W are never stated in the paper (only in code). Refiner token/dollar cost is not accounted separately. Reset-free vs reset-based comparison not done. Co-learning: only Gemma-4 31B is viable, 5 runs, no aggregate statistics, no convergence. Depends on an engineered ASCII text map, not pixels. Code-level: the Refiner's skill-creation path (harness_evolver.py _evolve_skills store.add call) drops the `code` field, so Refiner-authored executable skills land as text-only unless later updated; open issue #52 (Aug 2026, unanswered) shows the exec sandbox exposes __import__ and /mcp/process_skill and /mcp/process_subagent are unauthenticated, so harness state can be injected by any network peer. Stars are inherited from the renamed PokeAgent Challenge repo.
deep_reads.key_insight: Applying LLM-authored CRUD edits to the whole harness (prompt, sub-agents, skills, memory) in place mid-episode, with no gate at all, recovers most of the minimalist-to-expert gap only when the base model is strong enough to use what it writes; below that floor the same unguarded loop makes the agent worse and more expensive, and even above it, newly authored components silently displace better inherited ones, which is direct evidence that harness update activity is not harness benefit.
open_gaps: No validation, testing, shadow evaluation, rollback, or version pinning of any harness edit before it goes live; regressions (Flash-Lite, step-213 sub-agent collapse, Power Plant loop) are observed post hoc only.
Refiner is the same model as the agent: no independent judge, no ground-truth signal used to accept or reject edits.
Emulator save-states exist in the infrastructure but are never used to counterfactually evaluate a candidate edit on the recent window.
Refinement frequency F and warm-up W unreported in paper; refiner cost not separated from acting cost.
Only seed medians, no CIs; Flash results high-variance; automated loop demonstrated only on early-game milestones, not full-game completion.
Newly authored sub-agents/skills lack a reuse prior or incumbent-vs-challenger comparison; most authored skills and memories are never invoked.
Released harness_evolver.py drops `code` when the Refiner creates a skill, so executable skills only enter via the agent's own process_skill or a later update.

Security: exec sandbox exposes __import__; /mcp/process_skill and /mcp/process_subagent accept unauthenticated writes, so harness integrity/provenance is unprotected (issue #52, open, no maintainer response).
Co-learning: single viable checkpoint (Gemma-4 31B), 5 runs, no convergence or aggregate stats; teacher is a frontier model, not self-teaching.
Reset-free vs reset-based refinement never compared head-to-head on the same task.
Repo activity stopped at the 2026-05-13 release; issues from Aug 2026 unanswered.
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer: This paper is the clearest published negative-space example for an acceptance layer: a full self-modification loop over prompts, sub-agents, skills, and memory with zero acceptance gating, applied live and reset-free. What it proves: (1) unguarded edits are net-positive only above a capability floor (Pro: ~40% cost reduction, 100% milestones at $130 vs H_min 98% at $215) and net-negative below it (Flash-Lite), so an acceptance layer must measure realized benefit per edit, not update activity; (2) concrete failure classes a harness-agnostic gate must catch, each observable from generic signals: a newly authored tool that is invoked with a malformed contract and silently no-ops for 842 turns while the agent claims success (gate: contract/smoke test on first invocation, and 'claimed success without state delta' detection); new components displacing proven inherited ones with lower per-invocation success (gate: incumbent-vs-challenger with a reuse prior, tracked via per-component invocation/success counters the repo already collects); create-and-forget accumulation (gate: retention conditioned on usage evidence, GC of never-invoked entries); refiner-created executable skills with no code (gate: schema-level invariant 'executable skill has code that compiles'). What to reuse: the (p, G, K, M) CRUD taxonomy as the edit schema an acceptance policy is written over; evolution_log.jsonl (per-generation diff + store counts) as the audit-trail format; the failure-signature list as trigger conditions; the pairwise PRM weighting (progress/action correctness/reasoning/format) as a candidate online score for accept/reject decisions; the H_min-to-H_expert bracket and Dijkstra-oracle path deficit as benchmark metrics for what a gate recovers or protects. What it leaves open and where a layer can add value: the infrastructure has emulator save/load state, so a gate could evaluate a candidate Delta by replaying the last window from a checkpoint with H_t vs H_t (+) Delta before committing, something the paper never does; the same-model Refiner has no independent judge, which is exactly the role an external acceptance layer plays; and issue #52 shows acceptance must also cover provenance and integrity (who wrote this skill, does the sandbox actually confine it), not only quality. Caveat: results are Pokemon-only with an engineered text map and 3-seed medians, so effect sizes should not be transferred to coding or web agents without re-measurement.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Essentially none at the acceptance level. Code-level guardrails only: sub-agent tool lists filtered to a fixed allowlist (fallback to press_buttons), sub-agent max_turns capped at 50 and system_instructions/directive truncated to 12k chars, each refinement pass wrapped in try/except so a failed pass is logged and skipped (prompt falls back to the previous prompt on exception), skills run via exec() in a hand-built __builtins__ allowlist (which nonetheless includes __import__, per open issue #52), and an opt-in X-Internal-API-Key that only protects /save_state and /load_state, not the /mcp/process_skill or /mcp/process_subagent write routes. No pre-application testing, no regression check, no rollback, no human review in the automated loop; the paper acknowledges regressions and proposes a reuse prior and deprecation rule only as future work. Emulator anticheat utilities exist for the benchmark but do not gate harness edits.
deep_reads.key_results: Emerald, Gemini 3 Pro: H_CH from scratch reaches 100% of 9 milestones at $130 median vs H_min 98% at $215 (~40% cost cut); bootstrap variants 96-100% at $110-140. Flash: bootstrap-updating 80% at $42 vs H_min 77% at $30 (high variance). Flash-Lite: H_min 20% at $11; all H_CH variants 13-33% at comparable or higher cost. Red (11 milestones): H_CH cuts button presses at every milestone vs H_min, bootstrap-updating beats from-scratch at every milestone, H_expert remains best; claim is 'recovers a majority of the H_min-to-expert efficiency gap' with no numeric percentage given. Pathfinding skill: path-cost deficit vs Dijkstra drops from ~50% to single digits over a 24h run; hundreds of skill invocations vs zero for H_min. Table 2 inheritance: frozen variants route 98-100% of invocations to inherited components; Red bootstrap-updating drops to 6.4% +/- 5.7 for sub-agents. Co-learning (Gemma-4 31B SFT init, K=256, DAgger + PRM + Gemini-3.1-pro relabeling): SFT/GRPO warm-up alone yields no in-game progress; online loop yields staircase milestone progress in 5 runs from start and from mid-game checkpoints; Qwen3.5 27B/35B without warm-up cannot leave the starting area. GPP (human-in-the-loop harness): first to finish Blue (May 2025), Yellow Legacy hard mode no losses (Aug 2025), Crystal no endgame losses (Nov 2025); Elite Four took 18-20 attempts per member, Champion on attempt 4. At least 3 seeds/condition, medians only.

deep_reads.name: MOSS: Self-Evolution through Source-Level Rewriting in Autonomous Agent Systems
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Qianshu Cai (USTC; remote RA at HKGAI/HKUST), Yonggang Zhang, Xianzhang Jia, Huajiang (Vito) Zheng, Wei Xue (Hong Kong Generative AI R&D Center / HKUST), Jun Song (HKBU), Xinmei Tian (USTC), Yike Guo (HKUST). Code org: hkgai-official.
deep_reads.last_activity: Repo last push 2026-05-23 (4 commits total: initial commit + tec_report.pdf). Issues #2 (security, 2026-08-03) and #3 (reproducibility, 2026-08-19) open and unanswered by maintainers; last community comment 2026-09-04.
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (cs.AI, cs.LG), 12 pages; not peer-reviewed. OpenAlex: 0 citations as of 2026-09-14. Coverage limited to aggregator blogs (emergentmind, startuphub.ai, alanhou.org). GitHub: 22 stars, 3 forks, Apache-2.0 (vendors OpenClaw, MIT).
deep_reads.mechanism:
MOSS bolts a self-rewriting loop onto OpenClaw (a production TypeScript agent gateway) running in Docker. Evidence: a 30-min cron (`moss evo catch-up`) scans session JSONLs, and an LLM "task-evaluator" tags 4-7 keypoints per chunk (strong/adequate/weak/missing); weak/missing chunks are appended to a per-conversation batch (auto-sealed at 8 chunks). Users can also flag a turn in chat (`moss evo flag`). `moss evo start [--depth shallow|standard|deep]` runs a bounded loop (max iters 3/5/8; trials per task 2/3/5; plateau window 1/2/3).

Per iteration, a deterministic orchestrator inside the container spawns an external coding-agent CLI on the host (Claude Code default, invoked with `--dangerously-skip-permissions --model sonnet`; Codex/DeepSeek-TUI/OpenCode pluggable) once per stage: Locate -> Plan -> Plan-Review (multi-round) -> Implement (single git commit on the inner OpenClaw repo; allowed write paths `src/**`, `test/**`, Dockerfile, package.json, etc.) -> Code-Review (multi-round, hard-reset between rounds) -> Build candidate image -> Trial (host daemon spawns N ephemeral containers from the candidate image, bridge-networked, no user-state mount, replays the batch tasks n_trials times) -> Task-Evaluate (LLM re-tags the locked keypoints from trial traces) -> Reviewer (LLM reads per-task evals plus a baseline-vs-iter keypoint matrix and emits CONVERGED / NEED_MORE_WORK / FUNDAMENTAL_LIMIT_MODEL / FUNDAMENTAL_LIMIT_ARCHITECTURE; orchestrator downgrades NEED_MORE_WORK to CONVERGED on plateau).

On CONVERGED the batch is marked ready_to_apply and a webhook tells the chat agent; the user says "apply", the gateway writes swap-req.json, and the host-daemon supervisor does `docker compose up` with the new image, then a 90 s probe window (every 5 s, 4 checks: heartbeat <=30 s, container running, two CLI status probes); 3 consecutive passes commit and record last-good-image.txt, otherwise rollback to the last-known-good record. User-state volume survives the swap.

Case study: four claweval compliance-audit tasks (DeepSeek V3.2 substrate); one iteration produced a 3-file, +177/-1 harness patch (annotation branch in tool-result mediator + pre-call deny gate in before-tool-call hook + a test).
deep_reads.eval_loop: Two separate evaluators. (1) Internal gate: LLM task-evaluator tags 4-7 keypoints per task (locked at baseline) from trial transcripts; matrix.ts builds a per-(task,keypoint) [baseline, iter1..] matrix with improved/regressed/unchanged deltas and a normalized pass rate mean(tag)/3; an LLM reviewer issues the 4-way verdict with a "grounding mandate" to cite matrix rows; `detectPlateau` converts NEED_MORE_WORK into CONVERGED when no row improved over the depth window; `decideContinue` also aborts on max_iter, no-progress streak, build-failure streak, session-crash streak. A Stage 9b "validation" trial runs on CONVERGED, but in the shipped user-mode path `validationSet: batchId` (evolution-http.helpers.ts:667), i.e. it re-runs the same batch, not a holdout. (2) External witness: claweval grader (rubric + LLM judge, 0.75 pass threshold, 0.20 score floor from robustness term) is reported in the paper only and, per code comments, is "demo-only display data, not evolution decision input". Trials: mean of 3 per task. Deployment gate: user consent (auto-acknowledged in the paper's run) + 90 s health probe with rollback. No unit-test gating; Code-Review is an LLM judgment of the diff against the plan.
deep_reads.key_results: Table 2 (claweval grader, mean of 3 trials, OpenClaw + DeepSeek V3.2, one iteration): T141zh SLA audit 0.3273 -> 0.5330 (+0.2057); T142 0.2527 -> 0.5453 (+0.2926); T137zh restock chain 0.2213 -> 0.4567 (+0.2354); T138 0.2090 -> 0.9049 (+0.6959, all 3 trials above the 0.75 pass line); mean 0.2526 -> 0.6100 (+0.3574). T137zh: 1/3 trials pass. The patch: 3 files, +177/-1, harness-only (mediator + hook), no prompt/skill change. The authors explicitly state the four tasks are both the evolution input batch and the test set. No ablations, no repeated runs, no variance, no wall-clock or token cost, no comparison against a prompt/skill-level fix for the same failures, no held-out tasks. Repo issue #3 (unanswered) reports that `benchmark/claw-eval/runner/benchmark.py`, the "demo" evolution mode used for the experiment, and the auto-scan-to-flag-batch adapter are absent from the public tree, so Table 2 is not currently reproducible from the repo; it also notes the paper's undisclosed judge was Gemini and that baselines of 0.21-0.33 imply ~1-16% completion, consistent with mis-wired tool access rather than reasoning failure.
deep_reads.limitations: Evidence is a single one-iteration run on 4 tasks with train == test; the internal reviewer prompts were themselves tuned on those same four tasks (prompts/strategic-reviewer.md embeds T137zh/T138/T141zh/T142 with the exact Table 2 baselines as a "calibration anchor" instructing the reviewer to bias toward APPROVE_CONVERGED). The core "source-level is a strict superset of text-level" claim is argued, not tested: no head-to-head against a prompt/skill fix. The user-consent gate was auto-acknowledged in the experiment, so "user-consent-gated" was never exercised. No holdout/regression check: user-mode validationSet is the training batch. Acceptance is an LLM judging LLM-produced tags; plateau (no progress) is treated as convergence; verdict parsing is substring-based (`NEED_MORE_WORK (not yet CONVERGED)` parses as CONVERGED, issue #2). Benchmark runner and demo mode are missing from the repo; maintainers unresponsive since May. Cost is only informally estimated (standard tier ~1-2 h, deep 3-5+ h). Only OpenClaw substrate demonstrated. Security: coding agent runs on the host with bypassPermissions and inherits the daemon's full environment; host daemon socket is 0666 and unauthenticated yet mounted into the very container being self-modified; swap target image is not digest-pinned or signed.
deep_reads.key_insight: MOSS's real contribution is the promotion plumbing (candidate image -> ephemeral replay workers -> consent -> in-place swap -> health-probe rollback with an independent last-known-good record), not its acceptance decision: the decision that a self-modification is "good" is an LLM reviewer reading LLM-assigned keypoint tags on the training batch, with plateau-equals-converged and no holdout, and the modifier's write scope (`src/**`) includes the evolution pipeline and its prompts, so the gate is inside the mutable surface it is meant to guard.
open_gaps: No held-out or regression evaluation: validationSet is the training batch; nothing checks that the harness patch did not break other channels/tasks.
Acceptance verdict is an LLM judgment over LLM tags; no deterministic, reproducible pass criterion (no test suite, no numeric threshold on the internal metric).
Plateau detection downgrades NEED_MORE_WORK to CONVERGED, so a stalled loop is promoted rather than rejected.

Implementer may write anywhere under src/** including src/evolution/** (reviewer prompts, verdict parser, matrix builder) — the gate is not isolated from the thing being modified; only a prompt rule fences it.
Verdict parser uses substring matching with the positive token first (issue #2); no exact-token closed-set parsing.

Host trust boundary: unauthenticated 0666 daemon socket mounted into the self-modifying container; coding agent runs with --dangerously-skip-permissions and full env; swap target image not digest-pinned.
Reproducibility: benchmark runner, demo mode and flag-batch adapter absent from the repo (issue #3, unanswered); judge model undisclosed in paper.
No ablation of pipeline stages, review gates, depth tiers, or coding-agent providers; single run, no variance.
No comparison to text-level (prompt/skill) fix for the same failures, so the superset/determinism claims are untested.
No cost/latency accounting; no measurement of health-probe false-negative rate (probes check liveness, not behavior).
Batch curation is itself an LLM tagger (weak/missing) with a 1 MiB chunk threshold that in practice yields zero chunks for typical sessions (issue #3).
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer:
Directly on-topic: MOSS is a full self-modification-to-production loop whose weakest link is exactly the acceptance decision, so it is a useful negative example and a partial parts bin.

Reusable pieces: (a) the deployment-side gate design — build a candidate image, replay evidence in ephemeral workers off the live container, require explicit apply, then a time-boxed health probe with N consecutive passes and rollback to an independently recorded last-known-good artifact (supervisor.py) — is harness-agnostic and worth copying as the last stage of any acceptance layer; (b) the "keypoint matrix" idea (lock a rubric at baseline, re-score every candidate on the same keys, compute per-row improved/regressed/unchanged) is a clean shape for a harness-agnostic behavioral diff, if the tagger is made deterministic or at least ensembled; (c) the CLI-in / webhook-out / capability-doc contract for talking to any substrate (five primitives: shell exec, fs read, scheduler, webhook delivery, system-prompt injection) is a good minimal substrate interface; (d) the explicit "forbidden write paths" list in implementer.md is the seed of a scope policy, but it must be enforced by the gate (git diff path check), not by prompt.

What it proves: a coding agent can land a real harness-level patch (mediator + hook, +177 LOC) that a prompt edit could not, and the container-swap/rollback machinery works mechanically.

What it disproves or leaves open for an acceptance layer: (1) LLM-reviewer-over-LLM-tags is not an acceptance gate — it has no holdout, treats plateau as convergence, and its prompts were tuned on the very tasks reported; an acceptance layer needs an evaluator that the modifier cannot reach and a fixed, pre-registered pass rule. (2) Scope isolation must be structural: MOSS lets `src/**` (including src/evolution/**) be rewritten, and the daemon socket that runs the coding agent with bypassed permissions is mounted into the self-modifying container — the acceptance layer should run out-of-band (host side, separate identity, authenticated channel, digest-pinned artifacts) and diff-check that the candidate did not touch evaluator/gate code. (3) Verdict parsing shows why gate outputs must be typed/closed-set, not free-text substring matched. (4) Health probes check liveness, not behavior; an acceptance layer needs post-swap behavioral canaries or shadow replay against held-out evidence. (5) Missing entirely: regression suite, cost budget, multi-run variance, and provenance from failure evidence to accepted diff — all of which a harness-agnostic acceptance layer should own so that the coding agent (any of MOSS's four CLIs) becomes an untrusted proposer.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Stated: user-consent gate before swap (`moss evo apply`; MOSS_AUTO_APPLY_ON_CONVERGE=1 opt-in auto-swap; auto-acknowledged in the paper's experiment); 90 s / 5 s / 3-consecutive-pass health probe with 4 checks and rollback to host-recorded last-good-image.txt (rollback-history.jsonl kept); trial workers in separate bridge netns without the user-state mount, torn down per iteration; user-state volume preserved across swap; all plans/diffs/logs/matrices readable by the agent for audit; Plan-Review and Code-Review LLM gates with round budgets and git hard-reset between code rounds; stop sentinel (`moss evo stop`); stage-abort streaks (build failures, session crashes); prompt-level write-scope list for the implementer and a prompt rule that the chat agent never writes evo-loop-state/. Actual gaps found in code and issues: Claude Code runner uses `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and a bundled settings file with `defaultMode: bypassPermissions`, inherits full daemon env; host RPC socket chmod 0666 with no peer-cred/token auth, mounted into the gateway container (issue #2 PoC); swap-req `target_image` accepted without digest/signature; verdict parser substring bug; implementer write scope includes src/evolution/**; no holdout validation.
