deep_reads.name: karpathy/autoresearch
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Andrej Karpathy (solo; 7 small community PRs merged)
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-03-26 (last push, commit 228791f). Issues/discussions still active through 2026-09-09 but no maintainer commits since March; 142 open PRs vs 7 merged.
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: GitHub only (no paper). 95.7k stars / 13.4k forks in 6 months; 30+ derivative repos >500 stars (pi-autoresearch 8k, AutoResearchClaw 14k, darwin-skill 6k, autokernel 1.5k, NousResearch/autoreason). Cited by AutoKernel (arXiv 2603.21331), Fortune (2026-03-17), latent.space AINews 'Sparks of Recursive Self Improvement'. Two entries on nanochat's 'Time to GPT-2' leaderboard (#5, #6).
deep_reads.mechanism:
What evolves is the ML training script of a target model (train.py: architecture, init, optimizer, hyperparameters, batch size, depth), not the agent itself. Three files: prepare.py (389 lines, fixed: data download from karpathy/climbmix-400b-shuffle, BPE tokenizer vocab 8192, dataloader, evaluate_bpb), train.py (630 lines, agent-editable: simplified single-GPU nanochat with Muon+AdamW, DEPTH=8 ~50M params, torch.manual_seed(42) inside the editable file), program.md (7KB, human-edited: the 'skill' that IS the harness).

Loop (verbatim from program.md): create branch autoresearch/<tag>; first run is baseline; then LOOP FOREVER: edit train.py -> git commit -> `uv run train.py > run.log 2>&1` -> `grep "^val_bpb:\|^peak_vram_mb:" run.log` -> if grep empty, `tail -n 50 run.log` and fix or mark crash -> append row (commit, val_bpb, memory_gb, keep|discard|crash, description) to untracked results.tsv -> if val_bpb strictly lower, advance branch; if equal or worse, git reset to previous commit. Kill runs >10 min. NEVER STOP; never ask the human.

Training: wall-clock budget TIME_BUDGET=300s counted only after step 10 (excludes compile); progress-based LR warmdown; NaN/loss>100 fast-fail exits. Eval: bits-per-byte on pinned val shard 06542, EVAL_TOKENS=40*524288 (~21M tokens) at fixed MAX_SEQ_LEN=2048, computed inside train.py by calling prepare.evaluate_bpb and printed to stdout.

There is no orchestration code: the agent (Claude Code / Codex, run 'with all permissions disabled') interprets the Markdown loop interactively in a tmux session that Karpathy babysits. Karpathy explicitly rejected a scripted Ralph loop (#42) because he wants to inject ideas mid-run. Scale promotion is manual and out-of-repo: he ran the loop on nanochat d12, then hand-ported ~20 kept changes to d24 on 8xH100 (commits 6ed7d1d, a825e63).
deep_reads.eval_loop: Single scalar proxy: val_bpb after exactly 5 min of training on one GPU. Acceptance rule is greedy strict-less-than against the running best, one run per candidate, no repeats, no seed variation, no noise floor, no statistical test, no holdout beyond the one val shard, no scale check. Soft secondary criteria (VRAM, 'simplicity criterion' weighing complexity vs gain) are left to the agent's judgment in prose. The only hard checks in code are NaN/loss>100 fast-fail and a 10-minute kill rule. Eval integrity relies entirely on prose ('prepare.py is read-only', 'do not modify evaluate_bpb'): the call site, the metric print, the seed, and the step counter all live in the file the agent edits. The real acceptance gate that produced the headline results happened outside the loop: Karpathy manually re-validated d12 findings at d24 on the 8xH100 time-to-GPT-2 benchmark.
deep_reads.key_results: Demonstrated (independently verifiable in karpathy/nanochat): commit 6ed7d1d (2026-03-09) 'All of these improvements were developed by Claude running autonomously over ~2 days using autoresearch. I didn't touch anything', tuned on d12 and transferred to d24 -> nanochat leaderboard entry #5: time-to-GPT-2 2.02h -> 1.80h (11%); round 2 commit a825e63 (2026-03-14, 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6') added smear + backout -> entry #6: 1.65h (18% cumulative vs pre-autoresearch). Round-1 changes: ~13 bullet items (unembedding LR 0.004->0.008, WD 0.2->0.28, per-group Adam betas, Muon beta2/momentum warmup, cosine WD schedule, post-QK-norm scaling 1.15, embed init 0.8, RoPE theta 10K->100K, shorter window, softcap 20->15, VE gate changes). Claimed only via tweet: ~700 experiments, ~20 additive changes. README teaser run: 83 experiments, 15 kept, val_bpb 0.9979 -> 0.9773 (~2%), final 'kept improvement' is 'random seed 42->137'. Community: RTX 4070 laptop 282 experiments / 38 keeps 2.770->2.495 (#448); RTX 3060 27 exp 1.604->1.201 (#596, heavily undertrained regime); Tobi Lutke 37 exp / 19% (Fortune, unverified).
deep_reads.limitations: 1) Acceptance has no noise floor: the official teaser figure keeps a seed change (42->137) as an improvement, and three consecutive RoPE-theta bumps with sub-0.0005 deltas; run-to-run CUDA nondeterminism is a few 1e-4 bpb (PR #560 estimate), so many 'keeps' are coin flips that then anchor subsequent search. 2) Eval integrity is prose-only: agent owns train.py, can skip optimizer.step, wrap/replace evaluate_bpb, print a fabricated val_bpb, or change EVAL_TOKENS; issue #599 has a stdlib reproducer where a fake 0.05 bpb gets KEPT. Nothing binds the printed number to code/data/model. 3) 5-minute d8/d12 proxy; transfer to larger scale is asserted by Karpathy's manual d24 check, never measured in-loop; consumer-GPU runs (val_bpb 1.2-2.7) optimize an undertrained regime where 'halve depth, shrink batch' wins. 4) Harness-fragile: Codex stops after 5-8 experiments (#57, 41 comments, OpenAI staff engaged); Claude drifts/asks to stop as context fills (vlasenkoalexey). 5) results.tsv is untracked, printed metrics not persisted with artifacts; no reproducibility record. 6) README says MIT but no LICENSE file (API license=null, PR #605 open). 7) Effectively frozen since 2026-03-26; 142 open PRs, 7 merged. 8) Runs with 'all permissions disabled' - no sandbox. 9) Critics: essentially AutoML/NAS with an LLM proposer (Fortune); 'clean demo loop, not a research architecture' (#502).
deep_reads.key_insight: The entire 'harness' is a Markdown file plus git: fixed compute budget + fixed scalar metric + keep/revert-on-branch is enough to turn an off-the-shelf coding agent into a research loop that beat a top researcher's hand-tuned code. But every property that would make the loop trustworthy (eval not tampered, gains above noise, transfer to scale) is enforced either by prose the agent can ignore or by a human doing manual re-validation outside the loop.
open_gaps: No noise-floor or repeated-baseline protocol; greedy strict-less-than keeps seed luck (README teaser proves it). PR #560 proposed |delta| >= 2*sigma_noise, closed unmerged.

No binding of reported metric to execution evidence (code hash, val-shard hash, optimizer step count from optimizer state, final model hash). Issue #599's 'ExperimentReceipt' design sketches it; nothing merged.
Eval code and metric print live in the agent-editable file; no process/privilege separation between proposer and judge.
No in-loop scale-transfer check: the d12->d24 promotion that produced the headline numbers was manual.
Loop control depends on the agent obeying 'NEVER STOP'; Codex fails, Claude drifts; no harness-agnostic driver (Karpathy rejected one for interactivity reasons).
No persistence of run artifacts (results.tsv untracked, no checkpoint before eval, no run receipts), so kept commits are not reproducible after the fact.
No secondary acceptance signals (loss stability, VRAM hard cap, complexity budget) enforced in code; 'simplicity criterion' is agent judgment.
Repo is frozen; the ~700-experiment log that backs the headline claim was never published.
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer:
This is the canonical minimal specimen of a self-modification loop where the acceptance gate is the whole system, and it exhibits, in public and reproducibly, exactly the failure classes an acceptance layer must cover.

What to reuse: (a) the contract shape - fixed budget, fixed frozen evaluator file, single scalar with a 'lower is better' rule, git commit as the unit of candidate and git reset as rejection, an append-only ledger with commit|metric|resource|status|description; this is harness-agnostic by construction (works with any agent that can run shell) and is what the acceptance layer should wrap rather than replace. (b) The separation of 'program.md' (human-owned policy) from 'train.py' (agent-owned candidate) and 'prepare.py' (frozen judge) is the right three-role decomposition; the layer's job is to make the judge role actually frozen.

What it proves: a keep/revert gate on a real metric is sufficient for real gains (nanochat 2.02h->1.65h, verifiable in commits), and that a Markdown-only gate gets adopted at scale (95k stars, dozens of forks) - so an acceptance layer that is harder to adopt than 'edit a .md and run a script' will lose.

What it disproves / leaves open: prose-enforced integrity does not hold - the judge (evaluate_bpb call, EVAL_TOKENS, seed, step counter, metric print) is reachable from the mutable file, and issue #599 shows a fabricated metric is accepted. Greedy single-run acceptance accepts noise (seed 42->137 kept in the official figure). Transfer of proxy gains to the real objective was validated only by a human at d24. So the layer must provide, outside the agent's write scope: (1) a judge process that recomputes the metric from a checkpoint the candidate must emit, on a hashed frozen val set, with the agent's printed number ignored; (2) a receipt binding candidate commit + judge code hash + data hash + evidence of real training (optimizer step count, params changed vs baseline hash) + wall time; (3) a noise-aware decision rule (repeated baselines or paired seeds; reject |delta| below the measured floor) and a budget/resource hard cap; (4) an optional promotion stage that re-runs kept candidates at larger scale or longer budget before merging to the trunk; (5) a harness-independent loop driver or stop-hook so 'NEVER STOP' is not a model obedience question. Issue #599's thread already sketches assurance tiers (self-attested / signed / external witness / hardware attested) worth adopting as a schema field. The ~700-experiment log was never released, so the acceptance layer cannot be back-tested against it; the community runs in #448/#596 with results.tsv published are the available test corpora.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Prose only: program.md forbids editing prepare.py, evaluate_bpb, or adding dependencies; 'simplicity criterion'; 10-minute kill; NaN/loss>100 fast-fail exit in train.py; each run on a dedicated git branch so trunk is untouched; VRAM as 'soft constraint'. Human sits in an interactive tmux session and babysits. README instructs running the agent with all permission checks disabled; no sandbox, no privilege separation, no artifact signing, no reproducibility record. Later Karpathy tweet mentions his 'autoresearch labs got wiped out in the oauth outage' - no failover.

deep_reads.name: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Yizhe Chi, Wenyi Li, Deyao Hong, Xiaoqiu Wang, Mingju Gao, Kaisen Yang, Bingxiang He, Youjie Zheng, Calvin Xiao, Qinhuai Na — Einsia.AI (Navers Lab) with Tsinghua University affiliation
deep_reads.last_activity: Repo last push 2026-08-21 (3 commits total: v1.5 release + README badges); GitHub issue #1 opened 2026-09-02 (Awesome-Recursive-Self-Critiquing index asking authors to verify their summary, still open); Docker Hub image chiyizhe/ai4ai last updated 2026-08-20, 1,330 pulls as of 2026-09-14
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: arXiv preprint (CC BY 4.0). Citation count unavailable (Semantic Scholar rate-limited; paper is ~25 days old, expect ~0). Uptake so far: indexed in pILLOW-1/Awesome-Recursive-Self-Critiqung RSI benchmark list; one third-party blog (kenashe.ai, 2026-08-21). Code: github.com/Einsia/AI4AI-Bench, 38 stars, 2 forks, Apache-2.0.
deep_reads.mechanism: Each task is a tuple (C, a0, q, m, d): frozen research repo C (10 families: OpenR1 SFT, RAGEN multi-turn GRPO, on-policy distillation, Bradley-Terry RM, DPO, DDPO, NPO unlearning, DiGress graph diffusion, Model Soup, OWL/Wanda pruning), fixed start model a0, cheap proxy metric q, hidden final metric m, direction d. The agent (Claude Code or Codex CLI mounted into a Docker container, network_mode=no-network, host CONNECT proxy allowlisting only the model-API hostname) gets 4h on one B300 to edit anything under /workspace and query /opt/harness/fast_eval as often as it likes, then runs submit.sh, which git-diffs the workspace into candidate.patch. ONLY that patch crosses the boundary. A pre-GPU static check (task.py describe_patch_rejections) rejects patches carrying data/weights extensions, binary blobs, bytecode, new files >4 MiB, or >16 added rows in data-shaped files. The patch is applied to a fresh container and `bash /workspace/run.sh` executes from the fixed start for up to 12h with no inherited rollouts, checkpoints, caches or env. Up to three checkpoints (highest numeric progress) go through a frozen per-task validator computed from the artifact's own bytes, never candidate metadata: HF loadability; OWL decoder sparsity in [0.699,0.701] measured from weights (the metadata path was deliberately deleted); Model Soup affine-hull least-squares residual test proving the checkpoint is a combination of the 72 ingredients; RAGEN refuses any executable file or auto_map key in the checkpoint; BTRM train/RewardBench overlap gate. Each valid checkpoint is scored independently by the frozen evaluator on hidden assets; result = best_valid_of_up_to_3. Score sigma = 0.1 + 0.9*(phi(x)-phi_b)/(phi*-phi_b) with three anchors (uninformative, baseline, optimum): 0.1 = shipped algorithm, 1.0 = optimum, <0.1 = regression. host_contract.lock.json hashes every orchestrator .py/.sh plus task.toml/declaration/instruction/assets.lock; only strict matches yield "official_self_hosted" receipts. A separate LLM reads each diff and tags it run-side (budget/checkpointing, hyperparameters, checkpoint selection, capacity) vs learning-side (loss, supervision, update rule, training data).
deep_reads.eval_loop: Cross-sectional study: 29 configurations x 10 tasks = 290 cells, 6 systems — Claude Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 (Claude Code harness, 5 effort levels), Kimi K3 (Claude Code, one level), GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna (Codex harness, effort none/low/medium/high/xhigh/max). Each cell = one 4h exploration + one 12h fresh replay + frozen final eval; baseline = the repo's own committed code run under the identical 12h procedure, apparently once (no seed replication reported). Total exploration API spend $5,334. All 290 trajectories and scored submissions are published on lab.einsia.ai/ai4ai; replay of any external patch is supported via `trial.sh --candidate-patch`, but the paper/docs state an official blind evaluation service does not yet exist — all results are self-hosted.
deep_reads.key_results: Mean over 290 cells: 0.166 (0.1 = baseline). System means: Claude Opus 5 0.250, GPT-5.6 Sol 0.191, Kimi K3 0.174, Claude Sonnet 5 0.145, GPT-5.6 Terra 0.135, GPT-5.6 Luna 0.117; best single config Opus 5 medium 0.288. 124/290 cells (43%) score below 0.1 (worse than the shipped code); 19 score zero (8 exited with no usable patch, 11 ran 12h but produced no loadable merged model; 12 of 19 at the two lowest effort levels). Of 280 classified submissions (Kimi excluded), 17 unclassifiable; of 263, 141 stayed run-side, 122 touched learning; learning-side mean 0.226 vs run-side 0.126 (gap 0.100, SE 0.022). Raising Codex effort none->max lifted algorithmic-layer share 8.0%->64.0% and mean 0.094->0.196. Cost medians: Sol $434, Opus 5 $181, Luna $48 (Opus best at under half Sol's spend). RAGEN saturated: 7 configs hit 1.000 (Opus low/med/high, Sol low/high/max, Terra max) by abandoning GRPO for imitation learning on self-generated optimal Sokoban solutions (one added DAgger); baseline was 87/512. OWL: perplexity 53.4 -> 13.0 (sigma 0.42) via prune + layerwise distillation + 666-step masked KD fine-tune. Model Soup: agent built a 500x faster in-GPU eval rig (190s -> 0.38s per coefficient vector), greedy soup 0.7025 vs baseline 0.686. Hardest tasks (medians at/below 0.1): OpenR1 (best 0.138), DiGress, NPO.
deep_reads.limitations: Not recursive despite the title: one generation, no chaining, no test of whether a gen-2 agent inherits the gain. No noise model: baselines appear single-run, no CIs/stderr per cell, so many "below 0.1" cells and small "wins" (e.g. OpenR1 0.127->0.138, BTRM 74.9->77.1) may be inside seed variance; only one aggregate SE (0.022) reported. Run-side/learning-side labels come from an unvalidated LLM judge with no inter-rater check. Some proxies are drawn from the same corpus as the final (BTRM, DPO, Model Soup) so proxy overfitting is not fully excluded; no proxy-final correlation stats. RAGEN's seven perfect scores are contract-compliant but arguably a task-ceiling/specification artifact (writing a solver and distilling it), inflating aggregate means; OWL's "one-shot pruning" task was solved by adding fine-tuning stages the contract permitted. Only two agent harnesses (Claude Code, Codex) and one GPU type; 4h/1xB300 budget is tight. Small sample (10 repos, 1 run per cell). No blind evaluation service — every result, including the paper's, is self-hosted with a self-attested "strict" flag. Paper reports no submission ever rejected by the patch safety check, so its real-world stopping power is undemonstrated. Repo has 3 commits, 38 stars, one open issue; the source-vs-data boundary is porous in principle (task-specific heuristics or a hand-written solver are "source").
deep_reads.key_insight: To measure (and gate) self-improvement you must (a) let only source cross the boundary, (b) rerun it from a clean start under an evaluator frozen and hidden before the first run, and (c) verify invariants on the produced artifact's bytes rather than on the agent's self-reported metadata or the mount list — and once you do that, 43% of frontier-agent "improvements" turn out to be regressions and most of the rest never touched how the model learns.
open_gaps: No seed-variance model: an acceptance gate built on this needs a statistical threshold (multi-seed baseline, CI on delta) to distinguish improvement from noise
No multi-generation chaining: whether an accepted algorithmic change compounds when the improved model becomes the next agent is untested
LLM-judge diff classification (run-side vs learning-side) is unvalidated and used only for post-hoc analysis, not as a gate
Specification-gaming edge cases (solver-distillation on RAGEN, fine-tuning added to 'one-shot' pruning) are contract-legal; no mechanism for spirit-of-task adjudication or task-ceiling detection
Proxy-overfitting undetected: some proxies share a corpus with the final metric and no proxy-final divergence statistics are reported
12h fresh replay is too expensive for an inner-loop gate; no tiered/cheaper verification path is offered
No blind evaluation service — official results depend on self-attested strict-mode receipts
Source-only boundary is porous: a patch can embed hand-written task solvers or hardcoded heuristics as 'source'
Only two harnesses (Claude Code, Codex) and one GPU type; harness-agnosticism of the exploration side is untested, though the replay side accepts any external patch
Real-asset separation of the Model Soup affine-hull test was never measured (only synthetic smoke)
No rejected-patch statistics reported, so the patch safety check's real efficacy is unknown
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer: This is the closest thing in the literature to a worked reference implementation of an acceptance layer for self-modifying training code, and its verification half is harness-agnostic by construction: the formal/validation/score pipeline consumes only `candidate.patch` (replayable via `trial.sh --candidate-patch` from any source, hashed and bound to an immutable run-config), so it can sit behind any agent harness. Directly reusable patterns: (1) patch-only boundary with a pre-GPU static gate (`orchestrator/task.py:describe_patch_rejections`) that rejects data/weight extensions, binary blobs, bytecode, >4 MiB new files, and >16 added rows in data-shaped files — reads diff headers only, so rejection is free; (2) fresh-container replay that inherits no exploration state, with a frozen evaluator and hidden final assets fixed before the first run; (3) artifact-side invariant checks computed from produced bytes, never from candidate-written metadata — OWL's sparsity gate (they explicitly deleted the metadata path because it 'only proved the candidate could write 0.7 into a file'), Model Soup's affine-hull residual test (sketch chooses coefficients, full pass measures truth), RAGEN's refusal of any executable file or `auto_map` in a checkpoint (blocks code execution inside the scorer); (4) a protocol-identity lock (`host_contract.lock.json`) hashing all orchestrator scripts plus task contract files, yielding machine-readable `result_classification` (official_self_hosted vs non_official_local) — a template for 'was the gate itself tampered with'; (5) a failure taxonomy that separates invalid artifacts from infrastructure errors (retryable) and insists 'a missing result is not a score of zero', with SHA-256 receipts hashed before and after validation so tampering invalidates rather than silently mutates; (6) best-valid-of-up-to-3 checkpoint selection to bound checkpoint-shopping; (7) egress CONNECT proxy allowlisting only the model API; (8) a three-anchor normalized score (uninformative/baseline/optimum) that makes incommensurable metrics comparable and puts regressions below a fixed line; (9) an improvement-type taxonomy (run-side vs learning-side) that a gate could use to require 'this change touched learning' before granting credit. What it proves: frontier agents regress the codebase 43% of the time under an honest gate, so 'code runs / tests pass / proxy went up' is not acceptance; agents will exploit self-reported metadata and mount-level trust if allowed; and contract-legal exploits (solver distillation, adding fine-tuning) still slip through, so a gate needs spirit-of-task adjudication. What it leaves open for the layer: no noise/CI threshold for accepting a delta; no cheap tiered verification (12h replay per candidate); no recursion/inheritance check across generations; the LLM diff classifier is analysis, not a gate; the source-vs-data boundary is porous; and the exploration side is coupled to Docker mounts at /workspace and /opt/harness and to two CLIs.
deep_reads.safety_measures: Container isolation with task.toml network_mode="no-network"; host-side HTTPS CONNECT egress proxy that allows only the exact model-API hostname and logs every denied target; read-only /assets and /opt/harness mounts; pids_limit 8192; only a source patch crosses to the formal phase; static patch rejection of data/weights/binary/bytecode/oversized files; fresh formal container inherits nothing; evaluator and final data hidden from the agent and frozen before the first run; checkpoint validator refuses executable files and auto_map keys (prevents code execution in the scorer); artifact invariants (sparsity, affine-hull membership, no train/eval overlap) computed from weights; SHA-256 provenance on patches and checkpoints re-hashed around validation/scoring; secrets regex-scrubbed from lifecycle logs; host-contract hash lock distinguishing official from local results; explicit `no_candidate.sh` path so an agent can decline to submit; instruction text warns against early submission and treating smoke tests as evidence.

deep_reads.name: Awesome-Harness-Self-Improvement (Awesome Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement)
deep_reads.mechanism:
Not a system; a curated EN/ZH reading list (README.md 41.7KB, README_zh.md 38KB, a banner, MIT license; no code). Created 2026-07-08, four days after Lilian Weng's "Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement" (2026-07-04), which it explicitly mirrors: Weng's seven "Future Challenges" reappear nearly verbatim as the list's eight "Future Directions".

Organizing device is an "Optimization Ladder" of what the harness self-modifies: L0 instruction prompts (APE, OPRO, GEPA), L1 context/memory (ACE, ReasoningBank, MCE), L2 workflow/graph (ADAS, AFlow, GPTSwarm), L3 harness/agent code (STOP, Gödel Agent, DGM, SICA, Self-Harness), L4 optimizer/meta-harness (Meta-Harness, MCE), L5 harness+weights jointly (SIA, SEAL). Scope rule: the harness must be the object that improves itself; hand-built harness design (ReAct, SWE-agent, MCP) and weight-only self-improvement (SPIN, RLVR, STaR) are confined to a boundary section §7.

94 entries (EN), 106 unique arXiv links. Sections: §1 foundations (5), §2 core harness optimization (47 across 2.1–2.6), §3 auto-research loops (13), §4 evaluators that close the loop (14: ML-research benchmarks, coding/terminal benchmarks, 3 generic verifier papers), §5 challenges/failure modes (10: Misevolution, reward hacking, RM overoptimization, reward tampering, CoT-monitor obfuscation, METR's SWE-bench-merge report), §6 surveys (4), §7 boundary (1 + inline IDs).

Curation flow: maintainer wrote everything in a 2-day burst (Jul 8–9); since then only four merged PRs, every one submitted by an author/maintainer of the paper being added (ClawBench, Ouroboros, CORAL, HAT). One fork is literally named "-promo". The HAT author self-classified the paper as a boundary reference (developer-reviewed edits, frozen weights), which the maintainer accepted.
deep_reads.eval_loop: None — it is a document. Quality control is manual PR review by one maintainer. I spot-verified the five most acceptance-relevant 2026 citations and all resolve to the claimed papers: Self-Harness 2606.09498 (Zhang et al., v3 Aug 2026), Meta-Harness 2603.28052 (Lee, Finn, Khattab et al., Stanford/Krafton/MIT), Ouroboros 2608.08311 (Razzhigaev et al.), SIA 2605.27276 (Hebbar et al.), and Weng's post. Five entries carry no link at all (Good 1965, AutoHarness, Terminal-Bench, METR merge report, ADAS survey); AutoHarness does exist as arXiv 2603.03329 (Google DeepMind) and both competing lists link it, so this is a curation miss not a hallucination. One-line summaries match abstracts where checked. ZH README has drifted: 91 vs 94 entries (CORAL, ClawBench, Ouroboros missing) because three of four PRs edited only the EN file.
deep_reads.limitations: (1) Single-maintainer, low velocity: maintainer's last content commit 2026-07-09; all subsequent activity is merging author self-submissions. (2) Small reach: 88 stars / 5 forks vs 4,179 for ai-boost/awesome-harness-engineering (which already has a "Generators & Meta-Harnesses" section covering Meta-Harness, Self-Harness, HyperAgents plus ~10 tooling repos this list omits: Exo, Continual Harness, metaharness, Omnigent, AutoAgent, harness-evolver). (3) Misses papers named in its own inspiring essay: AHE "Agentic Harness Engineering" (Lin et al. 2026, read-only verifier + manifesto entries) and ScientistOne; also misses "Recursive Harness Self-Improvement" (arXiv 2607.15524, Lee, Zaharia, Tang, Jul 2026). (4) No acceptance/gating category: §4.3 "Verification & Verifiers" is three generic entries (PRM800K, GenRM, "LLMs cannot self-correct"), none about verifying harness diffs. (5) Entries are one-liners; acceptance mechanisms inside Self-Harness/Ouroboros/Meta-Harness are not compared. (6) Ladder is asserted, not argued; L4 "meta-harness" vs L3 boundary is fuzzy (MCE appears at both L1 and L4). (7) Stargazer timeline unavailable (API 404), so growth trend unmeasured. (8) ZH translation drift.
deep_reads.key_insight: The list's own thesis, stated in §5 and Future Directions 5–6, is that "the evaluator and permission control should sit outside the loop that evolves the harness" — the exact premise of an external acceptance layer — yet the list has no category for such a layer, and the only entries with real gates (Self-Harness: accept only after regression testing on held-in and held-out splits; Ouroboros: reviewed-commit gate with deterministic preflight, diff fingerprinting before/after review, blocking multi-model review panel with quorum) each embed the gate inside their own harness. The field, as mapped here, has evaluators and has self-modifiers but no named, harness-agnostic gate between them.
open_gaps: No section or tag for acceptance/verification of self-modifications; §4.3 covers only generic process/generative verifiers
Omits AHE (Lin et al. 2026) and ScientistOne despite both appearing in Weng's source essay, and RHI arXiv 2607.15524
Omits open-source self-improving harness tooling with gate designs (Exo immutable event log, Continual Harness, stanford-iris-lab/meta-harness, metaharness, Omnigent) that ai-boost lists

No comparison of gate mechanics across Self-Harness (regression on held-in/held-out), Ouroboros (fingerprinted reviewed commits + quorum panel), Meta-Harness (Pareto filter), DGM (archive + benchmark score)
No entries on rollback, provenance, diff fingerprinting, gate tampering, or verifier read-only enforcement as first-class topics
AutoHarness, Terminal-Bench, METR report, ADAS survey listed without links (AutoHarness = arXiv 2603.03329)
README_zh.md 3 entries behind README.md
Contribution stream is 100% author self-promotion; no independent curation since Jul 9
Ladder rung boundaries (L3 vs L4; MCE at both L1 and L4) not justified
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer:
Reuse: (a) The L0–L5 ladder is a ready-made taxonomy of diff types an acceptance layer must handle — prompt text, context/memory artifacts, workflow graphs, harness source code, the optimizer itself, and weight updates — and each rung's representative systems are the harnesses a harness-agnostic gate would need adapters for. (b) §4 (PaperBench, MLE-bench, RE-bench, SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, ClawBench with replayable traces, KernelBench fast_p, HAL cost-aware leaderboard) is the catalogue of external signals a gate can consume. (c) §5 is a usable threat model for the gate: Misevolution (ICLR 2026) across memory/tool/workflow paths, RM overoptimization scaling laws, Sycophancy-to-Subterfuge reward tampering, CoT-monitor obfuscation, and METR's finding that benchmark-passing PRs are rarely mergeable — the last directly says a test-pass gate is insufficient for code-level self-modification. (d) The three verified gate designs it points to — Self-Harness (accept only with no regression on held-in AND held-out), Ouroboros (preflight checks, diff fingerprint before/after review, blocking adversarial multi-model panel, sub-quorum cannot pass), Meta-Harness (Pareto frontier over logged traces) — are the concrete prior art to generalize; AHE's read-only verifier/tracer/LLM-config workspace and per-edit "manifesto" (evidence, root cause, fix, predicted impact), missing from the list but in Weng's essay, should be added to that set.

Proves/disproves: nothing empirically. What it documents is that as of Sep 2026 every published acceptance mechanism is bespoke and internal to one harness; no entry, section, or competing list names a separable acceptance layer, which supports the claim that the layer is an open niche rather than a solved one.

Leaves open: what gate semantics generalize across rungs (a regression split works for L0–L3 code/prompt diffs but not obviously for L1 memory growth or L5 weight edits); how to keep the gate itself outside the editable surface (Weng and the list assert this; only AHE and Exo's immutable log operationalize it); and whether any benchmark evaluates gates rather than harnesses. Practical use: seed corpus for a literature review, not a design reference — supplement with ai-boost's Generators & Meta-Harnesses section for tooling.
deep_reads.safety_measures: The repo has none of its own (it is a document). Its stated stance: §5 header and Future Directions 5, 6, 8 — evaluator and permission control must sit outside the loop that evolves the harness; the editable surface, permission control, and security layers must live outside the self-improvement loop; humans move up the stack rather than out. Cited safety literature: Misevolution (Shao et al. ICLR 2026), Skalse reward hacking, Gao RM overoptimization, Krakovna specification gaming, Denison reward tampering, Baker CoT-monitor obfuscation, AgentHarm, METR merge-rate report.

deep_reads.name: AgentDescent
deep_reads.org_or_authors: Danyang Chen (GitHub: Birfy, Shanghai; solo author). ~38% of commits are authored by "Claude" via Claude Code sessions; two minor external contributors (HugoXK: aggregator checkpoint PR; cyanneko: 3 small PRs).
deep_reads.date: Repo created 2026-07-24; v0.1.0 2026-07-26; paper preprint (Zenodo) 2026-09-05; v0.5.0 2026-09-07; sparse-audit layer merged 2026-09-13
deep_reads.last_activity: 2026-09-14 (push to main; PR #187 merged 2026-09-13; open PR #185 for a 20th algorithm port)
deep_reads.venue_or_citations: Zenodo preprint only (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22348027, 26 views / 4 downloads); not on arXiv, not peer-reviewed; no known citations. PyPI package `agentdescent` 0.5.0. 19 forks; 1 external issue in ~55 issues.
deep_reads.mechanism: N workers roll out tasks against git-ledger snapshots and emit keyed diffs plus evidence cards (task, rollout, reward, base version, and a self-verified before/after delta from re-running the trajectory with the diff applied). One aggregator thread runs a five-stage merge: (1) staleness filter on lag eta (Full/Guarded/Reflective policies); (2) conflict resolution: drop the weaker of two same-key diffs on a shared held-out subset, or keep contradictions; (3) fusion: union over disjoint keys, or "reflective merge" where an LLM writes the union of contradicting edits; (4) audit: `AuditScheduler.force_oracle` fires when blast_radius > 0.30 (L1) or per-artifact trust < 0.75, trust updated every merge from cheap-layer vs full-set agreement; priority = blast_radius x uncertainty / trust is computed but nothing drains the queue by default; (5) acceptance: Beta(1+prior_s+s, 1+prior_f+f) posteriors for incumbent and fused candidate on the FULL held-out split, a running per-artifact prior, candidate-only pseudo-counts w=min(1,4|delta|) from contributing cards, Monte-Carlo P(theta_c > theta_b) > 1-delta with delta annealed by version (half-life 64, floor 0.01), ANDed with a hard regression guard cand_rate >= base_rate; commit by CAS on `dev`; promote to `stable` after K regression-free rounds. Governance: L2 (blast_radius <= 0.30, user-declared) merges async; L1 (> 0.30) is oracle-gated on every merge, but with the shipped verifier the "oracle" is the same eval_fn on the same held-out set, so it is free and not independent; L0 is a frozen id list (oracle, audit_budget, merge_permissions, safety_constraints) refused by `assert_mutable`; `FileTree(frozen=["tests/**"])` is enforced at proposal time and by overlaying pristine files after materialisation. Sparse audit (Sept 2026): `AuditedReward` sends ~10% of rollouts to a truth source, records inclusion_prob and verifier_version, PPI++ estimates judge bias and residual sd, and `RectifiedAcceptance` discounts held-out counts by kappa (off by default). Meta-evolution may evolve decision slots including `acceptance` (L1; allowlisted source + Protocol check + smoke test); machinery slots (verifier, ledger, executor, sandbox) are refused.
deep_reads.eval_loop: Per artifact: a held-out validation split that the gate reads (full set, never sub-sampled for commit decisions; sub-samples only rank candidates) and a disjoint test split no gate sees. Acceptance = MC Beta-posterior test + hard regression guard; L1 artifacts additionally pass `_audit` (oracle must strictly beat base). `score_bounded` stops a held-out scan once the candidate cannot reach the floor (decision-equivalent, off by default because it changes the magnitude fed to the prior). Evaluations are cached on (render, task id, environment fingerprint). Self-verification re-runs the worker's own trajectory with the diff applied to produce the card delta. Gate optimism from reusing one fixed val split was measured: val gain exceeds test gain by 0.038 mean over 33 runs (11 ports x 3 seeds; run-level sign test p=0.019; port-level paired t CI [-0.073,-0.004]); no reusable-holdout mechanism exists. Sparse audit adds a reward-level pairing (proxy judge and oracle score the same output) with a Phase-0 kill test per workload. Offline deterministic test suite (2,278 test functions; 162 in the gate/governance/aggregator/audit files passed locally once numpy was installed).
deep_reads.key_results: RQ1 (GEPA/HotpotQA, GLM-5.2, N=4, 16 rollouts pinned, 3 seeds): wall-clock median 790 -> 152 -> 116 s (serial -> sync -> async), 6.8x end to end, per-seed 3.1-9.5x. RQ2 (BBH dyck_languages, one-key InstructionSlot, N=4, 48 rollouts, 4 seeds): keyed union fused 0/47 (defaults) and 0/48 (with tournament); reflective merge fused 42/48 and spent 528 vs 898 model calls (40% fewer, 95% CI 27-54%); quality NOT separable (test 0.233 vs 0.317, paired diff -0.083, CI [-0.279,+0.113]) and the cheaper arm committed less (8 vs 11). RQ3 (11 declarative ports, deepseek-v4-flash, barrier-free N=8, Full staleness, 3 seeds): 10/11 raise mean test score, only 6 significant at 3 seeds; gate optimism -0.038. RQ4 (bbh-keyed, 6 seeds, N=8 and N=4): merge uses 22-32% fewer calls than best-of-N fork and 11% fewer than serial; quality diff +0.005 [-0.186,+0.196] (N=8), -0.017 [-0.133,+0.100] (N=4); fork is FASTER in wall-clock; fused candidate wins only ~20% of contests and the gate refuses the rest. Sparse audit Phase 0 (deepseek-v4-flash judge): judge-vs-oracle disagreement 17.5% HotpotQA, 32.7% BBH, 0.0% GSM8K, 3.7% GSM-Hard, 18.6% MBPP; kappa ~0.60 (32 judged tasks ~ 19 oracle tasks); synthetic end-to-end: delta_hat +0.35 recovered, acceptance rate 0.60 -> 0.37; MBPP judge repair via 2 evolved rules: sigma 0.4747 -> 0.2549, false negatives 3.2% -> 0%. Meta-evolving the `acceptance` slot: 0/3 committed, no LLM-written rule beat the Beta gate. Directory demo: held-out EM 0.167 -> 0.583 on 40 HotpotQA items (12 held out).
deep_reads.limitations: Solo-author preprint, not peer-reviewed; single Python process, one merger thread (75.7% occupancy at N=4), N <= 8, thread workers, local git ledger. Effect sizes: 3-6 seeds on 30-task splits; merging shown non-inferior and cheaper in calls, never better in quality, and slower than fork in wall-clock; RQ4 seeds 3-5 reversed seeds 0-2 and the second batch was run after seeing a favourable first (data-dependent stopping); RQ4 per-run JSON not retained. Bounded staleness is designed, not measured (resync_on_commit on; stale_considered ~0). blast_radius is DECLARED by the caller (`evolve(blast_radius=0.2)`), no estimator exists, although docs say "measured, not declared". With the shipped verifier the L1 "oracle" is the same eval_fn on the same set (free, but not independent). The audit priority queue has no consumer; `L1SerialGate` is not wired; staged rollout/canary is not implemented; no rollback beyond dev/stable hysteresis; no reusable holdout; the MC test is unpaired; candidate-only pseudo-counts come from training-task deltas (an admitted asymmetry); the CAS rebase path does not re-run acceptance. README and paper still claim "zero required dependencies" but HEAD `pyproject.toml` requires numpy (since the audit merge) and `import agentdescent` fails without it, contradicting issue #179's own constraint (v0.5.0 on PyPI was zero-dep). Sparse audit: one model, 11.5% judge self-disagreement noise floor, off by default, rubric run succeeded once; a deadlock in evolve()'s concurrent round path was hit once and is unfixed. Governance is "a design position, not a result: no experiment attacks it"; the meta-evolution source gate is "not a sandbox". `kind=plugin` runs candidate plugin code inside the host process (container advised).
deep_reads.key_insight: Commit decisions must read only full held-out evidence (sub-samples rank, never veto); when the reward is itself a proxy, its disagreement with ground truth should be spent as uncertainty (discount the evidence counts by kappa, bound the rectifier to a verifier_version so it goes stale and conservative when the judge changes) rather than as a bias shift, because a uniform bias cancels in cand-base while sigma_eps^2/n does not; and the thing that judges must be frozen by name, since no measured quantity (blast radius, trust) can tell you an artifact is the oracle.
open_gaps: No independent second measurement in the default path: L1 'oracle' == the same eval_fn on the same held-out set; a real acceptance layer needs an out-of-band verifier contract
blast_radius has no estimator (user-declared constant) despite governance being framed as measured; an acceptance layer needs a real change-impact estimator (files/keys/tasks touched, call graph)
No reusable-holdout / val-rotation: measured 0.038 optimism from reusing one fixed val split across hundreds of decisions
No post-commit monitoring, canary, staged rollout or rollback; promotion is only K-round hysteresis on dev->stable
AuditScheduler priority queue has no consumer; L1SerialGate not wired; multi-merger CAS rebase skips re-acceptance
Governance never adversarially tested; meta-evolution source gate is an allowlist+smoke test, not a sandbox; plugin candidates run in host process
Acceptance policy contract is coupled to the engine's MergeContext/Evolvable/Diff types and runs in-process; no harness-neutral gate service or evidence schema
Sparse audit off by default, single model, one artifact pair in the ordering check, 11.5% judge self-noise floor; judge bias shown to depend on where the artifact is in its evolution
Acceptance test is unpaired MC over two Betas despite both sides scoring the same val set; candidate-only pseudo-counts from training-task deltas
README/paper 'zero dependencies' claim is stale at HEAD (numpy required; lazy import mandated by issue #179 was not done)
deep_reads.relevance_to_acceptance_layer: Directly relevant: this repo is one of the few places where the acceptance gate for a self-modifying agent is treated as the load-bearing component and instrumented as such. What to reuse: (1) the gate contract — `AcceptancePolicy.accept(ctx: MergeContext) -> AcceptDecision` where ctx carries (base_counts, cand_counts, prior, cards, artifact.version, diff) and the decision carries a category ("below-threshold", "oracle-rejected", "committed"), reason, p_improve and observed_delta so `outcomes()` can explain why nothing committed; wrappers (`AdvantageAcceptance`, `StableDistanceAcceptance`, `RectifiedAcceptance`) compose around the base gate via bind/configure hooks rather than replacing it, which is the right shape for a layered gate stack. (2) The invariant that commit decisions read only full held-out counts while cheap sub-samples may only rank — their bug history (regression guard reading the 4-task sample; an exhausted budget silently turning the oracle gate into a sub-sample veto) is exactly the failure class a harness-agnostic layer must design out. (3) The trust signal must be obtainable without spending oracle budget (else circular; they measured trust pinned at 1.0 and zero audits for a whole run). (4) The sparse-audit design for proxy verifiers: pair proxy and oracle at the reward level on the same output; persist inclusion_prob and verifier_version; keep calibration and improvement label pools disjoint by assertion; bind the rectifier to verifier_version so a changed judge makes the gate widen rather than trust stale labels; and the arithmetic that bias cancels in cand-base but sigma_eps^2/n does not, so discount evidence counts (kappa ~0.60 on their data) instead of shifting rates — with `enabled=False` being literally the same call so it can be switched on mid-run. (5) Governance primitives: L0 by name not by metric; frozen paths enforced twice (proposal filter + pristine overlay from outside the tree); `PLUGIN_FROZEN` (hooks, permission config, lockfiles, tests) and an `AGENTDESCENT_NESTED` recursion guard for evolving the host harness itself; decision-plane vs machinery split for meta-evolution. What it proves: a Beta gate with a hard regression guard keeps 11 published algorithms learning under the most aggressive async schedule, and it is the gate — not merging — that preserves quality (fusion wins only ~20% of contests; the gate refuses the rest). It quantifies holdout-reuse optimism (~0.04) and shows LLM-judge error is a property of the judging task (0% on numeric checks vs 18-33% on paraphrase/label/code equivalence), so an acceptance layer should choose per reward type whether calibration is needed. It also gives weak evidence that meta-evolved acceptance rules do not beat a well-chosen statistical gate at small budgets (0/3 commits). What it leaves open for a harness-agnostic layer: the default "oracle" is tautological; blast radius is declared not estimated; there is no post-commit monitoring, canary or rollback; no reusable holdout; the gate lives in-process and is coupled to the engine's types; multi-merger and adversarial cases are unaddressed; and the audit is off by default with single-model evidence. Net: reuse the contract shape, the full-held-out invariant, the kappa-discount rectification and the freeze-by-name rule; do not reuse the L1 oracle path or blast-radius governance as-is.
deep_reads.safety_measures: L0 frozen id list (oracle, audit_budget, merge_permissions, safety_constraints) refused by `assert_mutable` before any rollout, in both sync and async runtimes (tested end to end); `FileTree(frozen=[...])` enforced at proposal time and by overlaying pristine files after materialisation with the test gate invoked from outside the tree; L1 artifacts oracle-gated on every merge (with `oracle-rejected` category); hard regression guard on full held-out rate; trust region / adaptive trust region caps diff size; annealed acceptance risk; dev/stable promotion after K regression-free rounds; CAS commits on a git ledger with full history; for `kind=plugin`: hooks, permission config, lockfiles and tests frozen by default (`PLUGIN_FROZEN`), isolated copies of ~/.claude, ~/.codex, ~/.dsh, `AGENTDESCENT_NESTED=1` so a plugin being evolved cannot start a nested run, container sandbox advised, `plan` quotes call count and waits for a yes before writing back; meta-evolution: machinery slots refused, source gate with import allowlist, dunder refusal, Protocol isinstance and per-slot smoke test; sparse audit: `enabled=False` default, oracle answer never reaches the loop, calibration/improvement pools disjoint by assertion, verifier_version-bound rectifier goes stale on judge change, `VerifierWatch` fingerprint persisted across resume; sandbox leases so abandoned workspaces are reclaimable. Not present: rollback on post-commit regression, canary/staged rollout, adversarial testing of governance.

items.name: RSI-Exam: Measuring Recursive Self-Improvement on Long-Horizon, Executable Research Tasks
items.one_liner: 88 executable research tasks (35 public / 53 private) across 6 domains; agent gets up to 12h on a visible split, submission is replayed once from scratch on a sealed split and that single number is the score.
items.why_relevant: The canonical Sept-2026 'RSI' benchmark. Scores normalized 0.00 (inherited baseline) to 0.60 (frontier-calibrated reference): Opus 5 0.464, GPT-5.6 0.433, GLM 5.3 0.403, Kimi K3 0.382, Grok 4.6 0.367. Visible-to-hidden decay is 11.7-24.7% for every model, i.e. a large fraction of 'self-improvement' is overfitting to the dev split. Site: https://rsi-exam.ai

items.name: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for Recursive Self-Improvement
items.one_liner: 10 frozen research repos across 10 training-algorithm families; 4h on one B300 to rewrite the learning algorithm, rerun from scratch up to 12h, scored by hidden evaluator on a 0-1 scale (0.1 = original algorithm).
items.why_relevant: Directly operationalizes RSI as 'improve the process that produces AI'. Mean 0.166 across 29 configs of 6 systems, best 0.250: agents close under a fifth of the baseline-to-optimum gap. Agents that actually modify the learning mechanism score 0.226 vs 0.126; more reasoning raises willingness to modify algorithms from 8% to 64% of submissions. Explicitly isolates algorithm changes from hyperparameter tuning (positioned as rigorous successor to autoresearch).

items.name: PostTrainBench
items.one_liner: Measures how well CLI agents (Claude Code, Codex CLI) can post-train base LLMs on a single H100 in 10 hours, scored on 7 downstream benchmarks (reasoning, tool use, knowledge, math, health, code).
items.why_relevant: The 'AI improves AI' benchmark with the most traction; finding that data assembly and initialization remain the largest levers (data-centric, not algorithmic gains), which AI4AI-Bench cites as the gap it fills.

items.name: SEAGym: An Evaluation Environment for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Tsinghua. Turns Harbor-compatible benchmarks (Terminal-Bench 2.0, HLE) into self-evolution task streams with train batches, frozen update-validation, held-out ID/OOD views, replay diagnostics, snapshot + cost records; compares ACE, TF-GRPO, AHE under a shared epoch/batch protocol.
items.why_relevant: Core methodological point: a single sequential curve hides whether an update is reusable, overfits recent tasks, raises cost, or harms old behavior. Findings: frequent updates often fail to improve held-out performance, useful intermediate snapshots can collapse later, and source diversity / model backend change harness reliability. Repo: https://github.com/antropy-research/SEAGym

items.name: SEA-Eval: A Benchmark for Evaluating Self-Evolving Agents Beyond Episodic Assessment
items.one_liner: Fudan. Formalizes the Self-Evolving Agent and 'Evolutionary Flywheel'; sequential task streams measure evolutionary gain, stability, and implicit alignment convergence with Success Rate and Token consumption as co-primary metrics.
items.why_relevant: Introduces the 'pseudo-evolution' vs genuine evolution distinction: frameworks with identical success rates differ up to ~30x (31.2x per-task) in tokens; only architectures with effective experience distillation show monotonic token convergence. Argues success rate alone creates a 'capability illusion'.

items.name: EvoHarnessBench: Can Your Agents Keep Pace with an Evolving Harness?
items.one_liner: Salesforce/UNC (Zixuan Ke, Mohit Bansal, Shafiq Joty). 17 multi-stage harness streams, 802 tasks, 520 tools, 42 skills, 62 agents; non-stationarity is placed in the harness itself rather than the task stream.
items.why_relevant: Names 'harness-induced forgetting': harness expansion alone degrades performance on previously solved tasks. Adaptation gains are inconsistent across evolution stages, and retention and adaptation pull in different directions. Directly relevant to any framework that keeps adding skills/tools.

items.name: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
items.one_liner: Shifts the unit of evaluation to runnable infrastructure: Creation (from minimal seed + few cases) then Evolution (revise own harness from downstream feedback); 6 creator LLMs, 4 domains, 5 downstream benchmarks, 2,207 instances, capability + token cost.
items.why_relevant: Generated harnesses trail human-engineered references on code and search/research, match or exceed on writing and ML experimentation. Evolution gains exist but are unstable, transfer only partially to held-out tasks, and depend strongly on the model executing the harness (limited cross-model transfer).

items.name: MemEvoBench: Benchmarking Memory MisEvolution in LLM Agents
items.one_liner: First benchmark for long-horizon memory safety under adversarial memory injection, noisy tool outputs, and biased feedback: QA tasks over 7 domains / 36 risk types plus workflow tasks from 20 Agent-SafetyBench environments with mixed benign/misleading memory pools.
items.why_relevant: Shows memory evolution itself is a major contributor to safety degradation and that static prompt defenses are insufficient; establishes 'misevolution' as a failure class self-improving loops must measure. Repo: https://github.com/xiewwee11/MemEvoBench

items.name: Practice Makes Unsafe: Skill Misevolution in Self-Improving LLM Agents (SkillMisevo-Gym / SkillMisevo-Bench)
items.one_liner: Lifecycle-aware harness that versions skill state across 4 agent frameworks and 6 evolution methods; frozen benchmark from malicious exposure to carryover tasks with concept-aligned benign tasks and 9 lifecycle metrics; 25 configs x 525 tasks x 25 episodes.
items.why_relevant: All 21 evolved configurations author unsafe artifacts; 15 reach fresh-session harm. Unsafe success becomes reusable policy after the triggering input is gone because evolution optimizes outcomes, not procedure safety. SafeEvolve wrapper cuts unsafe retrieval / fresh-session harm by 26.7 / 17.3 pp at 0.4-pt utility cost.

items.name: FinEvo-Bench: A Longitudinal Benchmark for Self-Evolving Agents in Professional Financial Workflows
items.one_liner: 120 real-case-grounded multi-file tasks in 20 business scenes across 6 financial domains; each scene has 6 related cases sharing a professional procedure and reviewed rubric; interleaved streams with state-reset controls isolate cross-task self-evolution gain.
items.why_relevant: A paired (evolution on/off, state-reset) protocol is the pattern the critique papers demand; open-ended outputs scored for quality and compliance rather than pass/fail.

items.name: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
items.one_liner: RELAI tech report (Wang, Kattakinda, Feizi). Two-phase continual evaluation on hard Terminal-Bench 2.0 tasks comparing GEPA, Meta Harness, and RELAI-VCL under identical optimization budgets.
items.why_relevant: All three beat baseline in the static one-shot setting; once new tasks arrive they diverge: GEPA transfers below the unoptimized baseline, Meta Harness transfers but cannot improve with a second budget, only RELAI-VCL compounds (lifelong avg pass 76.4% vs 66.0 GEPA, 64.6 Meta Harness, 58.7 baseline). Vendor-authored, but the phase-2 protocol is the point. Artifacts: https://github.com/relai-ai/Continual-Learning-Terminal-Bench

items.name: Adaptive Auto-Harness: Sustained Self-Improvement for Agentic System Deployment on Open-Ended Task Streams
items.one_liner: Emory/Amazon/PSU/UIUC. Shows a single densely-updated harness (A-Evolve, GEPA, Meta-Harness style) is brittle on open-ended streams: accuracy peaks early then declines; proposes decomposing gap into evolution vs adaptation loss with a harness tree and solve-time routing.
items.why_relevant: Documents the peak-then-decay curve that fixed-benchmark evaluations never show; argues heterogeneous streams need multiple harnesses plus routing rather than one monolithic evolving harness.

items.name: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
items.one_liner: AI2 / UW (Hajishirzi, Tsvetkov, Dasigi, Teng Xiao). Argues harness evolution is an iterative search and must be compared with task-level search baselines under matched feedback and inference budgets, on held-out tasks rather than the search benchmark.
items.why_relevant: The most-cited critique: on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.6, automatic harness evolution does not consistently outperform simple test-time scaling and shows limited generalization. Reported gains risk being 'more search' plus overfitting to the public benchmark used for both search and eval.

items.name: Simple Baselines are Competitive with Code Evolution (Gideoni, Risi, Gal; ICLR 2026)
items.one_liner: Two trivial baselines match or exceed sophisticated LLM code-evolution pipelines on mathematical bounds, agentic scaffold design, and ML competitions.
items.why_relevant: Establishes that search space and domain knowledge in the prompt, not the evolution pipeline, dictate the performance ceiling; explicitly calls for more rigorous evaluation of self-improving/evolutionary systems. This is the 'trivial-baselines' paper the critique wave builds on.

items.name: What Do Evolutionary Coding Agents Evolve? (EvoTrace / EvoReplay)
items.one_liner: Pelleriti, Pokutta et al. EvoTrace: structured traces (programs, parent-child graph, prompts, scores, evaluator metadata) over 4 evolutionary frameworks and 16 math/algorithm tasks; EvoReplay reconstructs local search states and runs controlled interventions.
items.why_relevant: Separates gains from new algorithmic structure vs constant re-tuning vs recombination vs evaluator overfitting. Most score gains come from a small subset of edit types, and ~30% of lines added during search are byte-identical re-introductions of previously deleted lines. Mechanism auditing, not best-score, is the takeaway.

items.name: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit: Disentangling Evolution Capabilities in Self-Evolving LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Minhua Lin + 16 (PSU/Amazon et al.). Splits self-evolution into harness-updating (produce useful persistent updates) and harness-benefit (gain from them at solve time).
items.why_relevant: Harness-updating is flat across model tiers (Qwen3.5-9B produces updates comparable to Claude Opus 4.6); harness-benefit is non-monotonic, peaking at mid-tier models and shrinking for strong models. Implication: the evolving model and the executing model should be chosen separately, and strong-model results understate/overstate harness value.

items.name: Are Online Skill and Memory Modules Always Worth Their Tokens? A Budget-Constrained Study of Web Agents
items.one_liner: Re-evaluates online skill and workflow-memory modules under a fixed total inference budget across 3 WebArena domains and 3 models (Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-5.4-mini, Qwen 3.6-27B), plus WorkArena-L1.
items.why_relevant: Vanilla actor matches or beats all three augmentation methods in aggregate success while often using fewer tokens; apparent gains vanish against a budget-matched actor. Cost accounting is a first-order evaluation requirement.

items.name: Demystifying Agent Skills: Why They Work - Until They Don't
items.one_liner: 528 paired triples across SkillsBench (144), Terminal-Bench 2.0 (186), Terminal-Bench-Pro (198); controlled study of representation, outcome annotation, retrieval difficulty, cross-framework robustness.
items.why_relevant: Skills work mainly as procedural anchors (65.7% of successes) not knowledge injection (4.5%); retrieval precision collapses from 29.6% (5-skill pool) to 3.3% (100-skill pool); skills fail under brittle assumptions or incompatible contexts. Warns that growing skill libraries in self-evolving loops self-sabotage via retrieval. Repo: https://github.com/zhiyuanjiang04/demystify-agent-skills

items.name: SkillsBench: Benchmarking How Well Agent Skills Work Across Diverse Tasks
items.one_liner: 87 tasks across 8 domains with curated skills and deterministic verifiers; paper arXiv 2602.12670.
items.why_relevant: The reference substrate for skill studies: curated skills raise pass rate 33.9% -> 50.5% (+16.6 pp), which sets the bar that self-generated/evolved skills are then measured against (CTA finds +0.3 pp on SWE-Skills-Bench).

items.name: Counterfactual Trace Auditing of LLM Agent Skills
items.one_liner: Pairs each with-skill trace against a without-skill trace on the same task, segments and aligns goal-directed phases, emits structured Skill Influence Pattern annotations describing behavioral effect rather than only outcome.
items.why_relevant: On SWE-Skills-Bench with Claude across 49 tasks, pass rate moved only +0.3 pp on average, yet behavior changed substantively. Gives a template for auditing whether an evolved artifact actually altered agent behavior, not just the aggregate score.

items.name: Evo-Bench: Can Language Models Improve Agent Harness?
items.one_liner: RUC / Nanbeige. 608 harness-sensitive tasks from 5 benchmarks across Search, Office, General; long-horizon protocol measures whether a model can diagnose, rewrite and improve an executable harness while isolating harness gains from base-model strength and preventing task overfit.
items.why_relevant: Top of 9 frontier/open models gain up to 16.6 absolute points, approaching human-engineered baselines; treats harness-evolving as a measurable model capability. Repo: https://github.com/RUCAIBox/Evo-Bench

items.name: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
items.one_liner: Scale AI. Optimizer LLM receives a seed harness, graded feedback, and a fixed target-evaluation budget; nominated candidate scored by normalized gain over seed on a held-out test partition under expensive, stochastic evaluation.
items.why_relevant: Explicitly budgets evaluations and scores on held-out partitions (the two fixes the AI2 critique asks for); reveals substantial variation across models and tasks.

items.name: EvoAgentBench: Benchmarking Agent Self-Evolution via Ability Transfer
items.one_liner: Ability Graph where edges are shared reusable procedures (search strategy, debugging routine, validation workflow); 1006 train + 367 test tasks over web research, algorithmic reasoning, SWE, knowledge work.
items.why_relevant: Isolates procedural transfer specifically, the mechanism most self-evolution frameworks claim. Repo: https://github.com/EverMind-AI/EvoAgentBench

items.name: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents
items.one_liner: Gen-Verse (Mengdi Wang, Ling Yang). 26 scenarios / 204 episodes of fresh-session task sequences with retained experience toggled on/off under matched conditions; 7 base models x 4 frameworks.
items.why_relevant: Improvement from retained experience is real but uneven across memory, procedural reuse, information gathering and update; the on/off matched-condition design is the minimal causal test for 'does experience help'. Repo: https://github.com/Gen-Verse/PAST-Bench

items.name: GDPevo: Evaluating Agent Self-Evolution on Real Business Tasks
items.one_liner: Evolution-native benchmark with 'rule hybridization': atomic business rules distributed across 5 train tasks and recombined in 5 held-out tests per group (120 tasks, 12 groups; CRM/ERP/finance/healthcare/legal).
items.why_relevant: Makes test-time gains attributable to what was learned; self-evolution adds up to +16.44 pp held-out accuracy but best evolved agents remain far below the 91.6% fully-informed oracle. Repo: https://github.com/Prism-Shadow/GDPevo

items.name: AIDE²: First Evidence of Recursive Self-Improvement (Weco AI)
items.one_liner: Outer loop (Opus 4.7) rewrote the inner autoresearch agent's harness for 100 iterations over 8 days (~90% rejected, 7 survivors); AIDE85 beat the 2-year hand-tuned baseline on held-out MLE-Bench Lite, ALE-Bench Lite, WeatherBench 2, KernelBench; reward hacking on KernelBench fell 63% -> 34%.
items.why_relevant: The hottest RSI claim of summer 2026 and the empirical foil for the critique papers. Self-reported, no peer review; authors concede no 'ignition' (discovered agent did not improve the outer loop) and no evidence of takeoff. Discovered: bandit search with fork-on-stall, 16x context compression, 3-layer anti-reward-hacking.

items.name: karpathy/autoresearch
items.one_liner: AI agents running research on single-GPU nanochat training automatically; modify -> verify -> keep/discard loop.
items.why_relevant: The cultural substrate for the 2026 RSI wave; AI4AI-Bench and RSI-Exam position themselves as rigorous successors (full repos, hidden evaluators, algorithm-vs-hyperparameter isolation). Spawned thousands of derivative loops (AutoResearchClaw 14.4k, pi-autoresearch 8k, darwin-skill 6k).

items.name: AI's recursive self-improvement might not come so quickly after all (MIT Technology Review)
items.one_liner: Covers a Princeton study (Kapoor et al.) giving Claude Opus 4.8 six days and $3,000 to reproduce two unpublished NeurIPS 2026 papers: engineering completed, papers rejected for lacking novelty and bizarre experimental choices.
items.why_relevant: Sets the skeptical mainstream framing: agents are 'unambiguously bad at carrying out the research itself'; Jack Clark calls lack of creativity a bearish signal on short RSI timelines. Bottlenecks named: exploring alternatives, backtracking, resource management.

items.name: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: From Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops
items.one_liner: Survey of 1,250 arXiv papers (2024-2026) along 'what improves' and 'loop-closure degree'; v2 2026-09-06.
items.why_relevant: Supplies the vocabulary now used in discourse: 'bounded self-refinement' (convergent, evaluable, industrial) vs open-ended RSI (bounded by grounding, collapse dynamics, compute). Identifies two unsolved bottlenecks, the verification problem (hierarchy from formal verifiers down to self-assessment) and the prior problem (choosing what to evaluate), and calls governance-grade measurement of self-improvement the most underpopulated area.

items.name: The Red Queen Gödel Machine: Co-Evolving Agents and Their Evaluators
items.one_liner: Cambridge MLSys (Iacob et al.). Co-evolves learned evaluators with self-improving agents so the bar rises as the agent improves; applied to coding, paper writing, proof generation.
items.why_relevant: Addresses the stationary-evaluator assumption that every fixed-benchmark RSI eval makes; frames benchmark saturation and reward hacking as the central obstacle to measuring genuine self-improvement.

items.name: Self-Evolving Agents with Anytime-Valid Certificates
items.one_liner: JPMorgan (Sengupta). Confines self-modification to a steering adapter + versioned harness around a frozen base; each modification admitted only via an anytime-valid gate emitting an auditable certificate against a fixed error budget; +4/+5 on a 52-task SWE-bench Verified subset.
items.why_relevant: Companion to PACE (arXiv 2606.08106): statistically valid acceptance tests for harness updates, the missing piece behind 'snapshot collapse' and 'keep/discard' loops that accept noise.

items.name: Harness-Bench: Measuring Harness Effects across Models in Realistic Agent Workflows
items.one_liner: Diagnostic benchmark for configuration-level harness effects across model backends under shared environments, budgets and protocols while preserving each harness's native execution.
items.why_relevant: Provides the harness-vs-model factorization needed to attribute self-evolution gains; baseline for the cross-model non-transfer that HarnessDev and Lin et al. report.

items.name: HarnessEvolve: Learning from Reference Trajectories for Reliable Agent Self-Evolution
items.one_liner: Names three failure modes of self-evolving agents (credit-assignment failure, shortcut learning, catastrophic forgetting); uses ground-truth-conditioned reference trajectories to extract error signals and decouples execution / evaluation / optimization / gating agents.
items.why_relevant: A method paper that adopts the critics' diagnosis (gating, forgetting, shortcut learning) as its design spec; useful as a checklist of what a loop must defend against.

items.name: ICLR 2026 Workshop on AI with Recursive Self-Improvement
items.one_liner: Organized by Zhuge, Zeng, Zhu, Sherry Yang, Chandra, Schmidhuber et al.; five lenses: what changes, temporal characteristics, mechanisms, deployment contexts, measurable evidence of improvement.
items.why_relevant: Where much of the 2026 RSI-eval community coalesced; emphasis on auditable, production-demonstrable loops over speculative approaches.

items.name: Weco AI Claims Its AIDE² Loop Beat Two Years of Human Tuning in Eight Days - a Narrow, Self-Reported Result
items.one_liner: Critique framing AIDE² as a bounded engineering result: outer loop tunes an inner ML-research agent on pre-specified benchmarks, first-party report, not peer reviewed.
items.why_relevant: Representative of the pushback on the summer's headline RSI claim; pairs with the AlphaSignal thread (x.com/AlphaSignalAI/status/2077810068146270627) questioning whether the external benchmark used to decide what stayed was truly held out.

items.name: lobehub/awesome-rsi
items.one_liner: Curated RSI research map (models, agents, harnesses, embodied, automated AI R&D, benchmarks, safety) with explicit operational definitions of self-refinement vs persistent vs recursive self-improvement vs 'RSI substrate'.
items.why_relevant: Most-starred list literally named awesome-rsi; its 'Harness-level RSI' and 'Direct RSI & Self-Improvement Evaluations' sections (RSIBench-Data, PostTrainBench, LongWoF-Bench, RSI-Bench) are the cleanest entry point for harness-verification work.

items.name: KaiWU5/Awesome-AI4AI
items.one_liner: AI4AI survey companion: 223 papers on long-horizon agents, benchmarks, harness design and RSI, auto-refreshed every Monday with citation/star rankings and a monthly top-11 news digest; companion survey on Preprints.org 2026-08-28.
items.why_relevant: Only list with live citation velocity (Meta-Harness 27 cites/mo, ACE 26.6) and a curated news feed tying model releases (GPT-6 Astra, Fable 5.1, Gemini 3.8) to harness papers; good for 'what is hot' signal.

items.name: leezythu/Awesome-Harness-Self-Improvement
items.one_liner: EN/ZH reading list on harness engineering for RSI, organized around an 'Optimization Ladder' L0 prompts -> L1 context/memory -> L2 workflow -> L3 harness code -> L4 meta-harness -> L5 harness+weights, plus 'Evaluators That Close the Loop' and 'When Self-Improvement Goes Wrong'.
items.why_relevant: The most framework-designer-oriented taxonomy; its stated rule that 'the evaluator and permission control should sit outside the loop that evolves the harness' and its 8 open problems (weak evaluators, diversity collapse, reward hacking, broken abstraction boundaries) map directly onto self-evolving-harness verification.

items.name: pinkbubblebubble/awesome-rsi
items.one_liner: Evidence-aware RSI collection with RSI / Self-improvement / Enabler badges, a 'Safety harness and evaluator evolution' section, and a checklist 'What a convincing RSI evaluation should report'.
items.why_relevant: Its reporting checklist (multi-generation performance incl. regressions, held-out evaluator the system cannot rewrite, ablations, generalization, compute/trajectories/failed attempts, isolation/rollback/human interventions) is a ready-made verification spec; also the most complete index of Sept-2026 safety-side harness papers (HackProbe, EvoUndo, Auditing Harness Tampering, Safe Harness Self-Evolution).

items.name: wkqdzkd/Awesome-Reliable-Self-Evolving-Agents
items.one_liner: Companion to the Tencent Hunyuan / ZJU survey 'Diving into Reliable Self-Evolving Agents' (OpenReview Aug 10, Preprints.org Sep 11): 549 papers classified L0 Output / L1 Model / L2 Scaffold / L3 Improver / L4 Criterion, each with a characteristic failure (self-confirmation, model collapse, scaffold overfitting, metric capture, criterion drift).
items.why_relevant: Most-starred RSI-specific list; defines RSI structurally as beginning at L3 (improver mutable) and insists the evidence source and acceptance gate stay outside the update boundary, with a 'Cross-Level Reliability: Evidence, Acceptance, and Control' section on audit independence.

items.name: wannabeyourfriend/awesome-harness-evolution
items.one_liner: Brand-new (Sep 12) 104-work harness-evolution list with a research timeline, sections for Meta-Harness & Recursive Evolution, Model-Harness Co-Evolution, Harness-Engineering Capability benchmarks (HarnessDev, HarnessOpt-Bench, Evo-Bench, EvoHarnessBench, LoopArena, LoopsBench, SEAGym) and an explicit 'Evidence & Critique' section.
items.why_relevant: The only list that groups the skeptical papers (Rethinking Harness Evolution Eval, Harness Updating != Benefit, Do Agent Optimizers Compound?, Budget-Splitting Trap, Safe Harness Self-Evolution theory) into one section; best single index for the Aug-Sep 2026 harness benchmarks.

items.name: D2I-ai/awesome-recursive-self-improving-agents
items.one_liner: Living index for the survey 'The Path to Recursive Self-Improving Agents': taxonomy by improved component (harness / data system / trainer / cross-component) and an L1-L5 grading (Manual, Assisted, Programmatic, Bounded RSI, General RSI) keyed on autonomous proposal, implementation, validation, mutable improvement mechanism, and domain generality.
items.why_relevant: Its L3-vs-L4 boundary (can the system rewrite its own improvement mechanism?) and open problems (observable/modifiable infra, protecting governance components with rollback and incident logs) are directly usable as capability-grading criteria for a self-evolving harness.

items.name: FrontisAI/Awesome-Self-Improving-Agents
items.one_liner: Survey site + list 'Self-Improving Agents in the Era of Experience: From Self- to Meta-Evolution', with a rolling 7-day 'Latest additions' table mapped to survey chapters (Harness as Experience Infrastructure, Skills, Meta-Evolving Agents, Safety as Moving Attack Surface).
items.why_relevant: Fastest-updating feed: the Sep 11 snapshot alone added MetaRSI, SkillAdam, NeoHorse-1, RobustSGPO, Ecdysis, Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models, HackProbe; Frontis.AI also co-authored OpenRSI/Frontis-MA1.

items.name: selfimproving-agent/Awesome-Self-Improving-Agents
items.one_liner: Survey-backed bibliography of self-improvement in foundation-model agentic systems with 'Measuring Improvement' and 'Benchmarking Improvement' subsections and a table of Aug-2026 RSI systems with code stars (Meta^n, J-Zero).
items.why_relevant: Second most-starred self-improving-agents list; useful as the 'where the community looks' baseline and for its evaluation subsections.

items.name: ANative-Lab/Awesome-Self-Evolving-Agents
items.one_liner: Companion to 'A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents' (single-agent / multi-agent / domain-specific optimisation / evaluation incl. safety for lifelong agents).
items.why_relevant: By far the most-starred list in the space: shows community attention still flows to the 'self-evolving agents' vocabulary rather than 'RSI'; less harness-verification depth than the 2026 RSI lists.

items.name: ai-boost/awesome-harness-engineering
items.one_liner: Practitioner-oriented harness-engineering list (tools, patterns, evals, memory, MCP, permissions, observability, orchestration); wannabeyourfriend/awesome-harness-evolution follows its layout.
items.why_relevant: Most-starred harness list overall (4.2k) - the practitioner audience a self-evolving-harness framework would ship to; not RSI-specific.

items.name: Shiyao-Huang/awesome-agent-evolution
items.one_liner: Chinese-language 'open survey and evidence map' for self-evolving agents framed as a change loop over prompts/memory/workflows/code/weights, with an evidence pipeline and 'Evolve-AGI Index'.
items.why_relevant: Evidence-pipeline framing (what counts as evidence of evolution) complements the English lists; strong CN-community signal.

items.name: EvoMap/awesome-agent-evolution
items.one_liner: Broad agent-evolution directory (memory systems, protocols, platforms, safety, embodied) maintained by EvoMap, whose 'Genes' consolidated from verifier-confirmed trajectories are evaluated in LongWoF-Bench.
items.why_relevant: Product-adjacent list; moderate relevance, but EvoMap's verified-experience-provenance idea (LongWoF-Bench, arXiv 2608.23200) is relevant to verification design.

items.name: Liuziyu77/Awesome-RSI
items.one_liner: 'From Experience to Systems to Models' taxonomy (Experience Accumulation / System Modification / Model Parameters) with benchmark, evaluation-study, model-checkpoint and company/lab sections.
items.why_relevant: Its 'Evaluation Studies' table surfaces the two key audit papers (Phantom Gains, Fragility of Self-Improving Agents) with practical takeaways; also lists MetaRSI, SafeEvolve, RSI-Exam, HarnessDev.

items.name: theseus-labs-rsi/awesome-rsi
items.one_liner: 519-paper taxonomy organized by an L1-L5 autonomy roadmap (improvement execution -> strategies -> future learning experience -> deployment adaptation -> meta-improvement), companion to 'The Last AI Built by Humans' (arXiv 2609.11873).
items.why_relevant: Newest large taxonomy with a strict source-verification update policy; its 'Updated-Object Families' and improvement-loop anatomy are useful for scoping what a harness may mutate.

items.name: iSEngLab/Awesome-Self-Evolving-Coding-Agents
items.one_liner: Coding-agent-specific self-evolution list: framework / memory / skill-tool / model / workflow / environment self-evolution, plus benchmarks and self-evolving coding products.
items.why_relevant: Indexes Harness Updating != Benefit and Rethinking Harness Evolution Eval in a software-engineering context; relevant if the harness targets coding agents.

items.name: Picrew/awesome-rsi
items.one_liner: RSI list with per-entry 'Boundary' notes stating exactly what recursion acts on (e.g. Meta^n, J-Zero) and reading paths that ask 'does the revised agent participate in its next improvement?'.
items.why_relevant: Boundary-labeling discipline is a good model for how a framework should document its own mutable surface.

items.name: MetaRSI / RSI2: A Meta-Recursive Self-Improving System for RSI Systems Themselves
items.one_liner: Three typed operators (Data-RSI, Harness-RSI over 5 slots: system prompt, memory, tools, skills, MCP; Model-RSI) sharing one 7-stage loop kernel, with a meta-agent that rewrites operator scheduling each 'term' under contract-bounded authority; +10.9 avg on Qwen3.5-35B (SWE-bench, Terminal-Bench, GPQA, AIME), +7.3 for GPT-5.6 Sol / Opus 5 from harness ops alone.
items.why_relevant: The hottest Sept-2026 RSI claim and the first to explicitly formalize 'authority boundaries' to stop the loop from gaming its evaluator; institution not stated (flagged N/S by awesome-harness-evolution) - treat results as unreplicated.

items.name: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?
items.one_liner: ByteDance Seed / SUTD / Georgia Tech benchmark with Creation (build a runnable harness from a minimal seed) and Evolution stages; 6 frontier models, 4 domains, 2,207 held-out instances. Model-built harnesses match or beat human references on writing and ML but lag on code and search; evolution gains are unstable.
items.why_relevant: Turns 'harness engineering' into a scoreable model capability with held-out evaluation - the protocol a self-evolving-harness framework will be judged against.

items.name: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
items.one_liner: UW / AI2 (Wang, Hajishirzi, Tsvetkov, Dasigi et al.): harness evolution is itself iterative search and must be compared to test-time-scaling/discovery baselines under matched feedback and inference budgets; on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with GPT-5.4 and Opus 4.6 it does not consistently win and generalizes poorly to held-out tasks.
items.why_relevant: The central skeptical counterweight every list cites; any framework claiming harness-evolution gains must now report matched-budget baselines and held-out generalization.

items.name: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit: Disentangling Evolution Capabilities in Self-Evolving LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Separates harness-updating (producing useful persistent updates) from harness-benefit (actually using them); updating is flat across model tiers, benefit is non-monotonic (mid-tier gains most, weak models fail at activation/adherence); many automated updates silently degrade without a benefit gate. Code in A-EVO-Lab/a-evolve.
items.why_relevant: Argues for a 'benefit gate' rather than counting updates - a concrete verification primitive for self-evolving harnesses.
