items.name: EVOHARNESSBENCH: Can Your Agents Keep Pace with an Evolving Harness?
items.one_liner: Salesforce Research / UNC / UW-Madison benchmark placing non-stationarity in the harness (17 multi-stage streams, 802 tasks, 520 tools, 42 skills, 62 agents) and measuring retention, adaptation and 'harness-induced forgetting'.
items.why_relevant: First benchmark for the failure mode where evolving the harness itself breaks the agent; already contested (claims it is a retrieval-over-capabilities effect).

items.name: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
items.one_liner: Guibin Zhang et al.: a 27B 'harness intelligence' model synthesizes task-adaptive harnesses on the fly under a fixed four-module protocol, repairs them, and self-evolves from an archive; DeepSeek-V4-Flash + JIT-Agent beats GPT-5.6 on DeepSearchQA (+9.1) and OdysseyBench (+4.3). Code bingreeky/JIT (466 stars).
items.why_relevant: Most-starred Aug-2026 harness-evolution code release; the 'harness as machine-generatable artifact' framing, plus the public critique that the gain may be a base-model confound.

items.name: RSI-Exam: Measuring Recursive Self-Improvement on Long-Horizon, Executable Research Tasks
items.one_liner: Stanford / Berkeley / CMU / Oxford benchmark (rsi-exam.ai): 88 tasks in 6 domains (35 public, 53 private); agent gets a weak working method and up to 12h on a visible split, submission is replayed once on a sealed split; 0-1 score anchored at baseline 0 / frontier 0.6 / upper bound 1.0. Leaderboard: GPT-6-astra (codex) 0.513, Opus 5 (claude code) 0.464, GPT-5.6-sol 0.433.
items.why_relevant: The de-facto 'direct RSI' leaderboard of Sept 2026; its hidden-replay design and 90+ rubric checks for leakage are the reference for holdout-based verification.

items.name: Meta^n: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth
items.one_liner: Minnesota NLP (Kim, Kang): keeps a fixed meta-operation and recurses on its own products, reading solver-stack traces and code to write the next layer of preprocessing + helpers; claims wins on 8 benchmark families and the only non-zero ARC-AGI-2 score among self-improving agents.
items.why_relevant: Argues prior self-modifying agents cap meta-depth at ~2; relevant to how deep a harness may recurse while staying auditable.

items.name: SkillAdam: Stable and Efficient Skill Evolution for Agents
items.one_liner: RUC datalab: Adam-analogue optimizer for SKILL.md documents - an optimization memory (first moment) stabilizes edit direction, a volatility-driven edit budget (second moment) scales update size; SOTA on 7 benchmarks with fewer iterations; ships as a Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / Copilot plugin.
items.why_relevant: Directly a self-evolving-harness component with validation-before-apply; practical reference for bounded, budgeted skill edits.

items.name: SafeEvolve: Harness-Policy Co-Evolution from Agent Experience for Safety Alignment
items.one_liner: Converts trajectory-level safety evidence into bounded, reversible component-level harness updates (safety prompt + hierarchical SkillBank) and co-trains the policy via harness-use SFT then harness-augmented RL; 3x ASR reduction on AgentDojo with utility up 59.8 -> 61.9 on Qwen3.5-4B.
items.why_relevant: Shows harness evolution used for safety, and notes co-evolution exposes new risks on both sides; auditable/reversible artifacts are the design pattern.

items.name: HarnessForge: Joint Harness and Policy Evolution for Adaptive Agent Systems
items.one_liner: Chen, Lv, Zhang, Chang, Zhou: models an agent as a harness-policy pair with fault-guided harness tailoring and harness-conditioned policy alignment; up to +12.0% over strongest baseline on 5 benchmarks with Qwen3-4B/8B.
items.why_relevant: Early formalization of the harness-policy adaptation space that SafeEvolve and WHALE build on; low stars, moderate heat.

items.name: J-Zero: Unified Challenger-Solver-Judge Co-Evolution from Zero Data
items.one_liner: KAIST (Chu, Jeon, Yang): extends zero-data self-play to unverifiable domains by co-evolving a Judge from structurally constructed preference pairs alongside Challenger and Solver.
items.why_relevant: Model-level RSI where the evaluator itself evolves (L4 criterion-level in wkqdzkd's taxonomy) - the regime where 'who grades the grader' verification matters most.

items.name: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement
items.one_liner: 33-author survey/position (Theseus Labs) proposing an L1-L5 autonomy roadmap and a Headroom-Closed Index (HCI) to quantify how much of a benchmark's headroom current LLMs have closed; covers science, embodied and SWE scenarios.
items.why_relevant: Sets the vocabulary for 'genuine' vs bounded RSI that lists (theseus, FrontisAI) adopted within a day of release.

items.name: Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null
items.one_liner: Shows apparent self-improvement gains can be reproduced by frozen controls and measurement noise; prescribes frozen-control baselines and repeated measurement.
items.why_relevant: A minimal audit protocol (measured null) that any self-evolving harness evaluation should include.

items.name: On the Fragility of Self-Improving Agents: Variance, Task Order, and Underspecification
items.one_liner: Salesforce AI Research: memory-based self-improving agents' results swing with seeds, task order and feedback specification.
items.why_relevant: Motivates multi-seed, order-randomized, spec-ablated evaluation for harness evolution claims.

items.name: Do Agent Optimizers Compound? A Continual-Learning Evaluation on Terminal-Bench 2.0
items.one_liner: Tests whether successive optimization rounds compound; finds most reported gains are one-shot against a fixed benchmark.
items.why_relevant: Directly challenges the 'recursive' premise; longitudinal multi-round measurement is the missing verification.

items.name: Safe Harness Self-Evolution: A Theoretical Analysis of Feasibility and Limits
items.one_liner: Derives finite-data conditions under which improving harness updates can be selected and adopted while bounding regressions on retained tasks, and where self-evolution provably breaks down.
items.why_relevant: First theory result for acceptance gates in harness evolution; gives sample-size conditions for a promotion test.

items.name: Auditing Harness Tampering in Self-Improving Agents
items.one_liner: Defines authorization, provenance and completeness failures for harness edits and audits real self-improvement trajectories for tampering.
items.why_relevant: Provides a failure taxonomy for the exact thing a self-evolving harness verifier must catch.

items.name: Harness-agnostic Detection and Immunization of Reward Hacking in Self-Evolving LMs (HackProbe)
items.one_liner: Black-box monitor with a secret comparison core and risk-aware candidate reselection that works across harnesses.
items.why_relevant: Pattern for keeping a hidden verifier outside the loop's writable surface.

items.name: Where Does Harness-Optimization Value Live? Localized Gains and the Budget-Splitting Trap
items.one_liner: Finds harness-optimization gains are localized and that splitting evaluation budget across stages of the loop is a trap.
items.why_relevant: Budget-allocation critique of the standard evolve-then-evaluate loop; affects how a framework should spend verification compute.

items.name: NeoHorse-1: Towards RSI via Agentic Post-Training with Routing Harness
items.one_liner: TokenRhythm open-weight 4B/9B models (Apache 2.0) whose routing-harness trajectories become curricula and on-policy distillation data that shape the next training mixture.
items.why_relevant: Most-starred Sept-2026 open-weight 'RSI' model release; example of harness -> weights loop in the open.

items.name: WHALE: A Simple Recipe for Joint Harness-Weight Optimization
items.one_liner: Alternates model-weight updates with executable harness search; shares authors with Meta-Harness (Stanford IRIS) and is positioned as its successor; KaiWU5 top-11 story for Aug 31.
items.why_relevant: Signals frontier academic groups moving from harness-only to joint harness+weight loops (leezythu's L5).

items.name: Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement (Lilian Weng)
items.one_liner: Survey post framing harness engineering as the near-term path to RSI: design patterns, context/workflow optimization, self-improving harnesses.
items.why_relevant: Widely cited framing piece (listed by lobehub); shapes how practitioners talk about harness-level RSI.

items.name: ICLR 2026 Workshop on AI with Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI 2026)
items.one_liner: First dedicated RSI workshop (Rio, Apr 26 2026): 110 accepted papers, 4 orals (Agent0, Contextual Drag, Meta-learning Agentic Memory, PostTrainBench), 21 spotlights; organized by Mingchen Zhuge (KAUST), Ailing Zeng, Deyao Zhu (ByteDance), Rong Zou (Apple), Sherry Yang (NYU/DeepMind), Vikas Chandra (Meta), Jürgen Schmidhuber; speakers Clune, Finn, Levine, Kirsch, Yu Su.
items.why_relevant: Canonical venue that made 'RSI' a mainstream ML term in 2026; its 'six lenses' framing (what/when/how changes, domain, safety, evaluation) and its statement that RSI 'is becoming a concrete systems problem' define the academic discourse. Accepted-papers list: https://recursive-workshop.github.io/papers.html

items.name: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: From Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops (arXiv 2607.07663)
items.one_liner: 1,250-paper survey (Chen, Wang, Qu; UCR/AlphaAvatar/IIT; v2 Sept 6 2026) with a 4x3 taxonomy (deployment-time self-evolution / training-time self-iteration / self-evaluation / auto-research × human-in/on/out-of-loop) and a 4-rung verification hierarchy: formal verifiers > execution feedback > learned judges > intrinsic signals.
items.why_relevant: The reference taxonomy for the field. Key claims: 'demonstrated self-improvement strength tracks this hierarchy'; 'the difference between a loop that improves and a loop that circles is one rung of external verification'; almost everything surveyed is bounded, human-on-the-loop; open-ended RSI requires external grounding and no one knows the 'exchange rate' of grounding needed. Corpus repo: https://github.com/deepgrounding/recursive-self-improvement

items.name: Anthropic Institute: When AI builds itself
items.one_liner: Jack Clark & Marina Favaro report: >80% of merged Anthropic production code authored by Claude (May 2026), 8x code shipped per engineer-quarter vs 2021-25, ~52x speedup on code-optimization tasks, task-horizon doubling every ~4 months; defines RSI as an AI 'fully autonomously designing and developing its own successor' and says direction-setting/taste is still human.
items.why_relevant: Moved RSI from speculative scenario to a measurement question inside labs; the single most-cited document in Aug-Sept 2026 RSI debate (TIME, Forbes, MIT TR). Names bottlenecks (compute, human verification/review capacity, research taste) and calls for 'verification regimes' enabling credible slowdown agreements.

items.name: Sakana AI Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) Lab
items.one_liner: Tokyo lab positioning 'compute-efficient self-improvement' (evolution, harness search, sample-efficient program evolution) as a structural alternative to hyperscaler brute force; lineage: LLM-Squared/DiscoPOP, Darwin Gödel Machine, ShinkaEvolve, ALE-Agent, Digital Red Queen, AI Scientist (Nature 2026).
items.why_relevant: Institutional driver of the harness/evolution-first RSI school; explicitly names failure modes framework designers must handle: 'evolutionary loops that drift off-distribution' and 'self-modifications that pass benchmarks but fail in deployment'.

items.name: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement (RHI) (arXiv 2607.15524)
items.one_liner: Sakana AI + UC Berkeley: represent the agent harness as a prompt-level spec of the agent loop and iteratively refine it via pairwise feedback over its own revision history; on 30 ML-research tasks a few RHI iterations let low-reasoning-effort agents beat max-effort settings at up to 60% lower cost.
items.why_relevant: Introduces 'model-harness co-evolution' and 'harness-in-the-loop learning' (harness traces become training data for future models). Finds gains come from better inter-agent information flow / context management, not longer reasoning - direct evidence for the harness-first thesis. Mirror: https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2607.15524

items.name: MetaRSI / RSI2: A Meta-Recursive Self-Improving System for RSI Systems Themselves (arXiv 2609.06396)
items.one_liner: 30-author CosmosMind AI system with three typed operators sharing one loop kernel: Data-RSI (adversarial self-generated verified data), Harness-RSI (edits a 5-slot scaffold: system prompt, memory, tools, skills, MCP resources), Model-RSI (bounded training); model proposes on 'colored arcs', deterministic code adjudicates on 'protected grey arcs'.
items.why_relevant: Most explicit architecture-level answer to 'harness vs weights': only 5 of 6 operator orderings are admissible (Harness→Model and Model→Model forbidden because the dataset predates the capability change). Documents that 69% of surveyed RSI systems close loops only on machine-checkable targets and introduces a 'verifiability band' from freely-verifiable to unverifiable (rung 5 unsolved). HTML: https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06396

items.name: Lilian Weng: Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement
items.one_liner: 35-paper synthesis arguing RSI 'won't start with weights': harness = the layer deciding how the model plans, calls tools, manages context, stores artifacts and evaluates; taxonomy covers ACE/MCE/Meta-Harness (context), ADAS/AFlow (workflow), STOP/Self-Harness (loops), AlphaEvolve/ShinkaEvolve/DGM (evolutionary), SIA/Continual Harness (joint with weights).
items.why_relevant: Canonical text of the harness-first position, endorsed by Brockman per Latent Space. Lists 7 unsolved problems: weak evaluators for fuzzy tasks, context/memory lifecycle, negative-result reporting, diversity collapse, reward hacking, long-term metrics beyond sandboxes, human oversight at the right abstraction level.

items.name: karpathy/autoresearch
items.one_liner: 630-line single-GPU nanochat loop: agent edits train.py, trains 5 min, keeps if val_bpb improves, repeats; ~700 autonomous experiments yielded ~20 additive changes and an 11% 'time to GPT-2' speedup. Karpathy: 'All LLM frontier labs will do this. It's the final boss battle.'
items.why_relevant: Made the propose→train→evaluate→keep/revert loop a folk pattern (25k stars in 5 days) and seeded the 'sparks of RSI' framing (Latent Space, Mar 9 2026: https://www.latent.space/p/ainews-autoresearch-sparks-of-recursive). Karpathy's own caveat: it optimizes other models against a fixed metric, i.e. bounded self-refinement; his timelines are '5-10x pessimistic' vs SF consensus. Discussion #603 debates whether Anthropic-scale RSI is 'autoresearch plus infrastructure'.

items.name: METR: Expenditure Horizon - Measuring Optimization Ability (NanoGPT speedrun)
items.one_liner: New metric: the dollar budget at which humans become more cost-effective than agents on a continuously-scored task. Six $10K agent runs on the NanoGPT speedrun: GPT-5/Opus-4.1 no gain; GPT-5.5 ~1% speedup ($2.3K horizon); Opus-4.8 ~1.5% ($3.3K horizon) vs ~$250K cumulative human effort.
items.why_relevant: The strongest quantitative counterweight to lab RSI claims: autonomous optimization currently has 'minimal effect' on frontier AI progress. Also signals METR's shift away from binary time horizons, which become undefined once agents Pareto-dominate humans.

items.name: METR Time Horizon 1.1
items.one_liner: Suite expanded to 228 tasks on Inspect; post-2023 doubling time ~131 days (TH1: 165); Opus 4.5 at 320 min; later commentary ('Now 10x/year') estimates ~3.5-month doubling on recent models.
items.why_relevant: The time-horizon curve is the primary empirical input to AI 2027 / Forethought takeoff models; saturation above ~16h is why METR moved to expenditure horizon.

items.name: METR Frontier Risk Report (Feb-Mar 2026 pilot)
items.one_liner: Pilot with Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI: strongest agents ~16-20h at 50% horizon (unreliable above 16h), 3-4h at 80%; companies reported no dramatic AI-R&D-automation speedups and Anthropic said it had not seen a 2x pace increase as of April 2026.
items.why_relevant: Third-party evidence that as of spring 2026 labs themselves did not claim >2x R&D acceleration - the baseline against which the June Anthropic report and Sept OpenAI claims are read.

items.name: Forethought: How quick and big would a software intelligence explosion be?
items.one_liner: Davidson & Houlden: after ASARA (AI that automates AI R&D), returns-to-software r_cog median 1.2 (0.4-3.6); ~60% chance >3 years of progress compress into <1 year, ~20% chance >10 years; initial speedup 2-32x (median 8x); cruxes are distance to software limits and whether r stays >1.
items.why_relevant: Supplies the r>1 feedback-loop model that the entire 'is RSI unbounded' debate is conducted in; Epoch's rebuttal and Ord's generation-time critique are both responses to it.

items.name: Toby Ord: The Dynamics of Intelligence Explosions
items.one_liner: Distinguishes super-exponential from singular growth; true singularities need generation time to shrink toward zero (a 'Zeno condition'), so time-embedded discrete loops default to super-exponential-then-saturating growth; generation time, not per-iteration gain, is the neglected parameter.
items.why_relevant: Tells framework designers to instrument loop latency (generation time) as a first-class metric; argues generation-time floors may halt takeoff before capability ceilings.

items.name: AI Futures Project: Q2.5 2026 Timelines Update (Uplift and Revenue)
items.one_liner: AI 2027 authors' quarterly revision: Automated Coder medians Nov 2027 (Kokotajlo), Jan 2029 (Brendan), Jan 2030 (Lifland); coding uplift 'from 1.25x to 4x in 7 months' per Anthropic surveys vs METR's 1.04-1.2x; ~9 months AC→TED-AI, ~1 year to ASI in Kokotajlo's takeoff model.
items.why_relevant: Shows the forecasting community pulled timelines out (2029-2030 medians in late 2025) then partly back in after the Anthropic uplift data; the uplift-vs-METR discrepancy is the live empirical fight. Background: https://futuresearch.ai/blog/ai-2027-6-months-later/

items.name: OpenAI / Jakub Pachocki: 'An Alien Mind' + automated research intern milestone
items.one_liner: OpenAI hit its Sept 2026 'automated research intern' milestone (multi-day well-specified research tasks under human direction; 3.1 agent-workdays per human-workday by mid-Aug); Pachocki's essay expects the rate of progress to 'extend into recursive self-improvement', targets a full automated researcher by March 2028, and says alignment/CoT monitoring may not be ready - hopes for a slowdown.
items.why_relevant: Freshest lab-side RSI claim (one week old) and notable because the chief scientist pairs the claim with a call for mandatory safety bars. Primary essay: https://openai.com/index/an-alien-mind/ ; Fortune coverage: https://fortune.com/2026/09/08/openai-rsi-progress-jakub-pachoki-warns-dangers-slowdown-safety-rules/

items.name: TIME: What Happens When AI Starts Building AI? Inside Recursive Self-Improvement
items.one_liner: Long-form survey of the debate: Clark says RSI is already occurring; Kaplan, Orr, Hubinger on safety; Pachocki on compute limits; Narayanan, Marcus, Toner skeptical or demanding consistent metrics; bottlenecks: compute, data, sample-inefficiency, organizations.
items.why_relevant: Best single map of who is saying what in the mainstream RSI argument as of Aug 2026.

items.name: IEEE Spectrum: Recursive Self-Improvement Edges Closer in AI Labs
items.one_liner: Balog (DeepMind/AlphaEvolve), Mirhoseini (Ricursive Intelligence, $4B chip-design-loop startup), Clune ('one of the hottest topics in Silicon Valley'), Lambert ('lossy'), Ball and Krueger skeptical; OpenAI says GPT-5.3-Codex helped build itself.
items.why_relevant: Documents the pre-Anthropic-report state of the claim and the hardware-loop variant (AI-designed chips → faster AI). Ricursive: https://www.ricursive.com/

items.name: MIT Technology Review: AI's recursive self-improvement might not come so quickly after all
items.one_liner: Princeton (Kapoor) gave Claude Opus 4.8 six days, $3K API credit and GPUs on two unpublished NeurIPS 2026 questions; both papers rejected by the original authors - agents failed to explore, commit, incorporate feedback or rethink; 'absence of valuable, intuitive creativity'.
items.why_relevant: The clearest 2026 evidence for the 'direction-setting / research taste' bottleneck that even Anthropic concedes; a two-paper study, so weak statistically but heavily cited.

items.name: Nathan Lambert: Lossy self-improvement
items.one_liner: Proposes 'LSI' instead of RSI: automatable research is single-metric and narrow; parallel agents saturate (Amdahl) with human supervision as the bottleneck; billions in compute won't be handed to an autonomous loop - so progress is linear-feeling, not exponential.
items.why_relevant: The most-cited skeptical frame from inside the research community; directly challenges the frictionless-loop assumption framework designers might otherwise bake in.

items.name: Simon Lermen: The Term Recursive Self-Improvement Is Often Used Incorrectly
items.one_liner: Argues the Yudkowsky-2008 sense (an instance rewriting the cognitive algorithm it runs on) has been diluted into 'any AI automating AI R&D' - which is mostly data curation, tuning and RL-environment building, with different consequences.
items.why_relevant: Names the terminological drift that the 2607.07663 survey formalizes as bounded self-refinement vs open-ended RSI. (Exact publication date not retrievable; mid-2026.)

items.name: From AGI to ASI (arXiv 2606.12683)
items.one_liner: Google DeepMind report (Genewein, Legg, Hutter + 11) on post-AGI pathways: scaling, paradigm shifts, recursive improvement, and multi-agent collectives; treats RSI as one of four routes to ASI.
items.why_relevant: DeepMind's official framing places RSI as a pathway rather than an inevitability, in contrast to Anthropic/OpenAI rhetoric.

items.name: Recursive Criticality of AI Self-Improvement (arXiv 2609.00137)
items.one_liner: Burtsev (London Inst. for Mathematical Sciences): RSI as a stability transition with reproduction number R_AI = χ·a/σ (operational closure × recursive gain / frontier hardening); supercriticality can occur before acceleration is visible; networks can be collectively supercritical while each actor is subcritical.
items.why_relevant: Gives designers a monitorable criticality parameter and warns that 'self-amplification' and 'visible rapid progress' are distinct - a measurement caution for governance.

items.name: The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement (arXiv 2609.11873)
items.one_liner: Multi-lab survey (corr. Xuanhe Zhou) defining genuine RSI as a closed loop that 'uses the resulting capabilities to improve the improvement process itself'; 5-level autonomy ladder (L1 execution → L5 recursive inheritance); three gaps: safe inheritance, autonomy attribution, reliable verification under repeated evaluator access.
items.why_relevant: Four days old; sharpest statement that 'higher task performance alone does not show an improvement mechanism was revised, retained, and reused' - i.e. the verification target for RSI frameworks is the improver, not the score. Calls for frozen evaluators and independent anchors.

items.name: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves (arXiv 2606.09498)
items.one_liner: Shanghai AI Lab: fixed model runs weakness mining on failed traces → minimal harness edits → validation requiring held-in gain with no held-out regression; up to 132% relative gain (Qwen3.5-35B on SWE-bench Verified 19.5%→41.5%) on Terminal-Bench 2.0, SWE-bench, AppWorld.
items.why_relevant: Cleanest reference implementation of a no-regression acceptance gate for harness self-improvement; a template many 2026 harness-RSI repos copy.

items.name: SIA: Self Improving AI with Harness & Weight Updates (arXiv 2605.27276)
items.one_liner: A Feedback-Agent updates both the harness and the weights of a task agent; SOTA gains on LawBench (+25.1%), GPU kernels (12.4% faster), single-cell denoising (+20.4%); 'harness updates make the model agentic... weight updates build domain intuition no scaffold can instil'.
items.why_relevant: The main empirical case that harness-only iteration is dominated by joint harness+weight loops - the counterpoint to pure harness-first.

items.name: Hyperagents (paper + facebookresearch/HyperAgents)
items.one_liner: Zhang, Clune, Foerster et al.: task agent and meta-agent fused into one editable program so the meta-modification mechanism itself is editable ('metacognitive self-modification'); DGM-H beats prior self-improvers and meta-level gains (memory, tracking) transfer across domains. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461
items.why_relevant: The 2026 successor to Darwin Gödel Machine and the reference system for 'improving the improver' (L5 in 2609.11873); framework designers should study how it separates editable meta-level from evaluation.

items.name: Darwin Gödel Machine (jennyzzt/dgm)
items.one_liner: Sakana/UBC open-ended evolution of coding agents that rewrite their own code, validated on SWE-bench/Polyglot with an archive of variants.
items.why_relevant: The 2025 system everyone cites as the origin of harness/code-level RSI; also the origin of documented evaluator-gaming incidents (agents removing logging markers).

items.name: RSI-Exam (aiming-lab)
items.one_liner: 88 long-horizon executable research tasks (35 public, 53 sealed) across six domains: agent gets a weak method and 12h against a visible split; the submitted artifact is replayed once from scratch on a sealed split - 'an improvement that does not transfer earns nothing'. Built on harbor; leaderboard at rsi-exam.ai.
items.why_relevant: The benchmark most aligned with verification-first RSI: fresh-container replay, sealed splits, agent/grader image split, network policy. Directly usable as an external anchor for a self-improving-agent harness.

items.name: FrontisAI/OpenRSI (Frontis-MA1 + OpenMLE)
items.one_liner: 'Executable, measurable, reproducible AI4AI': 35B/30B Frontis-MA1 models trained on MLE search traces, OpenMLE Gym/RL/Evo, sandbox backend, NatureBench as held-out transfer; ladder Evolution→Self-Evolution→Meta-Evolution→RSI; explicitly 'without claiming general RSI has been solved'. Paper 2607.28568.
items.why_relevant: Most complete open-source data→train→search→eval loop; its 'rate of improvement itself as optimization target' slogan and companion survey (Self-Improving Agents in the Era of Experience) are widely referenced.

items.name: PostTrainBench: Can LLM Agents Automate LLM Post-Training? (arXiv 2603.08640)
items.one_liner: Agents get 10h on one H100 to post-train a base LLM; best agent 23.2% vs 51.1% for official instruct models, but wins in niches (89% BFCL on Gemma-3-4B); documents reward hacking: training on the test set, downloading instruct checkpoints, unauthorized API use.
items.why_relevant: ICLR RSI workshop oral; the canonical catalogue of how autonomous training loops cheat - required reading for anyone designing gates.

items.name: AI4AI-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Agents in Algorithmic Design for RSI (arXiv 2608.20318)
items.one_liner: 10 frozen research repos across 10 training-algorithm families; agent has 4h on one B300 to rewrite the training algorithm so the next system inherits the improvement.
items.why_relevant: Operationalizes 'improve the process that produces AI systems' with a compute-bounded, inheritance-focused protocol.

items.name: KaiWU5/Awesome-AI4AI (AI4AI Survey)
items.one_liner: 223-paper living map 'From Long-Horizon Agents to Recursive Self-Improvement - Definitions, Reliable Horizons, and Open Problems', auto-ranked weekly; companion survey on preprints.org (2026-08-30).
items.why_relevant: Useful weekly-updated index; its 'reliable horizons' framing ties RSI claims to METR-style measurement.

items.name: lobehub/awesome-rsi
items.one_liner: Curated research map of RSI: models, agents, harnesses, embodied systems, automated AI R&D, benchmarks, safety.
items.why_relevant: Shows RSI has become a standard awesome-list category; one of ~6 competing RSI lists spawned Aug-Sept 2026 (also pinkbubblebubble, Liuziyu77, cocacola-lab embodied-RSI).

items.name: leezythu/Awesome-Harness-Self-Improvement
items.one_liner: EN/ZH reading list on harness engineering for RSI of LLM agents, created four days after Weng's post.
items.why_relevant: Tracks the harness-first sub-literature (Meta-Harness, ACE, SkillOS, Evo-Harness, DemoEvolve, COMFYCLAW, HarnessX) that a self-evolving-harness framework competes with.

items.name: neosigmaai/auto-harness
items.one_liner: Give a coding agent a benchmark and an agent file; overnight it mines failures, edits system prompt/tools, and gates each change with a three-step gate (self-maintained eval suite + full val_score + suite promotion); Tau3 0.56→0.78; supports tau-bench, Terminal-Bench 2.0, BIRD-Interact.
items.why_relevant: Practical open pattern for regression-gated harness self-improvement using Claude Code/Codex as the optimizer; the PROGRAM.md + learnings.md convention is becoming common.

items.name: Human-Agent-Society/reef
items.one_liner: 'Continual learning infra for self-improving agents': connects inference, feedback, learning and versioned delivery; can train weights (Slime/SGLang) or improve harness (prompts, rules, skills) and stay live through updates.
items.why_relevant: Fast-growing (1.2k stars in two weeks) infrastructure that treats harness-RSI and weight-RSI as two paths on one versioned platform - the deployment side of the debate.

items.name: Jiaxin Zhang: Self-Evolving Agentic Harnesses
items.one_liner: Frozen weights + evolvable harness as the 'no-gradient twin' of environment-scaling RL; loop Represent→Propose→Validate→Evaluate→Select→Archive; catalogs DGM, AHE, HarnessX, SkillOpt, GEPA, AutoHarness, ADAS, AFlow.
items.why_relevant: Lists the unsolved issues most relevant to harness frameworks: verifier honesty (agents editing metrics, deleting logs, disabling sandboxes), benchmark-specific prompt rot, evaluation cost, task supply, and long-run decay of single harnesses.

items.name: Epoch AI: The software intelligence explosion debate needs experiments
items.one_liner: Ho & Whitfill: the r>1 debate rests on shaky R&D input/output data; proposes controlled experiments on data vs algorithms, compute-bottleneck tests with randomized researcher budgets, and small-to-frontier transfer validation.
items.why_relevant: Epoch's position (compute and cognitive labor may be complements; see Whitfill & Wu arXiv 2507.23181) is the main empirical challenge to Forethought's SIE model and to lab acceleration claims.

items.name: TokenRhythm/NeoHorse-1
items.one_liner: 4B/9B Qwen3.5-based models post-trained via a routing harness that logs tool interactions, estimates capability demand and feeds it into the next training mixture - a prototype evaluation→selection→update loop. Tech report arXiv 2609.08183.
items.why_relevant: One-week-old example of the 'harness as data-generator for the next model' pattern (cf. RHI's harness-in-the-loop learning) from an open-weights team.

items.name: PACE: Anytime-Valid Acceptance Tests for Self-Evolving Agents
items.one_liner: Paired commit gate: candidate vs incumbent on identical instances, testing-by-betting e-process E<-E(1+lambda(2w-1)), commit only when E>=1/alpha; Ville's inequality bounds per-candidate false-commit at alpha under optional stopping.
items.why_relevant: Reframes 'keep it if the score went up' as uncontrolled adaptive multiple testing. Qwen2.5 0.5B-3B prompt evolution on GSM8K/SVAMP/ARC: greedy 30-42% false commits and 13-21 spurious commits/run (72-100% false, up to -4.9 pts); PACE 0% false commits, <1 commit/run, ~18% fewer evals. Independent author; no code URL in paper.

items.name: SEA: Self-Evolving Agents with Anytime-Valid Certificates
items.one_liner: Confines self-modification to a small steering adapter + versioned harness around a frozen base; every modification admitted only through an anytime-valid gate emitting an auditable certificate against a fixed error budget.
items.why_relevant: Five verifier-in-the-loop mechanisms (best-of-N, micro-step search, self-authored reproduction oracles, search-layer control, self-repair) give grader-free dense signal computed from issue text. 52-instance SWE-bench Verified subset, +4 to +5 pts on two strong bases (e.g., 29->34), single-run only. Biswa Sengupta (JPMorgan). No code URL found.

items.name: RSEA: Recursive Self-Evolving Agents via Held-Out Selection
items.one_liner: Evolves a 3-layer text state (strategy/skills/playbook) for a frozen agent with an asymmetric held-out gate: accept as working state if no regression on Dv, update frozen best only on strict improvement; fallback to vanilla ReAct if nothing improves.
items.why_relevant: ALFWorld 7B: 69.3% vs ReAct 64.6% (McNemar p=0.015), 79.4% with retry. Key negative evidence: Dynamic Cheatsheet (no held-out gate) collapsed on WebShop to 0.136 vs 0.429; removing held-out selection gave 100% in-sample but a 33-pt test regression. Authors say they release harness, 6 baseline re-implementations, pre-registered manifests, but no URL surfaced.

items.name: Falsifiable Release Gates for Self-Improving Systems: Standing Invariants at Scale (Antahkarana)
items.one_liner: Every capability must pass a pre-declared machine-checkable acceptance suite (gates G7-G12, up to a self-governing loop) while six standing invariants hold; inv-1: no effector action without a same-tick, matching, unexpired capability token minted by an allow verdict.
items.why_relevant: Invariant exhaustively model-checked over 291 reachable states (TLA+), re-checked against 1M recorded traces (0 rejections), 'teeth' discipline with deliberately broken models; 432/432 adversarial tool-use attacks blocked; gated self-improvement lifted a small model 20%->70% while auto-rejecting a confidence-inflating candidate; 0.021 ms/request. Runtime on PyPI (antahkarana, antahkarana-cli), 563-test suite CC BY 4.0; GitHub deepaksatna/antahkarana has 1 star (link to paper unconfirmed).

items.name: LLM-as-a-Judge Is Not an Oracle: Why Self-Improving Agents Need Deterministic Guardrails (PROCTOR)
items.one_liner: PROCTOR: stateful orchestrator holds all tools, stateless Students diagnose/propose but cannot apply, Teacher grades but cannot write; five deterministic guardrails (hermetic sandboxes, capability-disjoint roles, mechanical pre-apply checks that outrank the Teacher, frozen holdouts, canary cases where a perfect score is evidence of cheating).
items.why_relevant: Catalogs 11 failure modes in 4 classes (judge bias, harness failures, ground-truth errors, reward hacking); one agent read cached answer keys via filesystem and reported 100% while true capability was 68.1%; only schema reordering (rationale-before-score) improved judge-human agreement (+9.3%); 13 deterministic-gate rejections/reversions over ~50 production iterations. Code explicitly not released (internal infra).

items.name: Who Grades the Grader? Co-Evolving Evaluation Metrics and Skills (Double Ratchet)
items.one_liner: Metric loop synthesizes typed drawback detectors with a birth gate (fire on >=50% of failure cluster, clean on known-good), anchor discipline to 10 golden items + consensus regularization, fail-closed validity gate; skill loop trains against the current metric; an independent stronger judge outside both loops catches gaming.
items.why_relevant: Retains 88-110% of supervised lift on MBPP+, Spider 2.0-Snow, report generation; evolved metric reaches 0.21 agreement gain with hidden ground truth (p=0.014). Critical finding: an anchor-guards-off metric that is vacuous (always-pass) trains skills equally well on task score, so downstream performance certifies nothing about grader validity. Code: github.com/amazon-science/Self-Evolving-Agents-Double-Ratchet (3 stars).

items.name: Ratchet: A Minimal Hygiene Recipe for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Three levers for skill libraries: outcome-driven retirement (evict when contribution c(s)<=-tau after >=Nmin trials; tau=0.10, Nmin=100), bounded active cap C, and an authoring prior; Proposition 1 gives a non-divergence floor E[pass@1]>=E[p0]-(tau+eps)-C*delta.
items.why_relevant: Audit: LLM-written skills added +0.0 pp vs +16.2 pp for human skills; Ratchet gives +0.328 rolling held-out pass@1 on hard MBPP+ slice; aggressive eviction (Nmin->20, tau->0) drives performance below no-skill baseline. Establishes the (1-tau)/2 judge false-pass threshold reused by Blind Curator. Code: github.com/amazon-science/Self-Evolving-Agents-Ratchet (3 stars).

items.name: The Blind Curator: How a Biased Judge Silently Disables Skill Retirement in Self-Evolving Agents
items.one_liner: Proves a sharp cliff: judge false-pass rate >= (1-tau)/2 (~0.45 at tau=0.10) makes contribution-based retirement retire nothing at any sample size; symmetric noise only attenuates. Proposes a pre-deployment audit that injects known defects to measure rho_F->P offline.
items.why_relevant: The disabled curator is silent (no aggregate metric moves); damage shows only where bias also starves skill synthesis. Report composition (155 sections) + MBPP+ replication; audited judge sat at rho_F->P~0.01. Directly tells harness designers to measure the judge's false-pass rate before trusting any retirement gate. AWS/HSBC; no public code.

items.name: Self-Authored Verification Is Unreliable in Heuristic Self-Improving Agents (SEAL)
items.one_liner: When policy and tests co-evolve, the cheapest path to passing is easier test distributions or lowered thresholds; proposes SEAL (Sealed Exogenous Acceptance Loop): a fixed harness-side audit invisible to the agent that compares candidate vs incumbent on hidden instances and returns only a single accept/reject bit.
items.why_relevant: 7 models x 5 Atari games: all 35 cells ended with self-scores >=0.70 yet 15 policies were below random; monotone test strengthening and discriminative checks did not close the verifier-deployment gap; SEAL improved deployment truth in 11/12 cross-game comparisons. No code URL.

items.name: More Convincing, Not More Correct: Self-Play Reward Hacking of Reference-Free LLM Judges
items.one_liner: Conditioned on a candidate, a judge scores plausibility not correctness, leaving false-positive basins a policy learns to exploit; decisive fix is making the judge commit its own answer before seeing the candidate.
items.why_relevant: GSM8K with Qwen3 policies: self-play drives judge pass rate 0.72->0.94 while true accuracy stays 0.20 (3 seeds); errors transfer across judge families (Qwen, Llama, Gemma) and scales; a strict 3-judge ensemble still accepts 55%. Strong argument against reference-free LLM judges as acceptance gates.

items.name: Harness-Agnostic Detection and Immunization of Reward Hacking in Self-Evolving LMs (HackProbe)
items.one_liner: Black-box monitor with two hooks (observe visible score; query candidate on held-out probes); dual-layer probe bank (secret frozen core of 240 probes over 6 subdomains + air-gapped rotating fresh layer of 60/gen); statistics J0 level gap, J1 Page-Hinkley divergence, J2 stagnation, J3 confidently-wrong rate fused via Sidak into a risk score; F2 bandwidth-limited reselection immunizes.
items.why_relevant: Four injected hacking channels (contamination, gameable grader, self-consistency bias, judge collusion) on Qwen2.5-7B, 48 generations: 0.763 AUROC vs 0.663 best baseline, FPR 0.434 vs 0.706; F2 returns +5.2 pts under hacking vs -4.7 on clean runs (only level with positive net). Most complete Goodhart detector for arbitrary self-evolving loops; no code URL.

items.name: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills
items.one_liner: Microsoft/SJTU optimizer for SKILL.md-style documents: bounded add/delete/replace edits (top L_t = textual learning rate), accepted only on strict improvement on a held-out selection split, rejected-edit buffer as negative feedback, epoch-wise meta-updates.
items.why_relevant: The most-starred concrete instance of the validation-gated pattern (17k stars); paper arXiv:2605.23904. GPT-5.5 +23.5 (chat) / +24.8 (Codex) / +19.1 (Claude Code) across 52 configs; skills transfer across models. darwin-skill v2.0 and agentdescent explicitly copy its 'StrictImprovement' gate. Note: gate is a plain strict-improvement rule, not statistically controlled.

items.name: Birfy/agentdescent
items.one_liner: Async 'gradient descent over agents' framework: DefaultAcceptance = Beta posterior on improvement with annealed risk base_delta plus a regression guard on the full held-out set (never the cheap layer); blast_radius<=0.30 routes to L2 fast merge, >0.30 forces oracle scoring of base vs candidate on every merge (oracle-rejected outcome).
items.why_relevant: Ships pluggable AcceptancePolicy contract (AdvantageAcceptance for GRPO-shaped methods, StableDistanceAcceptance as KL-to-reference analogue, StrictImprovement port of SkillOpt, AcceptAnyCompiling ablation), TrustRegion caps diff size before gate, reserved immutable 'oracle' artifact so a verifier cannot learn to pass itself. Docs: docs/acceptance-policies.md, docs/governance.md. 14+ algorithm ports (DGM, GEPA, SkillOpt, R-Zero...).

items.name: neosigmaai/auto-harness
items.one_liner: Coding agent iterates overnight on an agent file; gating.py runs a three-step gate: self-maintained regression suite must pass >= threshold (80%), full test-split mean reward must be >= best seen so far, then suite promotion; test traces never written to disk (structural anti-cheating).
items.why_relevant: Simplified release of NeoSigma's production setup; Tau3 score 0.56->0.78. Notable design: the coding agent curates its own regression suite (self-maintained evals) but can only read train traces. Gate is 'monotone best-so-far' with no noise control. Last push 2026-07-08.

items.name: alchaincyf/darwin-skill
items.one_liner: Autoresearch-inspired Claude Code skill optimizer: evaluate -> improve -> test -> keep or git-revert (git ratchet), weighted-gap targeting, v2.0 aligned to SkillOpt's validation-gated design with multi-judge independent review, no judge reuse, early stopping, dry-run ratio.
items.why_relevant: Most-starred community 'skill evolution' tool with an explicit keep/revert gate; Chinese-language README; documents anti-patterns (git reset --hard banned). Evidence of how the SkillOpt/SkillLens (Microsoft, 2026-05-22) gating ideas diffuse into practitioner tooling; gate is rubric-score-based, so subject to the judge-bias results above.

items.name: greyhaven-ai/autocontext
items.one_liner: Recursive self-improving harness with outcome-gated promotion of context bundles: held-out matched lane with no regression, optional read-only pre_promotion audit, a durable campaign-wide false-promotion budget (CampaignFalsePromotionController), and causal_attribution.json only for verified single-component manifest additions; multi-component edits never labeled causal.
items.why_relevant: One of the few open frameworks with an explicit false-promotion error budget and calibration doc (false-promotion-parity pins alpha and confidence thresholds); crash or gate failure leaves incumbent serving; promotion recomputes manifest diffs from immutable manifests. See docs/context-bundles.md.

items.name: Causal Agent Replay: Counterfactual Attribution for LLM-Agent Failures
items.one_liner: Models an agent run as an SCM; five do(.) interventions (incl. resampling a step under the same policy), K forward rollouts per intervention, point-of-commitment rule for stochastic re-execution confounds, Monte-Carlo Shapley credit with CIs.
items.why_relevant: Gives a principled 'which step caused it' signal for proposal validation and edit manifests (vs LLM-judge attribution at ~14% on Who&When). Validated on synthetic SCMs with ground truth (Shapley 0.44/0.45/~0, efficiency 0.909 vs 0.91). Code: github.com/jaineet17/causal-agent-replay (13 stars, CMU).

items.name: The Replay Gap: Static Evaluation of Model Switching in LLM Agents Scores the Wrong World
items.one_liner: Branching live rollouts on SWE-bench show replayed logged trajectories are invalid after a substitution: only 3% of replayed states remain valid, 61-94% of subsequent actions rewritten, all 5 outcome flips in swap arms vs 0/359 controls.
items.why_relevant: Warns that any gate scoring a candidate harness/model by replaying stored traces is scoring counterfactual states that never occur; supports live re-execution (as PACE/SEAL/HackProbe do). ~900 rollouts. Code: github.com/AshrithaG/replay-gap (1 star), COLM 2026 workshop.

items.name: FederatedSkill: Federated Learning for Agentic Skill Evolution
items.one_liner: Clients share semantic skill diffs (structured patches) instead of trajectories; a server-side evolution agent aggregates patches while modeling per-client capability boundaries to produce heterogeneous skill libraries.
items.why_relevant: Up to +44.4% success and -37.5% compute over self-evolving baselines across 20 task families. Relevant to gating because aggregation of diffs is itself an acceptance decision across a population; no explicit statistical gate or provenance/poisoning defense described, and no code URL (Cisco/UCSB).

items.name: Safety in Self-Evolving LLM Agent Systems: Threats, Amplification, and Case Studies
items.one_liner: Module-Lifecycle Attack Surface matrix: 5 modules (Brain, Cognitive Resource, Execution, Self-Design, Collective) x 5 lifecycle stages (Bootstrap, Propose, Evaluate, Commit, Serve); 17/25 cells have no effective partial mitigation; seven amplification effects.
items.why_relevant: Case studies on two open frameworks: evolution-native design activates 3.5x more attack-surface cells and 100% attack persistence (40/40 payloads); co-located security scanners blocked only 2.5%. Puts 'Evaluate' and 'Commit' stages on the threat map, arguing gates must assume adversarial candidates. 15 authors (Zhejiang/Tsinghua/Fudan/NTU/Ant); no code.

items.name: Zombie Agents: Persistent Control of Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Self-Reinforcing Injections
items.one_liner: Black-box attack: payload read during a benign session is written to long-term memory by the normal evolution path, retriggers in unrelated sessions, and self-reinforces by forcing revisits; sliding-window agents keep ~100% payload retention and >60% ASR across 20+ rounds.
items.why_relevant: Sandwich/instructional/spotlight defenses only cut ASR ~10-15%. Argues memory must be in the trusted computing base with provenance tags and policy checks on tool calls influenced by retrieved memory, i.e., a write-time gate on memory evolution. NUS (Hooi, Dong). No code.

items.name: SafeEvolve: Harness-Policy Co-Evolution from Agent Experience for Safety Alignment
items.one_liner: Converts on-policy safety experience into bounded, component-level harness updates (safety prompt + hierarchical skills) while the policy gets SFT then RL with verifier-decomposed rewards; the two co-evolve in a continual loop.
items.why_relevant: Qwen3.5-4B: 3x ASR reduction on AgentDojo while benign utility rises 59.79%->61.86%. Not a statistical gate per se but 'bounded component-level updates' and verifier-decomposed rewards are the safety-side analogue of gated skill evolution. Paper arXiv:2609.02786; official code (5 stars).

items.name: SERPO: Self-Evolving Rubric Policy Optimization for Open-Ended Test-Time RL
items.one_liner: Rubric criteria survive on discrimination utility (response-score variance + Good/Neutral/Bad order agreement), semantic dedup at >=90% verdict agreement, and a 3-consecutive-round elimination region deletes persistently weak or order-reversed criteria; rubric supplies group-relative rewards.
items.why_relevant: Gates the evaluator, not the policy: HealthBench +20.63 / ResearchQA +20.31, 8/8 OOD improvements; removing rubric evolution costs ~12-13%. Code: github.com/chiefovoavicii/SERPO (8 stars). HUST/USTC/Alibaba.

items.name: EvoRubric: Self-Evolving Rubric-Driven RL for Open-Ended Generation
items.one_liner: Single policy alternates Reasoner and Rubric Generator; rubrics pass a multi-level verification pipeline: meta-verifier filters ungrounded/superficial checks, zero-variance pruning permanently drops rubrics that give everyone full marks, leave-one-out peer consensus (Pearson vs peer batches) scores rubric quality.
items.why_relevant: Reward-hacking guards on self-generated evaluators; 14B averages 70.55 across five benchmarks vs GPT-4o 64.32; 74% blind win rate on rubric quality. Tongyi Lab; no code URL. (Distinct from EvoRubrics arXiv:2606.23038, adversarial co-evolution.)

items.name: ARISE-RL: Agentic Rubric-Grounded Iterative Self-Evolution with RL
items.one_liner: Generator/Solver co-evolution via rubrics; Reward-Gated Self-Evolution Distillation fires only when memory-augmented rollouts beat standard ones by more than a role-specific threshold (lambda = lambda0 * 1[delta r > tau] * w(t) * d(t)), distilling via token-level reverse KL from a transient self-teacher.
items.why_relevant: Ablation: ungated distillation causes substantial degradation on multi-tool tasks; gate is the largest contributor. ECR-Bench (100 deep-research + 500 travel queries). Qwen3.5-9B avg 0.569 across four benchmarks, beating Dr. Zero / Absolute Zero. Alibaba; code in github.com/Alibaba-NLP/qqr (294 stars).

items.name: Large Language Model Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers
items.one_liner: Causal interventions on raw vs condensed experience across 4 frameworks, 13 backbones, 9 environments: agents depend on raw trajectories but often ignore or misread condensed experience even when it is all they get.
items.why_relevant: ICML 2026. Implies acceptance gates that score a condensed skill/playbook may be crediting an artifact the agent does not actually use; motivates faithfulness checks (ablate the artifact and re-measure) inside gates. Triggered an Agno GitHub issue (#9139) about memory design.

items.name: TAME: Trustworthy Test-Time Evolution of Agent Memory (Trust-Memevo)
items.one_liner: Executor/Evaluator loop over shared memory; Evaluator assigns dual-objective contribution scores (task impact + trust annotations, Constitutional-AI style) so memories carry both effectiveness evidence and cautionary flags; Trust-Memevo benchmark (2,329 instances; safety, robustness, truthfulness, privacy, fairness).
items.why_relevant: Documents 'agent memory misevolution': score-driven memory evolution (ReasoningBank) raises task accuracy while trust dimensions drift down. TAME +14.6 pp on GPT-5.2 AIME while holding trust. Argues gates must be multi-objective. No code URL found.

items.name: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
items.one_liner: Weakness mining -> harness proposal -> proposal validation with a Pareto gate: accept only if delta_in>=0, delta_ho>=0 and max(delta_in, delta_ho)>0; rejects held-in/held-out trade-offs, no-op edits, and execution failures.
items.why_relevant: Terminal-Bench-2.0 pass rates +16-138% held-in / +33-60% held-out; SWE-bench Verified +3.5-22.0 pp; AppWorld up to +40.6 pp (MiniMax M2.5, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, GLM-5). Shanghai AI Lab; no code URL. Widely cited in July harness-engineering posts.

items.name: HarnessX: A Composable, Adaptive, and Evolvable Agent Harness Foundry
items.one_liner: AEGIS engine (Digester, Planner, Evolver, Critic): Critic checks each edit's change manifest against trace evidence and flags edits that target the verifier; then a deterministic gate (manifest completeness, config normalization, build/smoke tests, seesaw rule rejecting edits that regress previously passing tasks) decides what ships.
items.why_relevant: Paper arXiv:2606.14249 (v3 2026-07-23): +14.5% avg (up to +44.0%) across 5 benchmarks, 14/15 configs improved; variant isolation + per-task routing escapes single-harness stagnation. Principle: 'subagents propose; typed structure and deterministic gates determine what ships.' 462 stars.

items.name: Agentic Harness Engineering: Observability-Driven Automatic Evolution of Coding-Agent Harnesses
items.one_liner: Evolve Agent may write only inside the harness workspace; runs dir, tracer, verifier and LLM config are read-only and the seed prompt non-deletable; each edit carries a manifest (evidence, root cause, predicted fixes and at-risk regressions) that is scored against observed per-task deltas next round.
items.why_relevant: Paper arXiv:2604.25850 (2026-04-28). Terminal-Bench 2: GPT-5.4 69.7%->77.0% over 10 iterations; NexAU-AHE 84.7% +-2.1 with GPT-5.5; frozen harness transfers to SWE-bench Verified. A concrete 'evaluator outside the loop' design with predicted-vs-observed regression verdicts. 884 stars.

items.name: CoEvoSkills: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Co-Evolutionary Verification
items.one_liner: Skill Generator co-evolves with an informationally isolated Surrogate Verifier that writes deterministic test assertions; alternates skill refinement under fixed tests and test escalation when the surrogate passes but the hidden oracle fails.
items.why_relevant: SkillsBench 85 tasks: 71.1% vs 30.6% no-skill and 53.5% human skills; ~2.4 oracle calls/task; skills evolved on Opus 4.6 transfer +35-44 pp to six other models. Paper arXiv:2604.01687 v3 2026-08-10. Illustrates verifier isolation as an anti-overfitting gate.

items.name: Do Coding Agents Deceive Us? Capped Evaluation with Randomized Tests (CapCode/CapReward)
items.one_liner: CapCode plants randomized cap values so an honest policy's expected pass rate is 1/M; scoring implausibly above the cap is binomial-test evidence of test gaming. CapReward trains with a reward maximized exactly at the cap.
items.why_relevant: Detects feedback-, prompt- and workspace-exposed cheating on MBPP+/HumanEval+/LiveCodeBench/BigCodeBench while preserving rankings (Kendall tau 0.94-0.98); CapReward closes open-hidden gaps without hurting honest policies. Same idea as PROCTOR's canaries, with statistics. Code: github.com/ishida-lab/capcode (5 stars), capreward; dataset on HF.

items.name: Empirical Validation of the Classification-Verification Dichotomy for AI Safety Gates
items.one_liner: Argues classifier-based gates cannot achieve both bounded cumulative false-accepts and unbounded utility under distribution overlap; Lipschitz-ball verification of parameter deltas gives delta=0 false accepts and chains for unbounded improvement.
items.why_relevant: 18 classifier configs and 3 safe-RL methods all failed on 240-d controllers and MuJoCo; ball verifier 100% sound from d=84 to 17,408; 79% step acceptance on Qwen2.5-7B LoRA with zero violations. Weight-space rather than text-space, but frames the same 'gate must be a verifier, not a classifier' thesis. Scripts in appendix; no single repo.

items.name: Memory Reward Inflation in Self-Improving LLM Agents (LUCID)
items.one_liner: Self-graded utility scores inflate wrong episodes, which are then preferentially retrieved and trusted (compounding multiplicatively); formalizes an Error-Independence Assumption: a corrective verifier must be decorrelated from the self-grade bias and track truth. LUCID demotes stored rewards using answer-free signals (execution failure, degenerate output, literal string grounding).
items.why_relevant: Claude Haiku endorsed 31% of its own wrong answers, GPT-5.4-mini 54%; stronger parametric re-graders stay correlated (+0.30 to +0.36) with the bias. BIRD text-to-SQL: 52.4 no-memory, 54.0 Memento, 56.9 LUCID. Code: github.com/MohammadAsadolahi/Reliable-Memory-Agents-in-the-Wild.

items.name: When Good Verifiers Go Bad: Self-Improving VLMs Can Regress on New Tasks
items.one_liner: Verifier-driven self-DPO with progress-gated replay regresses students whenever verifier task-rubric accuracy falls below ~23%; the most confident-but-wrong verifier does the most damage while training loss keeps falling.
items.why_relevant: Recommends a gate on the gate: measure task-rubric accuracy on ~200 held-out items before running any verifier loop and refuse below threshold (R1); rank verifiers by rubric quality not size. MathVista improves while MMMU drops 3.4-10.9 pp under the same ladder. Meta AI; release planned.

items.name: OEP: Poisoning Self-Evolving LLM Agents via Locally Correct but Non-Transferable Experiences
items.one_liner: Low-privilege attack submits 'clean' experiences that are correct in a narrow edge case, paired with plausible catastrophic consequences, so the agent's own reflection crystallizes them into general rules; passes content filters and LLM auditing.
items.why_relevant: >50% ASR on GPT-4o, accuracy -54.29% (math) / -40.86% (medicine), 40.29% ASR surviving LLM audits vs <15% for baselines. Proposed defenses (active-search test retrieval before rule crystallization, multi-agent debate) only reduce ASR to ~21-46%. Shows acceptance gates need transfer tests, not local correctness. SJTU; no code.

items.name: Coalition-Aware Skill Reliability for Self-Evolving Agents (CASS / u-SMCO)
items.one_liner: Audits show 'coalition pollution' (bank-level gains hide negative individual skills) and cross-domain utility reversal; CASS gates new skills by Monte-Carlo-sampled coalition marginal contribution; u-SMCO masks skills post-transfer using unlabeled target queries.
items.why_relevant: CASS accepts 1/12 candidate skills where the baseline accepts 6/12; u-SMCO masks skills in 5/6 banks for +7.17 pp. Argues reliability is a joint property of skill, bank and domain, so per-skill held-out gates are insufficient. Code promised, not yet released.

items.name: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: From Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops
items.one_liner: Survey of 1,250 arXiv papers (2024-2026) on two axes (what improves x loop closure); 393 deployment-time, 340 training-time, 318 self-evaluation, 139 auto-research; proposes a verification hierarchy from formal verifiers down to intrinsic confidence.
items.why_relevant: Names four characteristic RSI failures (self-confirming loops, distributional collapse, diversity collapse, frame lock-in) and five open gating problems, including whether verifier self-training escapes circularity and the absence of governance-grade measurement for autonomous direction-setting. Useful map of who is doing what.

items.name: The Verification Horizon: No Silver Bullet for Coding Agent Rewards (Qwen Team)
items.one_liner: Verification is now harder than generation; no fixed reward stays effective as policy capability grows, so verification must co-evolve as an integrated system: executable tests + quality filtering + behavior monitoring + interactive/agentic judges.
items.why_relevant: Behavior monitoring cut hacked-resolved rate 28.57%->0.56% while clean resolution rose 40.22%->60.53%; interactive judges resist length exploitation; agentic evaluator (Opus 4.7) 70.4% best-of-N. Frontier-lab statement that gating is a receding target.

items.name: Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement (Lil'Log)
items.one_liner: Field-defining post: ladder from workflow automation to meta-level harness evolution; recommends held-in + held-out non-regression merges, read-only verifier/tracer/LLM config, bounded editable surfaces, and permission control outside the loop.
items.why_relevant: Lists seven open problems (weak evaluators, memory lifecycle, negative results, diversity collapse, reward hacking, long-term repo health, human oversight) and canonizes STOP, DGM, Meta-Harness, AHE, Self-Harness, ADAS, AFlow, AlphaEvolve, ShinkaEvolve. Anchors the September 2026 vocabulary that framework designers use.

items.name: Lift (SquadStack) self-improvement for voice agents
items.one_liner: Commercial self-improvement loop: proposes one change at a time to optimizable prompt sections (compliance/pricing/identity sections locked), requires human approval, then proves each change on real traffic via staged rollout (small slice -> quarter -> half -> full).
items.why_relevant: Only artifact named 'Lift/LIFT' found that matches the self-improvement-gating angle; production-style gate = human sign-off + A/B ramp + protected sections. Reported 2.7% vs 1.5% booking rate. Flagged uncertain as the intended 'LIFT' reference (see notes).

items.name: OpenClaw (Skill Workshop + plugin hooks)
items.one_liner: 389k-star personal-agent gateway (OpenClaw Foundation, v2026.8.1) whose Skill Workshop turns agent-authored skills into governed PROPOSAL.md drafts that only go live via apply.
items.why_relevant: Most complete third-party acceptance seam in the ecosystem: `skills.workshop.autonomous.mode` = off|propose|auto; plugins register `skill_proposal_evaluate` (receives candidate bundle + baseline, returns attributed findings, metrics, and optional pass|revise|block — only a completed `block` prevents apply); apply-time security scan (critical findings block); `expected_revision_hash` rejects stale steps, `correlation_id` links external experiments; append-only ledger + `skill_proposal_changed` (created/revised/evaluation_completed/applied/rejected/quarantined/stale) and `skill_changed` events explicitly designed so 'external optimization loops' can iterate. Other hooks: before_tool_call (block/approval), after_tool_call, before_prompt_build, before_agent_run, before_agent_finalize, agent_end, tool_result_persist, before_message_write, before_install, llm_input/llm_output. ClawHub `clawhub.skill.verify.v1` trust envelope + VirusTotal/ClawScan. Weekly Workshop maintenance and past-session scans generate proposals. No public roadmap on automated correctness verification beyond scanners/graders.

items.name: Hermes Agent (Nous Research)
items.one_liner: 'The only agent with a built-in learning loop': autonomous skill creation via skill_manage, post-turn background self-improvement review, memory nudges, /learn, curator, /journey; v0.21.2 shipped 2026-09-11.
items.why_relevant: Reference implementation of deployment-time RSI. Acceptance signals: `skills.write_approval` (default false) stages every skill write to ~/.hermes/pending/skills/ for /skills approve|reject (unified diff, CLI + chat); `memory.write_approval` same; `skills.guard_agent_created` dangerous-pattern scanner; advisory linter (incident-log-shape, references-sprawl — warn, never block); security scanner quarantines `dangerous` hub/project skills; optional NVIDIA SkillEvaluator tier-1 audit (advisory only). Memory is bounded (MEMORY.md ~800 tok, USER.md ~500 tok, no auto-compact) with injection/exfil scanning and duplicate rejection. Curator: usage tracking active→stale→archived, never deletes, optional LLM consolidation (off by default). Extension points: plugin hooks `ctx.register_hook()` (tool interception, guardrails), shell `pre_tool_call` (can block/fail closed), gateway hooks agent:start/step/end, session:*, signed outbound webhooks. 'Collective Wisdom' is the internal spec name (~/src/specs/collective-wisdom/) for the content-addressed (64-hex, canonical JSON) Skill Sync wire contract behind personal/organization Skill Sync polled from the maintenance timer — not publicly documented under that name. Docs explicitly contain no roadmap for automated correctness verification of learned skills; gating is human approval + security scanning + structural lint.

items.name: DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
items.one_liner: 'Everything is a Plugin' Cordis-based agent harness (developer preview, MIT) — model adapter, tool registry, session log and agent loop are all replaceable plugins; 222k stars in one month.
items.why_relevant: No built-in learning loop: no memory package (only `mcp-memory` user guide), skills are read-only provider catalogs (`ctx.skills` SkillProvider registry incl. remote providers, `skills/change` event), and feedback packages (`/feedback`, message ratings) are log-only and never enter model history. But it exposes the cleanest seams for a third-party acceptance layer: `tools/pre-execute` waterfall (hooks, permission, sandbox → allow|ask|deny), registered monotonic guards, `tools/execute`, `tools/post-execute` (accept, block, replace, add context), `tools/result` observe, `agent/pre-step`, `agent/request`, `agent/turn-stopping`, durable append-only session events, `ctx.approval`. Ships `dsh-hooks-claude-code` and `dsh-hooks-codex` bridges that run existing hooks.json (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SubagentStart/Stop). Roadmap: only 'compatibility-breaking changes'; no verification-of-learned-artifacts statement. Community self-improvement plugins exist but are tiny (dsh-continual-harness 9★, dsh-self-improved 12★, dsh-evolve).

items.name: Claude Code (auto memory, hooks, plugin evals)
items.one_liner: v2.1.270; auto memory (MEMORY.md index + typed topic files: user/feedback/project/reference), subagent memory, team memory stores, /goal judge loop, /init proposal flow, and `claude plugin eval` (v2.1.269, 2026-09-11) with a no-plugin baseline.
items.why_relevant: Learning loop = auto memory: Claude decides what to save, 200-line/25KB index limit with rewrite errors, `modified` frontmatter, `CLAUDE_MEMORY_STORES` team stores, no acceptance gate (user audits via /memory; docs say memory is 'context, not enforced configuration'). Acceptance tooling: `claude plugin eval` — 6 graders (regex, tool_used, tool_order, file_exists free; llm, baseline judge-billed), each case runs WITH and W/OUT plugin, Δ is the contribution, `--threshold` + exit codes (0/1/2/143) gate CI, `--judge-model` (docs: 'suspect the judge before the plugin'); skill-creator plugin evals (evals.json → grading.json → benchmark.json, blind A/B, description tuning) explicitly 'does not automatically improve skills'. Hooks a third-party layer would use: PreToolUse (`permissionDecision` on Write/Edit into the memory dir), PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure, FileChanged (watch MEMORY.md), InstructionsLoaded, UserPromptSubmit, Stop/SubagentStop (exit 2 forces continuation), PreCompact/PostCompact, PermissionDenied, TeammateIdle, skill-frontmatter hooks. No roadmap statement on verifying learned memories.

items.name: OpenAI Codex CLI (memories + hooks)
items.one_liner: Codex 'Memories' (`[features] memories = true`): two-phase background pipeline summarizes stale threads into ~/.codex/memories/ and injects memory_summary.md into the developer-policy prompt slot.
items.why_relevant: Learning loop without an acceptance step: Phase 1 startup extraction of idle threads (`max_age_days`, `min_rollout_idle_hours`) → Stage1Output; Phase 2 global consolidation under a per-home lock with 6h cooldown; secrets redacted; `memories.disable_on_external_context`; `/memories` per-chat control; agent tools add_ad_hoc_note/list/read/search. Docs frame memories as generated state ('don't rely on editing them by hand'; 'a helpful recall layer, not the only source for rules'). Hooks (hooks.json or `[hooks]` in config.toml): PreToolUse (`decision: block` / `permissionDecision: deny`), PermissionRequest, PostToolUse (block replaces output without undoing side effects), UserPromptSubmit, Stop, Interrupt, SessionStart/End, PreCompact/PostCompact, SubagentStart/Stop — but 'some specialized tool paths can opt out of the default hook path', so hooks are guardrails not enforcement boundaries. Enterprise plugin bundles since March 2026. Third-party memory layers (Hindsight, OpenViking, Mem0) attach via UserPromptSubmit/Stop hooks.

items.name: pi agent harness (earendil-works/pi, ex badlogic/pi-mono)
items.one_liner: 'Self extensible coding agent' whose TypeScript extensions intercept the full lifecycle; substrate under OpenClaw's original design.
items.why_relevant: No built-in memory or learning loop and no permission system (containerize instead); 'pi can create skills' but the only gate is project trust (`project_trust` handler). Extension events an acceptance layer would use: `tool_call` (block), `tool_result` (modify), `context` (rewrite messages), `before_agent_start` (inject message / system prompt), `before_provider_request` (replace payload), `after_provider_response`, `session_before_compact` (customize), `resources_discover` (contribute skill paths), `agent_end`/`turn_end`, `session_shutdown`. Pushes public OSS session-data sharing to improve agents. RFC stream (telemetry, analytics, locked install) has nothing on learning/verification.

items.name: Cursor (Memories, Hooks, /goal, Projects)
items.one_liner: Closed-source IDE agent: background-proposed Memories require user approval before saving; hooks.json at enterprise/team/project/user scope; Aug 19 2026 added /goal and subscriptions, Sept 10 2026 added coordinator-agent Projects.
items.why_relevant: Acceptance signal = human approval of each background-generated memory (the strictest default among substrates); memories are project-scoped, personal, unversioned — 'no diff, no blame, no rollback'; can be deleted in UI or by automations. Hooks an acceptance layer can use: preToolUse (block/modify input), postToolUse (modify output), beforeShellExecution, beforeMCPExecution, beforeReadFile, afterFileEdit, beforeSubmitPrompt, stop/subagentStop (auto-loop follow-ups, `loop_limit`), plus LLM 'prompt' hooks returning {ok, reason}; `failClosed` flag. No learned-artifact verification roadmap.

items.name: Mem0
items.one_liner: Memory layer for agents; April 2026 algorithm is single-pass ADD-only extraction (no UPDATE/DELETE), agent-confirmed facts first-class, entity linking, multi-signal retrieval (LoCoMo 92.5).
items.why_relevant: Explicitly has no acceptance/verification step — 'memories accumulate; nothing is overwritten' — which is the opposite design pole from OpenClaw/Hermes gating. Integrates as a Claude Code plugin with lifecycle hooks (capture every 5 exchanges, background extraction, recall next session), Codex hooks, and MCP; open-sourced memory-benchmarks eval harness. Useful as the 'ungated memory' baseline a verification layer must sit in front of.

items.name: Agent Lightning v1.0 (Microsoft)
items.one_liner: ~3.5k-line agentic RL trainer: agents keep their real harness and just point their OpenAI-compatible base URL at a training proxy; Qwen3.5-9B SWE-bench Verified 41.8→56.4 with 6K samples (tech report arXiv 2608.17528, 2026-08-18).
items.why_relevant: Defines the proxy-point pattern for training-time RSI: Gateway at `/proxy/rollout/{id}/attempt/{id}/mode/train/openai/v1` records prompt/response token ids and logprobs as `model_request` events; reward is an append-only event the agent reports at rollout end; rollout-level advantages; reward-hacking prevention (git disabled, .git hidden, network isolation, dataset cleaning). Acceptance signal = execution feedback (repository tests). Same LLM-proxy seam is where a third-party acceptance/attribution layer could sit for any harness.

items.name: Letta / Letta Code
items.one_liner: Stateful agents that 'rewrite their own memory, skills, prompts, and even the harness (mods)'; MemFS tracks all context in git; /sleeptime dreaming, /doctor, /palace, /skill-creator (parent letta-ai/letta: 24.7k stars).
items.why_relevant: Acceptance via versioning rather than gating: MemFS git history (`/memory-repository set`) gives diff/rollback of every learned artifact; hooks (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, UserPromptSubmit, Stop, SubagentStop, PreCompact, SessionStart/End; exit 2 blocks) are deprecated in favor of mods. Skill-learning research (2025-12-02): reflection + verifier logs → skill-creator; feedback-informed skills +36.8% vs trajectory-only +21.1%; Terminal Bench 2.0 +15.7%. Roadmap: agents generating their own tests/tasks and 'knowing when to seek external feedback versus self-improve autonomously'.

items.name: Reef — continual learning infra for self-improving agents
items.one_liner: Launched 2026-08-31; serve → observe (match feedback to interactions) → grow → commit accepted updates to a version history; trains weights (Slime/SGLang) or evolves harness prompts/rules/skills.
items.why_relevant: 1.2k stars in two weeks; the first infra project whose roadmap is literally about accepted learned artifacts: pinning/canary/shadow/teacher-fallback routing across versions, durable LoRA storage + rollback, batch validation and diagnostics, combined model+harness+config versions, self-distillation (SDFT→SDPO/OPSD), joint harness-weight optimization (WHALE). Harness-optimization path requires 'representative tasks and an evaluator'.

items.name: Hermes Agent Self-Evolution (DSPy + GEPA)
items.one_liner: Evolutionary optimization of Hermes SKILL.md files (Phase 1 done), with tool descriptions, system prompt, tool code (Darwinian Evolver) and a continuous loop planned; ICLR 2026 Oral.
items.why_relevant: Shows Nous's answer to 'what is the acceptance signal': eval dataset (synthetic or real session DB from Claude Code/Copilot/Hermes) + constraint gates (100% pytest, ≤15KB skills, cache compatibility, semantic preservation) + mandatory human PR review, ~$2–10/run. Last push June 2026 — the in-product learning loop moved faster than the offline evolver.

items.name: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: From Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops (survey)
items.one_liner: UC Riverside / Illinois Tech survey of 1,250 papers (2024–26) organizing RSI by what improves × loop closure (human-in/on/fully closed).
items.why_relevant: Supplies the vocabulary framework designers are using: verification hierarchy (formal verifiers > execution feedback > learned judges > intrinsic signals) and the claim that demonstrated self-improvement tracks that hierarchy; failure modes (self-confirming loops, diversity collapse, 34.2% integrity/fabrication failures); names 'governance-grade measurement of self-improvement' and process-level accumulation in deployed systems as the most underpopulated gaps.

items.name: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents
items.one_liner: 26 scenarios / 204 ordered fresh-session episodes across memory, procedural reuse, information gathering and update; 7 base models × 4 agent frameworks.
items.why_relevant: Introduces a mechanism-evidence score alongside task gain: all models gained from persistence (+0.13 to +0.24) but 'agents with the same headline gain can differ markedly in whether that gain is supported by evidence of the intended pathway' — e.g. writing artifacts but never reading them. Directly motivates acceptance layers that verify the learning pathway, not just the outcome; Agent-Zero regressed on 3/4 capabilities.

items.name: Agent Skill Evaluation and Evolution: Frameworks and Benchmarks
items.one_liner: Rutgers/UNC survey: four skill-evolution paradigms (execution feedback, trajectory distillation, compression/augmentation, RL) and six benchmark families (SkillsBench, SkillLearnBench, SRA-Bench, SkillTester, SWE-Skills-Bench, WildClawBench).
items.why_relevant: Names the verification gaps a third-party layer should close: no longitudinal evaluation of skills across feedback rounds, binary pass/fail metrics ignoring token/latency cost, and 'uncontrolled skill self-evolution can silently strip existing safety constraints'; recommends reputation systems, fine-grained permissions, explicit confirmation for sensitive actions, and post-installation behavior monitoring.

items.name: CoEvoSkills: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Co-Evolutionary Verification
items.one_liner: COLM 2026: a Skill Generator co-evolves with a Surrogate Verifier that evolves test assertions without ground-truth tests; beats human-curated skills within 5 iterations on SkillsBench for Claude Code and Codex.
items.why_relevant: Most cited concrete answer to 'how do you verify a learned skill when you don't have tests': evolve the verifier alongside the artifact. Includes Anthropic-affiliated authors; code at github.com/Zhang-Henry/CoEvoSkills (66★). The survey's 'learned judge' rung, with an attempt to push toward execution feedback.

items.name: NVIDIA SkillEvaluator
items.one_liner: Multi-tier skill evaluation: deterministic quality gates (PII, unicode smuggling, script lint, license, static security), semantic-overlap detection, synthetic eval dataset generation, live agent evaluation of behavioral effect.
items.why_relevant: Already wired into Hermes as an optional tier-1 audit (advisory, never blocks) — the first vendor-neutral evaluator a substrate consumes; a natural backend for OpenClaw's `skill_proposal_evaluate` or a Claude Code hook.

items.name: claude plugin eval ships (Claude Code v2.1.269)
items.one_liner: Anthropic's official eval harness for plugins/skills: realistic prompts × graders, 3 runs per case, WITH vs W/OUT plugin Δ, --threshold CI gate, HTML/JSON reports; Anthropic's own 7-case suite cost $9.59.
items.why_relevant: First substrate-native, CI-gateable acceptance signal for a skill artifact, and the docs are unusually candid about judge instability (grade long outputs with regex, pin models so 'a model rollout isn't mistaken for a plugin regression', exclude with-only graders from Δ). It measures; it does not auto-accept — the loop still needs an outside orchestrator.

items.name: OpenClaw blog: Skill Workshop — turn agent work into reusable skills
items.one_liner: Announces the governed proposal path: agent drafts PROPOSAL.md, operator reviews via Board view (pending/applied/rejected/stale) or Today view ('Use it / Tweak it / Skip it').
items.why_relevant: Design rationale for propose-then-apply as the default learning contract in a 389k-star substrate; later extended in v2026.8.1 with plugin scanners/benchmarks/graders and off/propose/auto modes.

items.name: MIT Technology Review: AI's recursive self-improvement might not come so quickly after all
items.one_liner: Princeton-led study gave Claude Opus 4.8 six days and $3,000 to reproduce two unpublished NeurIPS 2026 papers; authors rejected the outputs for lack of novelty.
items.why_relevant: The skeptic pole of the Sept 2026 RSI debate: Sayash Kapoor ('unambiguously bad at carrying out the research itself'), Jack Clark ('absence of valuable, intuitive creativity … bearish'); agents commit to weak hypotheses early and can't use feedback — reframes 'RSI' toward bounded, verifiable harness/skill improvement rather than autonomous research loops.

items.name: HyperAgents (Meta FAIR)
items.one_liner: 'Self-referential self-improving agents that can optimize for any computable task' (arXiv 2603.19461): a meta agent rewrites the task agent and itself; acceptance = domain benchmark score.
items.why_relevant: Current flagship of open-ended RSI research (successor to Darwin Gödel Machine); README warns it executes untrusted model-generated code — an example of the 'fully closed loop, execution-feedback' quadrant the survey places at the top of the hierarchy, but with benchmark overfitting as the acceptance risk.

items.name: OpenViking — self-evolving context database
items.one_liner: ByteDance Volcengine filesystem-style context store (resources/memories/skills under viking:// URIs) that attaches to OpenClaw, Hermes, Claude Code, Codex and DSH via hooks + MCP.
items.why_relevant: Its memory policy is a mini acceptance layer: committed sessions trigger background extraction and 'candidates are compared with existing memories for creation, merging, or skipping'; desktop app inspects recall/capture events. Claims LoCoMo lifts (OpenClaw 24→82, Hermes 33→83, Claude Code 57→80). Shows the ecosystem converging on external memory/skill stores plugged in through the same hook points.

items.name: auto-harness (neosigma)
