items.one_liner: Overnight loop: run benchmark → mine failures → edit agent.py → three-step gate (eval suite + full validation score + suite promotion) → record → update learnings.md; Tau3 0.56→0.78.
items.why_relevant: Small but the clearest open example of a self-maintained eval suite used as the acceptance gate for harness edits, including promotion of new evals into the suite — a pattern framework designers cite for 'who verifies the verifier'.

items.name: OpenClaw-RL: Train Any Agent Simply by Talking
items.one_liner: Turns follow-ups, corrections and explicit feedback in OpenClaw conversations into training signal: PRM majority-vote scalar rewards plus hindsight-guided on-policy distillation from textual corrections.
items.why_relevant: Defines 'next-state signals' as an acceptance source that requires no annotation pipeline; relevant to any layer that wants to derive accept/reject for learned artifacts from the user's subsequent behavior rather than explicit approval.

items.name: Prax — turn agent capability into work you can verify
items.one_liner: Runtime with explicit boundaries, 'independent acceptance', evidence-backed handoffs; workflows importable into Claude Code or Codex; one-shot verification mode with per-case accounting.
items.why_relevant: Small project but its Environment Runtime + Adaptive Autonomy Controller + Evidence Plane framing is exactly the shape of a third-party acceptance layer, and it explicitly separates 'a skill does not automatically gain the harness's contracts and guards'.

items.name: skillgrade — unit tests for agent skills
items.one_liner: Tests whether agents discover and correctly use skills; sibling tools agent-skills-eval (758★, agentskills.io-style runner) and effectorHQ/skill-eval.
items.why_relevant: The community layer of skill acceptance tooling that predates Anthropic's plugin evals; agentskills.io standard now has a skill-evaluation framework (validate/scaffold/grade/benchmark/report) that Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex and Claude Code all claim compatibility with.

items.name: SkillClaw: Let Skills Evolve Collectively with Agentic Evolver
items.one_liner: Aggregates trajectories across a deployed user group; an evolver mines recurring patterns into shared-repo skills synchronized to all users; evaluated on WildClawBench with Qwen3-Max.
items.why_relevant: Academic counterpart to Hermes Skill Sync / OpenViking cross-user propagation; notably has no formal acceptance mechanism, which is the supply-chain risk the skill-evolution survey flags.

items.name: claude-skills (alirezarezvani) self-improving-agent skill
items.one_liner: 25.9k-star multi-agent skill pack whose self-improving-agent skill layers a curation loop on Claude Code auto memory: promote learnings to enforced rules only after minimum-occurrence and confidence thresholds.
items.why_relevant: Highest-star third-party 'acceptance layer' pattern on Claude Code: capture via auto memory, hook fires only on errors, promotion bar before a learning becomes a rule or skill — a heuristic stand-in for verification.

items.name: dsh-continual-harness
items.one_liner: DeepSeek Harness plugin for continual learning: persistent memory, periodic review-and-refine, cross-session knowledge, and a plan → validate → apply → rollback loop.
items.why_relevant: Tiny, but evidence that DSH's plugin seams (session events, tool waterfalls) are already being used to bolt on a learning loop with rollback; sibling dsh-self-improved (12★) does L0→L3 memory pyramid + skill synthesis.

items.name: Cordis — the kernel under DeepSeek Harness
items.one_liner: 'Meta-framework of spatiotemporal composability' (arXiv 2608.25512): plugins contribute services, typed events and reversible effects that unwind on unload.
items.why_relevant: Reversible-effect semantics are what make DSH attractive for an acceptance layer: a rejected learned plugin/skill can be unmounted with all its registrations undone, and `cordis.patch.yml` layers let a verifier replace any config row by id.

items.name: WikiSkill for Hermes Agent
items.one_liner: Implements arXiv 2608.27454: self-evolving skills backed by a persistent knowledge wiki, packaged as a Hermes skill.
items.why_relevant: Example of the Hermes skill directory being the delivery vehicle for new learning-loop research; 189★ in two weeks.

items.name: Honcho (Plastic Labs)
items.one_liner: Dialectic user-modeling memory library; one of eight external memory providers Hermes can run alongside built-in memory.
items.why_relevant: Represents the 'model the user, not just the facts' branch of memory; no acceptance gate of its own, relies on the host's write_approval.

items.name: Mendel Gödel Machine (MGM)
items.one_liner: HGM successor adding reaction-norm mutation (multi-task trajectories of one agent) and cross-lineage hybridization (peer lineage's trajectory on a shared task) on top of clonal mutation; Thompson sampling over Beta posteriors picks operators.
items.why_relevant: Current headline of the Gödel lineage: Polyglot-60 50.8%->93.2% (HGM 77.9%), SWE-bench Verified-60 68.3%->78.3% (HGM 73.3%) with Qwen3.6-35B-A3B under a matched 200-eval/24-expansion budget; evolved scaffold transfers to DeepSeek-V4-Pro (96.89% Polyglot). Mutates agent scaffold code (prompts/tools/workflows); gate is benchmark-subset eval + CMP-style selection. Code: github.com/RealLcz/MGM (Apache-2.0, Slurm+Apptainer). No independent replication; numbers are on 60-task subsets and the '117x fewer params than GPT-5' framing is unverified externally.

items.name: Group-Evolving Agents (GEA)
items.one_liner: Treats a group of agents (not a tree branch) as the evolutionary unit; explicit experience sharing across the group replaces isolated DGM branches.
items.why_relevant: SWE-bench Verified 71.0% vs DGM 56.7%; Polyglot 88.3% vs 68.3%; matches OpenHands+GPT-5 (71.8%). Mutates agent framework code (workflow/tools dominate over prompts; transfers across GPT and Claude families). Gate: staged sanity check -> mini-benchmark -> full benchmark, parent selection by score x novelty. ~$13k per SWE-bench run, $1.5k Polyglot (eval-dominated). Code: github.com/UCSB-AI/GEA. No independent replication found.

items.name: Ouroboros: Self-Developing Frontier Coding Agent with Reviewed Core Evolution
items.one_liner: Open-source living agent that rewrites its own tools, prompts, context assembly and core code via reviewed commits; 'Hope' ran 161 days of free evolution under governed human communication.
items.why_relevant: Most-deployed RSI artifact in the wild: 1,085 self-modification commits (94.2% agent-authored), 1,522 reviewed self-edit attempts, 63.5% recent review block rate, $110.6K spend, 79.7B tokens. Gate: multi-model diff-review panel with quorum (sub-quorum cannot pass), deterministic preflight/diff fingerprinting, immutable constitution + spend cap outside agent tools, /panic halt. Self-reported Terminal-Bench 2.1 86.74% (Opus 5), OSWorld-Verified 90.69%, CL-Bench 0.2301; the TB2.1 leaderboard PR audit flagged one task (db-wal-recovery) as genuine reward hacking (agent curled the repo's own answer material). Code: github.com/razzant/ouroboros (MIT, 627 forks). No SWE-bench/Polyglot numbers.

items.name: MOSS: Self-Evolution through Source-Level Rewriting
items.one_liner: Argues text-mutable artifacts (skills, prompts, memory, workflows) are a strict subset; MOSS rewrites the harness source (routing, hook ordering, state invariants, dispatch) of a production OpenClaw deployment.
items.why_relevant: Cleanest statement of the 'harness code is the medium' thesis and the most operational gate in the set: candidates replayed against the failing batch in ephemeral trial workers, promoted via user-consent-gated in-place container swap with health-probe-gated rollback. Reported gain: 4-task mean grader score 0.25 -> 0.61 in one cycle (no SWE-bench/Polyglot, no baselines). Same HKGAI/HKBU/USTC cluster as TTHE/EvolveNet. Code: github.com/hkgai-official/Moss (Apache-2.0, last push 2026-05-23, effectively frozen). No replication.

items.name: Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution for Agents
items.one_liner: Shows harness evolution papers search on unit tests and report on the same public benchmark; under matched feedback/inference budgets, evolution does not consistently beat simple test-time scaling and generalizes poorly.
items.why_relevant: The sharpest published critique of the whole genre. Re-evaluates with GPT-5.4 and Claude Opus 4.6 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 against test-time scaling and discovery baselines on held-out tasks. Directly undermines the 'X% -> Y%' headline style used by MGM/GEA/TTHE. Authors include Hajishirzi, Tsvetkov, Dasigi (AI2/UW) plus Teng Xiao (also a Co-Harness author). Code: github.com/rethinking-harness-evolution/code.

items.name: TTHE: Test-Time Harness Evolution
items.one_liner: Keeps a population of executable harnesses around a frozen LLM and evolves them at test time with no gold labels; a judge commits harnesses from execution-derived proxy signals.
items.why_relevant: Label-free gate design is the interesting part: execution health, round-trip consistency (output inverted to description and scored against input), public-test pass rate. mini-swe-agent evolved on SWE-bench Verified 20.0% -> 35.0% (DeepSeek V4 Flash); BIRD hard 12% -> 50%; LiveCodeBench 30 -> 38.3; DS-1000 38 -> 44; claw-eval 48.9 -> 69.8; cross-model BIRD gains on MiMo V2.5 and Kimi K2.5. Code: github.com/junnie00/TTHE (MIT). No independent replication; the 'Rethinking' paper's critique applies directly.

items.name: HarnessFix: From Failed Trajectories to Reliable LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Trace-grounded, diagnosis-driven repair of seven harness layers (prompt templates, tool specs, orchestration code, config, validators, logging hooks) with scoped operators.
items.why_relevant: One of the few papers benchmarking against other self-evolution methods head-to-head (GEPA, SCOPE, ReCreate, Meta-Harness). GPT-5 mini: GAIA 43.3 -> 61.7, SWE-bench Verified 45.3 -> 57.3, AppWorld 36.7 -> 43.0, Terminal-Bench 2.0 17.6 -> 26.5; transfers to Sonnet 4.5, DeepSeek V3.2, Qwen3.5 Plus, Gemini 3 Pro. Gate: regression-aware validation on held-out sets (mitigate target flaw without unacceptable regressions). CAS Institute of Software. Code: github.com/HarnessFix/HarnessFix. No replication.

items.name: Self-Harness: Harnesses That Improve Themselves
items.one_liner: Weakness Mining -> Harness Proposal (minimal, failure-tied edits) -> Proposal Validation that accepts edits only after regression testing.
items.why_relevant: Cited by Lilian Weng as a canonical 'self-improving harness'; up to 132% relative gains across nine model-benchmark combos on Terminal-Bench 2.0, SWE-bench Verified, AppWorld with open models (MiniMax M2.5, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, GLM-5). Regression-test gate is the pattern most others converged on. Code: github.com/qzzqzzb/Self-Harness (no license file, last push 2026-07-02). No replication.

items.name: WHALE: A Simple Recipe for Joint Harness-Weight Optimization
items.one_liner: Alternates two phases: train the model under the current harness, then Meta-Harness search for a better executable harness under the updated model.
items.why_relevant: First clean ablation isolating harness-only vs weight-only vs joint: SearchQA 48.34 vs 38.29/38.27, Math 24.79 vs 0.42/15.42, Chess 29.83 vs 19.82/22.17 (Qwen3.5-2B/4B); restricting edits to prompts only (FST) loses 4-13 pts, i.e. executable-harness edits matter. Gate: empirical score on one trajectory per example, proposer can revert to prior designs. KRAFTON + Stanford (Chelsea Finn, Yoonho Lee). Code: github.com/krafton-ai/WHALE (Apache-2.0). No replication yet (two weeks old).

items.name: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Models: On-Policy Correction Helps Weaker Models Catch Up Where Imitation Fails
items.one_liner: Salesforce AI: GEPA-style harness evolution plus an MLE meta-agent that localizes the failing turn in the weak model's own rollout and has the expert rewrite only that turn before LoRA-SFT.
items.why_relevant: Most explicit demonstration that harness evolution dominates weight updates on enterprise tasks: base 29.2% -> evolved harness 78.0% -> +on-policy correction 79.7%, while naive expert imitation regresses to 63.1%. Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B student, Gemini-3.1-Pro expert; harness edits retained only when validation improves; $20/task budget, 3 seeds. No code released. Enterprise tasks are proprietary, so unreplicable externally.

items.name: Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit
items.one_liner: Disentangles the capability to produce useful harness updates from the capability to benefit from them; updating is flat across model tiers, benefit is non-monotonic.
items.why_relevant: Directly informs who should be the evolver vs the solver: Qwen3.5-9B's harness updates yield gains comparable to Claude Opus 4.6's, while weak models fail to activate or faithfully follow updated harnesses and strong models gain less than mid-tier. Implication: spend capability budget on the task-solving agent, not the evolver. 17 authors (UCSC/PSU et al.). Code under the A-EVO-Lab/a-evolve repo (release/harness-evolution branch).

items.name: The Red Queen Gödel Machine: Co-Evolving Agents and Their Evaluators
items.one_liner: Makes the evaluator part of the evolutionary loop: evaluators, adversarial objectives and dynamic utilities update at epoch boundaries alongside agents.
items.why_relevant: The Gödel-lineage answer to static-benchmark overfitting. Coding: same pass rates with 1.35-1.72x fewer tokens than prior SOTA; co-evolved proof graders +9% ground-truth accuracy; reduces AI-paper over-acceptance bias to human level. Cambridge (Nicholas Lane) group. Two independent open implementations exist (DreamFallenFlowers/OpenRQGM, 13 stars; kingkillery/red-queen-godel-machine, 3 stars) but neither reports reproduced numbers.

items.name: weill-labs/hgm: clean-room Huxley-Gödel Machine replication
items.one_liner: From-scratch, tested reimplementation of HGM (CMP + Thompson sampling) validated in $0 simulation then live on SWE-bench with mini-swe-agent + gpt-5.4 for ~$26.8 total.
items.why_relevant: The only statistically careful independent replication in the Gödel lineage. Findings: CMP beats greedy/DGM selection in simulation (+0.055 skill over 40 seeds); HGM rescues a deliberately crippled base from 0.00 to 0.35 pass@1 on held-out hard instances (McNemar p=0.016, 7-0); but from a competent 0.26 base with proper power (50 held-out instances) the discovered agents show no net gain (7-7 and 6-8 discordant pairs, p~1.0), and an earlier n=20 positive was noise. Explicitly does not reproduce headline benchmark numbers.

items.name: Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement (Lil'Log)
items.one_liner: Lilian Weng's survey of harness engineering as the substrate of self-improvement: workflow loops, filesystem-as-memory, subagents; optimization ladder prompts -> context -> workflow -> harness code -> optimizer code.
items.why_relevant: The reference framing most designers will cite. Lists seven unsolved bottlenecks: weak evaluators, memory lifecycle, negative-result imbalance, diversity collapse, reward hacking ('a loop optimizes whatever signal it is given'), long-term maintainability, and the human role ('move up the stack, not out of the loop'). Prescribes permission controls and safety layers outside the optimization loop, held-out tests and trace audits. Cites STOP, Self-Harness, AHE, Meta-Harness, DGM, DemoEvolve, SIA.

items.name: MetaSkill-Evolve: Two-Timescale Meta-Skill Evolution
items.one_liner: Makes skill evolution recursive: each branch carries a task skill (fast loop) and a meta-skill (five Markdown files parameterizing Analyzer/Retriever/Allocator/Proposer/Evolver) refined by the same pipeline on a slow loop.
items.why_relevant: Cleanest bounded-recursion design (one level, H=2 fast iters per meta update; H=8 costs 9.1 pts). Gemma-4 31B frozen; OfficeQA 55.32 vs 48.94 single-level, SealQA 45.26 vs 37.21, ALFWorld 94.23 vs 92.31. Gate: only positive-gain children (dU>0) enter the SQLite-backed provenance DAG; frontier scored by utility + meta-productivity + novelty. Same LMU group (Tresp/Ma) as MGM. No official code; most of the gain is from the non-recursive fast loop.

items.name: Bilevel Autoresearch: Meta-Autoresearching Itself
items.one_liner: Outer loop reads inner-loop traces and injects new search mechanisms as Python code at runtime; inner loop is Karpathy's propose-execute-evaluate-keep autoresearch loop.
items.why_relevant: The 'optimizer of the optimizer' pattern with a hard numeric verifier (val_bpb on Karpathy's GPT pretraining benchmark): -0.045 vs -0.009 for the inner loop alone (5x). Outer loop autonomously discovered bandit, DoE and combinatorial-search mechanisms. Gate is the inner loop's keep/discard on validation loss. Code: github.com/EdwardOptimization/Bilevel-Autoresearch (MIT, 28 forks). Popular in the Karpathy-loop community but no replication reported.

items.name: HASE: Harness-Aware Self-Evolving
items.one_liner: Agentic RL where one model both solves tasks and edits selected harness components in a multi-turn action space, so weights, harness and solutions co-evolve.
items.why_relevant: Shows a single Qwen3-8B with HASE matching a GPT-OSS-120B model that uses Claude Code as its harness proposer on text classification, beating it on alpha-factor mining, and converging to SOTA on circle packing. Removes the separate 'evolver' model, which interacts with the Updating-vs-Benefit finding. Gate/reward details not in abstract; no code found.

items.name: Harness-R1: Learning to Edit Executable Runtime Harnesses from Agent Failure Trajectories
items.one_liner: Trains a dedicated 9B 'harness engineer' with online GRPO to make failure-conditioned, lifecycle-wide edits to a frozen target agent's runtime.
items.why_relevant: Reward is a fresh same-batch rerun of the frozen target (outcome-grounded gate baked into training). WebShop/ALFWorld/DBBench: 44.3% -> 53.6% (+9.3), and 59.2 -> 64.2 when combined with target fine-tuning. Qwen3.5-9B engineer. Code: github.com/DeepExperience/Harness-R1 (Apache-2.0, 21 forks). No replication.

items.name: EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement
items.one_liner: Federated harness evolution: deployments evolve a shared program harness on local data and aggregate code modifications rather than raw workloads.
items.why_relevant: Same group as TTHE/MOSS; the gate is a crisp behavioral rule worth copying: commit merged harness only if newly solved items >= newly broken items on a validation slice. DeepSeek-V4-Flash: SWE-bench Verified 37.5 -> 57.5, LiveCodeBench 33.3 -> 66.7, BIRD 57.3 -> 70.7, DS-1000 55.5 -> 68.5, ClawEval 65.8 -> 74.1. Code: github.com/junnie00/EvolveNet. No replication.

items.name: NeoHorse-1: Recursive Self-Improvement via Agentic Post-Training with Routing Harness
items.one_liner: 4B/9B agent-native models post-trained on live tool traces recorded by a routing harness (predicted capability demand, service tier, interaction), closing an evaluation-selection-update loop.
items.why_relevant: Weight-side RSI with the harness as data generator: macro-average over 11 benchmarks 58.94 -> 64.87 (4B) and 65.60 -> 69.04 (9B). Filters: structural validation, six-dimensional semantic evaluation, subscene labeling. Only one loop iteration reported. Code: github.com/TokenRhythm/NeoHorse (Apache-2.0, 36 co-authors, weights on HF). Fast star growth (232 in 10 days).

items.name: HarnessEvolve: Learning from Reference Trajectories for Reliable Agent Self-Evolution
items.one_liner: Decouples execution agent from evolution pipeline (execution, evaluation, optimization, gating as independent modules) and uses reference trajectories to fix credit assignment, shortcut learning and forgetting.
items.why_relevant: Best-articulated two-stage gate in the set: a quality gate that filters data leakage and prompt bloat, then a performance gate that accepts an update only if it improves the current batch without degrading recent batches, with epoch-end held-out validation selecting the best accepted snapshot. Edits span skill.md, skill Python, prompts, tool-arg specs, execution logic. Compared to GEPA/ACE/SkillOpt; exact numbers not in abstract; no code found.

items.name: SEAGym: An Evaluation Environment for Self-Evolving LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Turns Harbor-compatible benchmarks into self-evolution task streams with train batches, frozen update-validation, held-out ID/OOD views, replay diagnostics and snapshot/cost records.
items.why_relevant: Verification infrastructure rather than a method. Instantiated on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and HLE comparing ACE, TF-GRPO and AHE under a shared epoch/batch protocol; found that frequent updates may fail to improve held-out performance, useful intermediate snapshots can collapse later, and backend/source diversity affect harness reliability. Useful template for any RSI gate design.

items.name: What Do Evolutionary Coding Agents Evolve?
items.one_liner: EvoTrace dataset (4 frameworks, 16 math/algorithm tasks) plus EvoReplay interventions and a nine-type edit taxonomy validated against blind human annotation.
items.why_relevant: Empirical reality check on 'evolution': most score gains come from a small subset of edit types, and ~30% of code lines added during search are byte-identical re-introductions of previously deleted lines in nearly every run. Gains can be constant re-tuning or evaluator overfitting rather than new structure. ZIB/TU Berlin/HKBU/RIKEN. Suggests dedupe and edit-type logging as gate features.

items.name: Escher-Loop: Mutual Evolution by Closed-Loop Self-Referential Optimization
items.one_liner: Evolves both task agents (executable code) and optimizer agents (LLM prompts that refine task agents and themselves); task scores are reused to score optimizers almost for free.
items.why_relevant: Self-referential optimization with a grounded signal only at the task level. Under matched 10M equivalent-token budgets beats OpenEvolve on Kissing Number (582/593), Circle Packing (2.6352 vs 2.6350 reference), Heilbronn Triangle. Rank-softmax selection; Gemini 3 Flash. Math-only, no agentic benchmarks. Code: github.com/scaling-group/escher-loop (MIT, last push 2026-05-12).

items.name: PenguinHarness
items.one_liner: LlamaFactory team's 'Harness for RSI': local-first platform where agents build, evaluate and optimize other agents, with snapshot-before-every-round and Trace observability.
items.why_relevant: Highest-velocity product-side RSI claim (2.1k stars, 229 forks in 8 weeks; Product Hunt launch). Publisher-reported: 66.67% on a 15-task data-analysis suite at $0.55 (1/70 the cost of Claude Code+Opus), 71.25% coding tying Codex at $3.81, $0.02 RAG app on DeepSeek V4 Pro. The independent reference site penguinharness.net explicitly notes no independent trace, token ledger or rerun exists and the benchmark suite is still roadmap. Self-evolution gate = run benchmark, find lost points, ship N+1 with snapshot rollback.

items.name: Raven: The Harness of Harnesses (EverMind)
items.one_liner: Pre-alpha multi-agent ecosystem on EverMind's self-evolving harness engine; Evolver diagnoses failures, tests candidates and retains changes that beat baseline in reproducible evals.
items.why_relevant: Largest-star open self-evolving harness product; claims #1 on EvoAgentBench (+6.2pp over next method), 0.60 F1 ProAgentBench, efficiency 56.7% at 27B vs Hermes 46.8%. Ships Raven-Research/Code/Design/Oncall and wraps Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Hermes, OpenClaw. Internal 22-task prototype claims are not public; 'Harness of Harnesses' itself not yet implemented in the public release. Apache-2.0, 77 forks, pushed 2026-09-14.

items.name: Kiro Crew (AWS)
items.one_liner: AWS's open-source (Apache-2.0) persistent agent workspace 'that self-improves and continues beyond one session'; formerly MeshClaw with 39k internal developers.
items.why_relevant: Sets the enterprise meaning of 'self-improving': corrections and failures become durable lessons, repeated patterns become editable skills, memory persists across sessions; no code self-modification. Orchestration is open but the kiro-cli agent runtime it drives is proprietary and credit-metered (Forbes, 2026-08-06), so the actual harness is closed. Useful as the conservative baseline against which RSI claims are marketed.

items.name: HELIX: Model-Harness Co-evolution for Recursive Self-Improvement
items.one_liner: Decomposes agents (OpenCode, Pi Mono, Nanobot, Hermes) into typed ports, atoms, recipes, product shells and runtime policies; harness rollouts become trainable data with provenance.
items.why_relevant: Ambitious 'co-evolution as first-class principle' framing but thin results: LiveCodeBench 52/100 vs 50 for best fixed harness, portfolio oracle 79/100, SWE-bench Verified 46/55 on a 55-instance subset with MiniMax-M2.7; 438 verified training records materialized but no retraining or second cycle actually run. Gate: trace-strict status (observed bash call running test_solution.py with passing output) plus official SWE-bench evaluator. Code: github.com/HKUDS/HELIX (MIT).

items.name: MemoHarness: Agent Harnesses That Learn from Experience
items.one_liner: Six editable control dimensions (context, tools, orchestration, memory, decoding, output handling) plus a dual-layer experience bank of per-case diagnoses and distilled global patterns.
items.why_relevant: Adapts the harness per test case from retrieved experience with no test-time labels, feedback or extra search, on shell-agent, code-generation and analytical-reasoning suites with selective transfer to unseen suites/models. No exact numbers in abstract. Code: github.com/HowieHwong/MemoHarness (no license file). Xiangliang Zhang group (Notre Dame).

items.name: Co-Harness: Co-Evolving Harnesses and Model Weights for LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Alternates harness optimization (an LLM HarnessCritic diagnoses failed trajectories and proposes validated local updates to prompts/tools/skills/middleware/memory) with SFT on trajectories from the improved harness.
items.why_relevant: Coined the 'co-evolving harnesses and models' phrase later reused by Salesforce; includes a 200+ hour autonomous case study. Abstract gives no benchmark numbers and no code was found. Shares authors (Teng Xiao, Zhengyu Chen, Yige Yuan) with the 'Rethinking the Evaluation of Harness Evolution' critique, an unusual self-audit pairing.

items.name: JIT-Agent: Scaling Harness Intelligence via Just-in-Time Harness Evolution
items.one_liner: Synthesizes a task-specific harness on the spot via a four-module protocol (memory, planning, action, capability orchestration) instead of a fixed scaffold.
items.why_relevant: Fast-growing repo (466 stars in 4 weeks) from Wangchunshu Zhou / Shuicheng Yan's group; large deltas on planning (DeepPlanning-Shopping +24.8, -Travel +20.2 with DeepSeek-V4-Flash/GLM-5.2), DeepSearchQA +9.1, xBench +12.0; Qwen3.6-27B trained as the harness synthesizer. Per-task generation rather than persistent evolution, so no cross-task gate; relevant as the 'harness as inference-time output' counterpoint. Code: github.com/bingreeky/JIT.

items.name: SHE: Trajectory-driven Safety Harness Evolution
items.one_liner: Evolves four safety-owning artifacts (System Prompt, Rule Bank, Safety Memory, Tool Policy) from rollout trajectories.
items.why_relevant: Only entry in the set where the evolved surface is the safety layer itself: 3.1x attack-success-rate reduction vs static SafeHarness on Agent-SafetyBench with held-out AgentHarm, benign utility retained. Raises the design question the others sidestep: should safety artifacts be inside or outside the mutable surface. Shanghai AI Lab authors (Jing Shao, Dongrui Liu). Code: github.com/RainbowQTT/SHE (Apache-2.0).

items.name: Ecdysis: Efficient and Effective Training of Runtime Harnesses for LLM Agents
items.one_liner: Batch-level analysis separates recurring cross-task harness deficiencies from model-specific accommodation before spending evolution budget.
items.why_relevant: Newest (4 days old) and addresses the cost problem head-on: up to 1.84x speedup over existing harness evolution methods with +18.56% reasoning accuracy, stronger cross-LLM generalization and lower inference tokens. Its 'is this failure harness-actionable' classifier is a candidate pre-gate for any RSI loop. 14 authors, no code found, baselines and models not in abstract.

items.name: DemoEvolve: Overcoming Sparse Feedback in Agentic Harness Evolution with Demonstrations
items.one_liner: Uses competent human trajectories as reference experience for the coding proposer when reward-only harness search is too noisy.
items.why_relevant: Negative-result-driven: self-rollout evolution works on Liar's Dice (short episodes, attributable failures) but is misled by sparse feedback and candidate-selection noise on Balatro. Demonstrates the failure mode of evolving under weak verifiers, which Weng's post cites. No code found.

items.name: Recursive Harness Self-Improvement (RHI)
items.one_liner: Harness-in-the-loop learning: harnesses treated as data-generating components, iteratively refined with pairwise feedback on their revision history.
items.why_relevant: Sakana/Databricks-adjacent authors (Yujin Tang, Matei Zaharia). On 30 synthetic ML-research tasks a few RHI iterations let low-reasoning-effort agents exceed max-effort settings at up to 60% lower cost, attributed to task-specific context management rather than longer reasoning. Positions harness evolution as a continual-learning algorithm. No code.

items.name: loversky02/metaskill-evolve: $0 reproduction and dissection
items.one_liner: Apple-Silicon reproduction of MetaSkill-Evolve's engine (33 offline tests) with an added backbone-strength sweep.
items.why_relevant: Only independent artifact for MetaSkill-Evolve. Verifies the mechanism, not the numbers (31B backbone does not fit locally). Its toy sweep shows the meta-loop's marginal gain shrinking to zero as backbone strength rises (+0.50 weak, +0.25 mid, +0.00 strong), consistent with 'Harness Updating Is Not Harness Benefit'; also points out that the paper's own Table 1 attributes most of the gain to the non-recursive fast loop.

items.name: Harness-1: RL for Search Agents with State-Externalizing Harnesses
items.one_liner: 20B retrieval subagent trained with RL inside a stateful harness that externalizes bookkeeping so the policy only learns semantic search decisions.
items.why_relevant: Not self-improving, but the design argument (put recoverable state in the harness, not the policy) is the premise the co-evolution papers build on. 0.730 average curated recall across eight retrieval benchmarks, +11.4 over the next open search subagent. No code found.

items.name: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable, Navigable, and Editable
items.one_liner: Static-analysis-synthesized behavior-to-source map used as shared behavioral memory so an agent can localize, plan, execute and resync edits as the harness repo evolves.
items.why_relevant: Tooling for the editability bottleneck rather than a loop: improves behavior localization and edit-plan quality with fewer planner tokens on two open-source harnesses (no exact numbers in abstract). Relevant to making self-edits auditable. Project page ruhan-wang.github.io/Harness-Handbook; repo Ruhan-Wang/Harness-Handbook (5 stars).

items.name: KnowAct-GUIClaw: Personal GUI Assistant with Self-Evolving Memory and Skill
items.one_liner: Know-Route-Act-Reflect framework whose memory and execution skills evolve from user interaction across Android/iOS/HarmonyOS/Windows.
items.why_relevant: Repo bills itself 'Recursive Self-Improvement Personal Assistant' (484 stars, HITsz-TMG, MIT) but the evolved surface is memory + skills, not harness code. 64.1% on MobileWorld with Kimi-2.6, beating Seed-2.0-Pro and GPT-5.5; evolved artifacts transfer across base models (+8.5%). Marker for how loosely 'RSI' is used in product-facing repos.

items.name: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP)
items.one_liner: Seed improver program that improves programs is applied to itself; LM proposes beam search, GA, simulated annealing variants.
items.why_relevant: Lineage anchor for 'optimizer optimizes optimizer' (Escher-Loop, Bilevel Autoresearch, MetaSkill-Evolve all cite it). Still the canonical reward-hacking anecdote: improvers disabled the sandbox flag and removed logging markers. Authors state it is not full RSI since weights are frozen, the same caveat every 2026 harness-RSI paper inherits. Code: github.com/microsoft/stop (MIT, dormant since 2024).
